5161171194.body:
REPLAN: `planned_features` resolved to filed numbers; `requires_features` is now the closed set [315, 316, 318, 319, 322, 329, 336, 337, 341, 349, 365] and `planned_features` is EMPTY. The mermaid graph is regenerated from the filed machine blocks, which deleted two of its ten ordering arrows and added three it was missing.

## 1. Resolution — eleven scopes, eleven filed issues, zero unresolved

Every number was checked against the target issue's own title and Abstract, never against its position in the roster. FEAT-043 is **#329** while FEAT-044 is **#328** — a transposed adjacent pair — so this roster is one of the places that error would have landed, and it was checked specifically.

| planned_features scope | Filed as | Title check |
|---|---|---|
| FEAT-040 the package and pinout library as data | **#349** | "FEAT-040: JLS knows what a real part is — pinouts, sections, footprints and loading are queryable data, extensible with a text file and no Java" |
| FEAT-041 packing, refdes, width cascade and electrical loading checks | **#365** | "FEAT-041: a drawn design becomes a buildable parts list — every element assigned a package and section deterministically, word-level parts cascaded into real slices…" |
| FEAT-027 strength lattice, driver kinds and net kinds | **#341** | "FEAT-027: a net has a kind and a driver has a strength, so open-drain buses, pull-ups and floating inputs behave the way the bench behaves" |
| FEAT-026 the four-state value core with a resolution fold | **#322** | "FEAT-026: a signal can say 'unknown' and 'undriven' per bit, and contention resolves as a property of the driver set rather than of draw order" |
| FEAT-043 the breadboard canvas and its physical-simulation binding | **#329** | "FEAT-043: a second canvas places parts on a solderless breadboard, and the placed arrangement — not the schematic — drives the simulation" — **not #328, which is FEAT-044, the Tiny Tapeout wrapper** |
| FEAT-004 shared net-partition IR with stable net naming | **#336** | "FEAT-004: exactly one net partition in JLS, and a synthesized net name that survives an unrelated edit" |
| FEAT-014 stable addressing and per-view geometry | **#318** | "FEAT-014 (RESIDUAL): nets, groups and nested instances get names that survive sharing, and geometry becomes one record per view" |
| FEAT-013 per-section internal versioning | **#319** | "FEAT-013: a saved file stops being accepted or refused as one unit — unknown optional sections are skipped and preserved…" |
| FEAT-001 (RESIDUAL) registry-keyed table totality | **#315** | "FEAT-001 (RESIDUAL): a thirty-sixth element type cannot ship until every registry-keyed table has a row for it" |
| FEAT-008 (RESIDUAL) SimpleEditor decomposition and a floored jls.edit | **#316** | "FEAT-008 (RESIDUAL): the editor's nine-state mouse machine is assertable without a display, and jls.edit carries a coverage floor" |
| FEAT-015 (RESIDUAL) headless CircuitOp application and construction verbs | **#337** | "FEAT-015 (RESIDUAL): every circuit mutation applies with no windowing system present, and a program can build a circuit without emitting save text" |

**No scope failed to resolve. Nothing was dropped and nothing was left in `planned_features`.**

**Independent corroboration in the far direction.** Every filed feature's `serves_capstones` was read and inverted. The features carrying `297` are exactly `{315, 316, 318, 319, 322, 329, 336, 337, 341, 349, 365}` — no extra, none missing. Had #328 been written where #329 belongs, the inversion would have shown #328 claiming `[302]` and #329 claiming `[297]` with nothing pointing back; it does not.

## 2. The DAG walk, per feature, before each number was written

**Upstream, followed to sources.** `#315 blocked_by []`, `#322 blocked_by []`, `#337 blocked_by []` and `#349 blocked_by []` are sources. `#336 blocked_by [315]`. `#341 blocked_by [322]`. `#316 blocked_by [317, 337]` with `#317 blocked_by [353, 354]` and `#353 blocked_by []`, a source. `#319 blocked_by [334]`, `#334 blocked_by [315]`. `#318 blocked_by [319, 337]`. `#365 blocked_by [336, 349]`. `#329 blocked_by [316, 318, 341, 365]`. Closure: {#315, #316, #317, #318, #319, #322, #329, #334, #336, #337, #341, #349, #353, #354, #365}, every branch terminating at a source.

**Downstream, followed to sinks.** `#315 blocks [314, 334, 336, 352, 358]`; `#316 blocks [324, 329, 355, 369]`; `#318 blocks [329, 333, 357]`; `#319 blocks [318, 332, 340, 343, 356, 357, 363, 364]`; `#322 blocks [341, 344, 370]`; `#329 blocks []` — a sink; `#336 blocks [321, 327, 332, 358, 365, 366]`; `#337 blocks [316, 318, 326, 345, 348, 352]`; `#341 blocks [329]`; `#349 blocks [323, 365, 366]`; `#365 blocks [329, 366]`. Continuing outward terminates in sinks throughout.

**Result.** **No number in the capstone range 295-313 occurs in any `blocked_by` or `blocks` reached by the walk**, so no feature in this closure is ordered behind a capstone and no path returns to #297. This capstone's `blocked_by` and `blocks` stay `[]`, the mirror of the same fact. Run mechanically over all 57 filed features as a cross-check: the feature-tier ordering graph is acyclic, every edge is mirrored with no half-edges, and no feature anywhere names a capstone in either ordering field.

**Ordering re-derivation.** CAP-04 has `requires_capstones: []` and `blocked_by: []` — no capstone precedes this one — so there is no inter-capstone ordering to propagate onto the eleven newly-numbered features and nothing lapses.

## 3. Graph regeneration — two arrows deleted, three added, eight kept

Rule applied: an arrow `X --> Y` is drawn **if and only if Y's own `blocked_by` contains X**.

**Deleted — two arrows no feature declares:**

- `F001 --> F040` (#315 → #349). #349's `blocked_by` is `[]`; FEAT-040 is a source. #315 blocks `[314, 334, 336, 352, 358]`, and #349 is not among them. (The same phantom edge was found and deleted on #298.)
- `F015 --> F043` (#337 → #329). #329's `blocked_by` is `[316, 318, 341, 365]`; 337 is not in it. FEAT-015 reaches the canvas *transitively*, through #316 and #318, which is what the two added edges below make visible.

**Added — three the features declare and the graph had omitted:**

- `F001 --> F004` (#315 → #336): `#336 blocked_by [315]`. This is the edge that makes FEAT-001's residual a genuine root rather than a side lint.
- `F015 --> F008` (#337 → #316): `#316 blocked_by [317, 337]`.
- `F015 --> F014` (#337 → #318): `#318 blocked_by [319, 337]`.

**Kept, verified on the far side:** `F040 --> F041`, `F004 --> F041` (#365 `blocked_by [336, 349]`); `F026 --> F027` (#341 `blocked_by [322]`); `F013 --> F014` (#318 `blocked_by [319, 337]`); `F014 --> F043`, `F008 --> F043`, `F027 --> F043`, `F041 --> F043` (#329 `blocked_by [316, 318, 341, 365]`).

**Two findings.**

1. **FEAT-015 (#337) is upstream of the canvas, but by two hops, not one.** The deleted direct arrow was not wrong about the dependency, it was wrong about its shape: `#337 → #316 → #329` and `#337 → #318 → #329`. That matters for scheduling, because it means the headless `CircuitOp` work must land before *two* other features can start, not merely before the canvas.
2. **FEAT-043 (#329) is this capstone's private spine, and the filed data says so outright.** Its `serves_capstones` is `[297]` alone and its `blocks` is `[]` — it serves no other capstone and nothing waits on it. That is direct corroboration of Open Question 5's recommended default ("this one pays"), which until now rested on an argument rather than on a machine-readable fact. It is also the graph's sink: every other required feature reaches CAP-04 either through #329 or directly.

## 4. Consequences recorded in the body

- The filing-pass sentence "No feature in this set is filed as an issue yet…" is **withdrawn as false** in §2 and replaced with the resolution.
- §2 roster rows carry the filed number alongside each feature; Status cells say "filed as #N, open". The Cost table rows carry the numbers too.
- The "Recorded DAG walk" paragraph is replaced by the walk actually performed over filed machine blocks.
- §3's package-layer deference is unchanged in substance — **#298 remains the named owner of the FEAT-040/FEAT-041 contract and this capstone cites rather than re-authors it** — and now names the features by number (#349, #365) so the obligation is machine-readable.
- §3's value-seam risk (FEAT-026 ↔ FEAT-027) gains a machine-block fact: `#341 blocked_by [322]`, so the four-state core genuinely does precede the strength lattice in the filed graph. What no edge can enforce is that they agree on **one** lattice, which is why AC-3 remains the only place they are forced to interact.
- Open Question 5 gains its corroboration: #329's `serves_capstones` is `[297]` alone.
- Open Questions 1, 2, 3 and 6 are annotated: each was recorded as blocking the *filing* of a feature that is now filed, so each blocks that feature's **children** instead.
- §5's "a required feature is filed" bullet is discharged and replaced by a bullet requiring the graph to be re-derived from the features' machine blocks.

**No measurement was changed.** The 86-132 mw standalone sum, the 31-46 mw marginal band, the 7-14 mw demo slice, the 9-of-35 no-realization census, KC-04-2's 60 s budget and KC-04-5's 13.5 mw trigger are all carried unaltered. Resolving a scope to an issue number is bookkeeping, not a re-cost.

## ORDERING — MIRROR (round-2 review, slice: ordering-coherence): two edges ordering work behind this capstone are withdrawn

Recorded here because both edges named this issue and a half-edge is worth less than none. **No change is made to this capstone's scope, criteria, required feature set or band.**

### The edges

| Issue | As filed | Why it is illegal / wrong |
|---|---|---|
| **#576** — FEAT-C33-2, documented assignment cycle (`tier:feature`) | `ordering_after: ["#300 CAP-06 verdict slice / #369 FEAT-053"]` | A feature ordered behind a capstone. | **#755** — TASK-C576-1, the distribution/submission layout spec, 0.5 mw (`tier:task`) | `ordering_after: [300, 369]` | A task ordered behind a capstone, and behind a feature whose blockers it does not consume. |

Both now point at **#466** (TASK-0111 — the verdict engine, expectations and report) where they consume anything at all, and at nothing where they do not. #300 and #369 are demoted to `related` on both.

### Why the edge shape matters here specifically

A capstone closes only when everything beneath it closes. So `ordering_after: [300]` does not mean "after the CAP-06 verdict slice" — the thing its author plainly intended — it means **"after the last of CAP-06"**, including the 25–36 mw handout-library half that #508 explicitly dropped from near-term scope. Every consumer written this way is deferred past a scope decision that has already been taken against it.

The correct encoding, and the one applied: **cite the artifact, not its owner.** #466 is the artifact. This is the same rule #224's 2026-08-02 edge-legality REPLAN applied to itself when it removed #163 and #59 as capstone-to-capstone edges and replaced them with feature-side edges.

### Consequence for this capstone

Mildly favourable and worth recording: two downstream items that appeared to wait on CAP-06 do not. #755 is unblocked outright and is the cheapest ready item in the CAP-33 cluster; #576's AC-1, AC-4 and AC-5 are unblocked, with only AC-2/AC-3 genuinely waiting on #466. Nothing is added to this capstone's required set, and nothing that was waiting on it stops waiting where the wait was real — #576 AC-2/AC-3 and #757 still consume #466, which remains CAP-06's to deliver.

**Standing guidance for future consumers:** order after **#466** for the verdict engine, report and exit status 3; order after **#369** only for properties, equivalence or coverage (TASK-0112's unfiled payload). Do not order after **#300**.

Nine filed features that are **not** in the required set are declared prerequisites of members of it: **#339 (FEAT-021)**, #315 (FEAT-001), #336 (FEAT-004), #319 (FEAT-013), #318 (FEAT-014), #325 (FEAT-031), #343 (FEAT-033), #353 (FEAT-005), #317 (FEAT-007).

The reason is legible: a real RV32 core has `inout` ports, and the third direction does not exist in the IR at `2d0ca9d`. That is arguably a §1 minimality answer — step 1 imports a real core, and a real core has bidirectional ports — which would make FEAT-021 a **missing required row** rather than a transitive prerequisite. **Nothing is promoted by this REPLAN.** A rule-E promotion needs its §1 minimality answer written down and its band added to the required sum (113–175 mw), and asserting one inside a bookkeeping pass is exactly the quiet edit rule E forbids. **Open Question 6** is rewritten to carry the disposition, with the recommended default now split: option (a) — walk-recorded transitive prerequisite — for eight of them, and option (c) — argue it into the required set — raised explicitly for **#339** in a follow-up `REPLAN:`. None of the nine becomes a `blocked_by` entry here, because **no filed feature declares `blocks: [304]`** and a capstone-side ordering edge with no feature-side counterpart is an unmirrored assertion.

## 5. The FEAT-019 disagreement, decided on the merits

`docs/plan/capstones/CAP-08-import-third-party-core.md:65` at `2d0ca9d` reads:

`| FEAT-019 | Yosys JSON write | round-tripping the imported core back out is how the import is proven lossless | beneficial |`

This issue carries FEAT-019 (#321) as **required**. **Decision: the issue is right, the document is wrong** — and not by the template's authority rule alone. Three independent grounds:

1. **The document contradicts itself.** Its own stated reason for the row — "round-tripping the imported core back out is how the import is proven lossless" — *is* §1 step 7 and AC-6, which are unconditional here. A row whose justification is an unconditional acceptance criterion cannot be optional.
2. **The tree.** Verified at `2d0ca9d`: `src/jls/hdl/yosys/` contains `YosysNetlist` (whose entry point is `public static YosysNetlist parse(String jsonText)` — a reader), `CellValidator`, `JsonValue`, `YosysLocator` and `YosysVersion`. The only emitters in `src/jls/hdl/` are `VerilogEmitter` and `VhdlEmitter`, which emit HDL *text*, not a Yosys JSON netlist. `grep -rln 'YosysWriter\|YosysJsonEmitter\|writeYosys' src/` returns `0`.
3. **The minimality test.** Remove FEAT-019 and §1 step 7 cannot be executed at all — nothing else in the tree writes a netlist. That is precisely the test a beneficial row is supposed to fail.

The promotion itself predates this REPLAN (it was made in the earlier correction pass, and the required sum was re-printed then from 110–171 to 113–175 mw). What this REPLAN adds is the explicit decision against the corpus document, the tree evidence for it, and a **Completion Criteria line requiring `CAP-08-import-third-party-core.md:65` to be corrected** — or this issue's grading refuted by a further `REPLAN:` that re-derives §2's minimality and re-prints the sum.

Do not open questions, file REPLANs, or write reconciliation obligations for this class. Record the prerequisite and move on."

5161234653.body:
`REPLAN:` roster resolution — all six `planned_features` scopes resolved to filed issues; `planned_features` is now **empty**; DAG re-walked outward against the filed features; mermaid regenerated from the corrected machine block.

**Why this REPLAN exists.** This capstone was filed when no feature issue existed, so it carried `requires_features: []` and its closed required set as six one-line scopes in `planned_features`. All 57 features are now filed as #314-#370. The template's rule E makes a roster change a REPLAN, not a quiet edit, so the resolution is recorded here.

## 1. Resolution — scope → filed number

Every number below was verified **against the issue title**, not against position in the number range, because the numbering is not monotonic in FEAT order.

| planned scope | resolves to | verified title prefix |
|---|---|---|
| FEAT-046 analog solver core + determinism gate | **#351** | "FEAT-046: JLS solves a continuous-time circuit in pure Java, produces the same bits on every platform…" |
| FEAT-047 physical time base + nominal real-time scalar | **#367** | "FEAT-047: a circuit can declare what one tick means in physical time, once…" |
| FEAT-048 A2D/D2A bridges + A-STEP synchronization | **#368** | "FEAT-048: a drawn design crosses between continuous and discrete in both directions…" |
| FEAT-049 analog device models, drawn palette, convergence hardening | **#331** | "FEAT-049: a student draws analog devices the way they already draw gates…" |
| FEAT-027 strength lattice, driver kinds and net kinds | **#341** | "FEAT-027: a net has a kind and a driver has a strength…" |
| FEAT-014 (RESIDUAL) per-view geometry in the shared model | **#318** | "FEAT-014 (RESIDUAL): nets, groups and nested instances get names that survive sharing, and geometry becomes one record per view" |

**Six scopes in, six numbers out. No scope failed to resolve, none was dropped, and no membership changed** — so §2's sufficiency and minimality arguments carry over unaltered and the Cost section's 61.5-94 mw standalone sum is unmoved. `requires_features: [351, 367, 368, 331, 341, 318]`; `planned_features: []`.

**Document cross-check (no disagreement found).** `docs/plan/capstones/CAP-12-heart-rate-monitor.md` was re-read at `2d0ca9dcd9db78b36c3caf4c6c57dd8701862cc7`. Its feature table (lines 58-66) grades FEAT-046, FEAT-047, FEAT-048, FEAT-049, FEAT-027 and FEAT-014 **required** and FEAT-045, FEAT-043, FEAT-008 **beneficial** — identical to this issue's partition. There is nothing to adjudicate for this capstone.

## 2. The DAG walk, per feature, outward — required before adding each feature

Walked each feature's **own machine block** `blocked_by` outward, transitively, until every branch terminates. Cross-tier cycles are possible because a feature may be `blocked_by` a capstone, so that direction was checked explicitly.

- **FEAT-046 (#351)** — `blocked_by: []`. Terminates immediately. No path to #305.
- **FEAT-047 (#367)** — `blocked_by: []`. Terminates immediately. No path to #305.
- **FEAT-049 (#331)** — `blocked_by: [351]` → #351 `blocked_by: []` → terminates. Closure `{351}`. No path to #305.
- **FEAT-048 (#368)** — `blocked_by: [331, 351]` → #331 → #351 → terminates. Closure `{331, 351}`. No path to #305.
- **FEAT-027 (#341)** — `blocked_by: [322]` → FEAT-026 (#322) `blocked_by: []` → terminates. Closure `{322}`. No path to #305.
- **FEAT-014 (#318)** — `blocked_by: [319, 337]` → FEAT-013 (#319) `blocked_by: []`; FEAT-015 (#337) `blocked_by: [315]` → FEAT-001 (#315) `blocked_by: []` → terminates. Closure `{315, 319, 337}`. No path to #305.

**Union of all six closures: `{315, 319, 322, 331, 337, 351}`. It contains no capstone number (#295-#313) and does not contain #305.**

**The cross-tier arm, checked directly rather than assumed.** Every `tier:feature` issue in the tracker was read and its `blocked_by` inspected: **no filed feature declares a `blocked_by` entry naming any capstone**. There is therefore no feature→capstone ordering arc anywhere for a cycle to close through, and this capstone's own `blocks:` is empty (nothing declares `blocked_by: [305]`). **Result: no cycle. The ordering graph remains a DAG.**

## 3. Three graph edges withdrawn, and why — this is a real change, not bookkeeping

The graph as filed asserted nine intra-set edges. The features as filed declare **three**:

- declared and kept: **#351 → #331** (`#331 blocked_by [351]`, mirrored by `#351 blocks [331]`), **#351 → #368** (`#368 blocked_by [351]`, mirrored by `#351 blocks [368]`), **#331 → #368** (`#368 blocked_by [331]`, mirrored by `#331 blocks [368]`).
- asserted at filing but declared by **neither endpoint**, and therefore **withdrawn**: **FEAT-014 (#318) → FEAT-049 (#331)** — #331's `blocked_by` is `[351]` only and #318's `blocks` is `[329, 333, 357]`; **FEAT-047 (#367) → FEAT-048 (#368)** — #368's `blocked_by` is `[331, 351]` only and #367's `blocks` is `[]`; **FEAT-027 (#341) → FEAT-048 (#368)** — #368's `blocked_by` is `[331, 351]` only and #341's `blocks` is `[329]`.

They are withdrawn rather than mirrored because rule A makes each feature's own machine block the source of truth for the edges it can express, and an edge drawn on a capstone that neither endpoint carries is unenforceable — the same reasoning #310 applied when it removed three unmirrored edges at its own filing. **The information is not discarded**: the three are recorded in §3 and raised as new **Open Question 9**, with a recommended default (contract-agreement rather than landing-order for FEAT-014 → FEAT-049 and FEAT-027 → FEAT-048; a genuine specification dependency for FEAT-047 → FEAT-048). Whichever way OQ-9 resolves, the edge is written onto **both** endpoints in one REPLAN before it is redrawn here.

## 4. Out-of-set predecessors, recorded but not promoted to `blocked_by`

The walk surfaced three features that must land before two required rows but are not themselves required here: **#322** (FEAT-026) in front of #341, and **#319** / **#337** (FEAT-013, FEAT-015) in front of #318. They are **not** added to this capstone's `blocked_by`, because the template defines that field as the mirror of a feature-side edge naming this capstone and none of them declares one; the ordering already reaches this capstone transitively through the required feature that carries the composition edge. They are named in §3 and in Related Issues so a scheduler sees them — #322 in particular is a large row sitting behind FEAT-027.

## 5. Mermaid regenerated from the corrected machine block

Nodes = this capstone + the six issues in `requires_features`, nothing else. Edges = the three declared intra-set ordering edges + six composition edges. Checked by construction: same set in the graph, the machine block and the §2 roster; **no node the machine block does not hold**; **no arrow at an issue carried only in `related`** (#297, #298, #299, #303, #308, #309 appear nowhere in the graph); **no direct capstone-to-capstone ordering edge**; **no beneficial feature drawn with an arrowhead** (FEAT-045 #346, FEAT-043 #329, FEAT-008 #316 are named in §2 and drawn nowhere).

## 6. Filing-pass sentences retired

The required set is fully resolved, so the following are now false everywhere and were removed or rewritten: the machine-block comment "none of the required features is filed yet; see planned_features"; §2's "No feature in this set is filed as an issue yet, so `requires_features` is empty and every row is carried in `planned_features`"; §3's filing-time walk text; and §5's "A required feature is filed" clause, replaced by a clause governing **additions** to a now-closed, fully-numbered set. Open Questions 1-4 said "Blocks filing FEAT-0xx" — those features are filed, so each now names what it actually blocks: **execution**. §2's roster rows and the beneficial paragraph now carry filed numbers throughout.

5161589592.body:
ADJUDICATED: Open Question 9 — the three withdrawn ordering edges. **All three withdrawals are confirmed. Nothing is added to any feature's machine block, and nothing is redrawn here.**

**Method.** Every mermaid ordering edge in all nineteen capstones (#295–#313) was checked against the two endpoint features' own filed `blocked_by`/`blocks`, both directions: **0 graph-asserted edges the features do not hold, 0 feature-held edges a graph omits**, 0 asymmetries across the 57 machine blocks. Each feature's filed `blocked_by` was then diffed against its own corpus `## Prerequisite features` table; they agree on every row of all 57 features except FEAT-031 (#325), whose corpus row itself says its FEAT-030 dependency "must not be used to gate the whole feature". So these three edges are absent from the per-feature technical analysis as well as from the machine blocks.

Rule applied: an arrow means *A must land before B*.

| Withdrawn edge | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **#367 → #368** (FEAT-047 → FEAT-048) | withdrawal confirmed | Reading (b) — "real and under-declared" — does not survive the corpus. FEAT-046's prerequisite table, the feature FEAT-048 *does* wait on, states: "The solver owns its own time internally and needs no declared physical time base… **FEAT-047 becomes necessary the moment a solved waveform must be reported in seconds rather than ticks**." A bridge publishes an exact crossing **tick**; converting that tick to seconds is FEAT-047's job downstream. FEAT-047's AC-2 makes absence the default and keeps every existing golden byte-identical, so FEAT-048 is fully specifiable and testable with no time base declared. Reading (a) is correct: a filing-time sketch. FEAT-047 stays **required** for this capstone — a 0.16 Hz high-pass is a statement about seconds — but that is composition, already drawn. |
| **#341 → #368** (FEAT-027 → FEAT-048) | withdrawal confirmed | Different concerns. FEAT-048 ships its own domain check — the port/net alphabet that keeps continuous and discrete apart — inside its own scope. FEAT-027 is driver strength, open-drain and pull-ups on **digital** nets. FEAT-048's corpus prerequisites are FEAT-046 and FEAT-049, and neither table names FEAT-027. |
| **#318 → #331** (FEAT-014 → FEAT-049) | withdrawal confirmed | FEAT-049's corpus table names FEAT-046 alone, with the reason given: "There is no matrix to stamp into, no Newton loop to harden and no timestep controller to veto until the solver core exists." Instance-path addressing and per-view geometry gate neither the device models nor the palette. |

OQ-9 is discharged in branch (a) for all three: artefacts of a filing-time sketch; the features are right to omit them.

No cost band, acceptance criterion or roster row was changed by this comment.

5161342206.body:
REPLAN: all eight `planned_features` scopes resolved to filed issues; `planned_features` is now empty. Mermaid regenerated from the filed feature machine blocks — **seven of the nine edges this issue drew at filing are withdrawn and four new ones are added**. The re-walk also found that two rows §2 grades BENEFICIAL are declared prerequisites of a REQUIRED one; that is now Open Question 10.

## 1. Resolution, scope by scope

Every number was checked against the issue **title**, not inferred from position — the FEAT-NNN sequence is not monotonic in issue number (FEAT-037 is #327 while FEAT-038 is #326).

| planned scope | resolved to | title check |
|---|---|---|
| FEAT-053 test-vector front end and autograding at scale | **#369** | "FEAT-053: 'this design was exercised' becomes 'this design passed or failed…'" |
| FEAT-034 retirement-indexed parity harness and `RetireRecord` | **#347** | "FEAT-034: two implementations of the same machine are compared per retired instruction…" |

| FEAT-023 (RESIDUAL) external toolchain differential oracle | **#359** | "FEAT-023 (RESIDUAL): an emitter that produces valid-but-wrong output fails a build…" |
| FEAT-009 measurement gate and tracked calibration fixture | **#335** | "FEAT-009: every wall-clock claim in the plan divides by a measured constant…" |
| FEAT-005 quadratic and materializing I/O paths eliminated | **#353** | "FEAT-005: a long batch run costs linear time and bounded memory…" |

| FEAT-007 CI long-run lanes, timeouts and cross-platform parity | **#317** | "FEAT-007: every CI job is time-bounded, an hours-long run has a lane that is not the required gate…" |

`requires_features: [317, 322, 335, 347, 353, 354, 359, 369]`. `planned_features: []`. Nothing dropped, nothing descoped.

The seven **beneficial** rows are filed too — FEAT-024 **#360**, FEAT-030 **#362**, FEAT-031 **#325**, FEAT-032 **#324**, FEAT-033 **#343**, FEAT-035 **#363**, FEAT-038 **#326** — and were added to `related` (reference-only, never blocking). They stay out of `requires_features` and out of the graph, per rule E.

## 2. The DAG walk, re-walked outward from every added feature

Transitive `blocked_by` closure per required feature, over the **filed** machine blocks:

- FEAT-005 `#353 -> {}`
- FEAT-006 `#354 -> {#353}`
- FEAT-007 `#317 -> {#353, #354}`
- FEAT-009 `#335 -> {#353}`
- FEAT-023 `#359 -> {#317, #358, #353, #354, #336, #315}`
- FEAT-026 `#322 -> {}`
- FEAT-034 `#347 -> {#325, #335, #343, #353, #319, #334, #315}`

**No closure contains #306, or any other capstone number.** No path returns here; the ordering graph stays a DAG.

**The structural check behind that, run once for the whole tracker.** Cross-tier cycles are possible because features may be `blocked_by` capstones. Across **all 57 filed feature machine blocks** (#314-#370), the union of every `blocked_by`, `blocks` and `requires_tasks` entry contains **no number in the capstone range #295-#313**. Not one filed feature declares an edge to any capstone, so no cross-tier cycle exists anywhere in the tracker at this commit. Re-run on every REPLAN.

## 3. Mermaid regenerated — seven edges withdrawn, four added

A feature's own machine block is the source of truth for the edges it can express (rule A). The graph now derives from those blocks.

| edge drawn at filing | status | why |
|---|---|---|
| `F026 --> F053` | **withdrawn** | #369 `blocked_by: [316, 321, 347]` — no #322 |
| `F005 --> F053` | **withdrawn** | same — no #353 |
| `F006 --> F053` | **withdrawn** | same — no #354 |

The net shape changes from *a fan into FEAT-053* to *a chain out of FEAT-005*. Node set = this capstone + the 8 entries of `requires_features` = the 8 required rows of the §2 roster. 8 nodes, 8 composition edges, 7 ordering edges. No beneficial feature has a node or an arrowhead; no out-of-set prerequisite is a node; no direct capstone-to-capstone edge; no arrow at anything carried only in `related`. Graph, machine block and roster agree by construction.

## 4. The substantive finding: five out-of-set prerequisites, two of them graded beneficial here

Five filed features that are **not** in this capstone's required set are declared prerequisites of members of it:

- **#316 (FEAT-008, editor decomposition)** and **#321 (FEAT-019, Yosys JSON write)** are prerequisites of required **#369 (FEAT-053)**. Neither appears in this issue's roster in any grading. #369 cannot land until both do, so this capstone cannot close until both do, and nothing here tracks them. #321 declares `blocks: [369]` from its own side, so the edge is mirrored and not a one-sided claim. **#321 is a required row of CAP-08 (#304)**, so the two capstones' schedules are coupled through a feature only one of them names. Added to §3 as a risk.
- **#358 (FEAT-018)** is a prerequisite of required **#359 (FEAT-023)**.
- **#325 (FEAT-031)** and **#343 (FEAT-033)** are prerequisites of required **#347 (FEAT-034)** — and §2 grades **both beneficial**.

That last one is the one that matters. Filed FEAT-034 carries `blocked_by: [325, 335, 343]`. So two rows this issue calls optional must land before a required row can, and therefore before this capstone can close.

**Nothing is promoted into the required set by this REPLAN.** Rule E asks "what breaks in §1 if it is removed", and for FEAT-031 and FEAT-033 the honest answer is still *nothing* — §1's seven steps run without either, and AC-7's two admissible attestations were deliberately chosen so step 6 does not wait on FEAT-033. Rule applied: an arrow means *A must land before B*. **"FEAT-053 needs something to run against" is the false arrow this set is built on** — a corpus to grade, a long run to grade it over, a lane to run it in. None of those is a construction dependency; #311 states the same test in one line for its own copy of it ("'Needs a corpus to run against' is a convenience, not an ordering dependency"). FEAT-053's corpus prerequisites are FEAT-008, FEAT-034 and FEAT-019, and all three are about what the verdict engine is *built out of*.

| Withdrawn edge | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **#353 → #369** (FEAT-005 → FEAT-053) | confirmed — **and already ordered anyway** | The filed tier carries **#353 → #317 → #316 → #369**, so FEAT-005 provably precedes FEAT-053 today without this arrow. The direct edge is a transitive shortcut that adds no constraint. |
| **#354 → #369** (FEAT-006 → FEAT-053) | confirmed — **already ordered** | Likewise **#354 → #317 → #316 → #369**. |
| **#335 → #369** (FEAT-009 → FEAT-053) | confirmed — **already ordered** | Likewise **#335 → #347 → #369**, through the parity harness FEAT-053 genuinely consumes. |
| **#322 → #369** (FEAT-026 → FEAT-053) | confirmed | A verdict is PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN on a named vector and signal. Four-state values widen which designs can be graded honestly; they are not an input to the verdict, the front end or the report. |
| **#359 → #369** (FEAT-023 → FEAT-053) | confirmed | The external-toolchain differential oracle and the batch grader are two independent oracles over the same designs. Neither reads the other's output; neither corpus table names the other. |
| **#322 → #347** (FEAT-026 → FEAT-034) | confirmed | The retirement alphabet deliberately has no field for a value's X/Z state, exactly as it has none for cycles or pipeline state. FEAT-034's corpus prerequisites are FEAT-033, FEAT-031 and FEAT-009. |
| **#354 → #335** (FEAT-006 → FEAT-009) | confirmed | FEAT-009's corpus prerequisite is FEAT-005 alone, and the reason is specific: "measuring per-event cost through a quadratic stimulus parse measures the parse". Suspend, watch and interrupt make a **long** run survivable; they are not needed to take a **measurement** on a tracked fixture. #296 records the adjacent case — #335 rejects the FEAT-007 edge in its own machine block because the two share a task, and a shared task is composition, not ordering. |

5161316101.justification: REPLAN documenting graph analysis and Open Question 9. Findings superseded by comment 5170566529's D13 decision. Content fully absorbed into body's current state (no OQ-9, finalized mermaid). Planning bookkeeping archived.
5161316101.body:
REPLAN: all four `planned_features` scopes resolved to filed issues; `planned_features` is now empty. Mermaid regenerated from the filed feature machine blocks. The re-walk **refuted two of the three edges §3 recorded at filing and found a third the filing pass missed** — the missed one contradicts this issue's beneficial grading of FEAT-049, and is now Open Question 9.

## 1. Resolution, scope by scope

Every number was checked against the issue **title**, not inferred from position — the FEAT-NNN sequence is not monotonic in issue number.

| planned scope | resolved to | title check |
|---|---|---|
| FEAT-045 host audio sink and source without a solver | **#346** | "FEAT-045: a drawn circuit makes a sound and hears one — host audio in and out, with no solver, and deterministic in CI" |
| FEAT-047 the physical time base and the nominal real-time scalar | **#367** | "FEAT-047: a circuit can declare what one tick means in physical time…" |
| FEAT-046 the analog solver core and its determinism gate | **#351** | "FEAT-046: JLS solves a continuous-time circuit in pure Java…" |
| FEAT-048 A2D/D2A bridge elements and A-STEP synchronization | **#368** | "FEAT-048: a drawn design crosses between continuous and discrete in both directions…" |

`requires_features: [346, 351, 367, 368]`. `planned_features: []`. Every scope resolved; nothing was dropped and nothing was descoped.

The three **beneficial** rows are also filed — FEAT-049 **#331**, FEAT-043 **#329**, FEAT-008 **#316** — and were added to `related` (reference-only, never blocking). They are deliberately **not** in `requires_features` and **not** in the graph, per §2's note and rule E.

## 2. The DAG walk, re-walked outward from every added feature

Transitive `blocked_by` closure per required feature, over the **filed** machine blocks:

- FEAT-045 `#346 -> {}` (declares `blocked_by: []`)
- FEAT-046 `#351 -> {}` (declares `blocked_by: []`)
- FEAT-047 `#367 -> {}` (declares `blocked_by: []`)
- FEAT-048 `#368 -> {#331, #351}` (declares `blocked_by: [331, 351]`)

**No closure contains #308, or any other capstone number.** No path returns to this capstone; the ordering graph stays a DAG.

**The structural check behind that, run once for the whole tracker.** Cross-tier cycles are possible because features may be `blocked_by` capstones — so the question is whether any filed feature is. Across **all 57 filed feature machine blocks** (#314-#370), the union of every `blocked_by`, `blocks` and `requires_tasks` entry contains **no number in the capstone range #295-#313**. Not one filed feature declares an edge to any capstone. No cross-tier cycle exists anywhere in the tracker at this commit. Re-run on every REPLAN — the first feature that declares `blocked_by: [<a capstone>]` reopens the question for every capstone downstream of it.

## 3. The filing-pass walk was wrong, in two directions

§3 as filed recorded: `FEAT-047 -> none; FEAT-045 -> {FEAT-047}; FEAT-046 -> {FEAT-047}; FEAT-048 -> {FEAT-046}`, and concluded *"every edge in the walk lands inside the closed set, so the set is closed under rule E as well as acyclic."*

**Two edges do not exist.** #346 (FEAT-045) declares `blocked_by: []`. #351 (FEAT-046) declares `blocked_by: []`. #367 (FEAT-047) declares `blocks: []` and names 346 and 351 only in `related`, which is reference-only and never blocking. So `FEAT-047 -> FEAT-045` and `FEAT-047 -> FEAT-046` are withdrawn from the graph.

FEAT-047 stays **required**. That is a composition claim, not an ordering claim, and §2's minimality answer is untouched: a "sample rate" over dimensionless ticks is a number with no referent. But the enforcement has moved — nothing in the tracker now forces FEAT-047 to land first, so a maintainer could build the codec and the resampler against an assumed nominal tick and discover the gap only at AC-1. That is added to §3 as a named risk.

**One edge was missed, and it is the important one.** `#368 declares blocked_by: [331, 351]` — and **#331 is FEAT-049**, which this issue grades **beneficial**.

The filing-pass sentence *"the corresponding walks in #303 and #305 reach one node this set does not — FEAT-049's element-admission slice — because their §1 steps require a drawn analog element, and this capstone's do not"* is **refuted, not qualified**. The prerequisite is a property of FEAT-048 itself, declared on FEAT-048's own machine block, and it does not vary with which capstone consumes FEAT-048. The reasoning underneath survives — §1 step 5's R-2R ladder really is built from FEAT-048's bridge elements, not from FEAT-049's device models — but the conclusion drawn from it does not.

## 4. What that costs, and what is NOT being done about it

FEAT-049 (#331) is now simultaneously:

- **beneficial in the sufficiency sense** — §1 steps 1-5 and 7 do not need device models; §2's minimality answer for it is still *nothing breaks*; and
- **blocking in the ordering sense** — #368 cannot land until #331 does, and this capstone cannot close until #368 lands.

**Nothing is promoted into the required set by this REPLAN.** Rule E promotion needs a §1 minimality answer — "what breaks in §1 if it is removed" — and FEAT-049 does not have one here. Promoting it to make the graph tidy would put work inside the closed set that the minimality test rejects, and would silently enlarge the required sum by 21-33 mw.

**Open Question 9 (new)** owns the disposition, with three options and a recommended default:

- (a) leave FEAT-049 beneficial, accept the ordering, record it as a close-out obligation;
- **(b) adopt the carve #303 already adopted** — FEAT-049's element-admission slice (the analog port permit and the datum/node-partition contract) becomes a required row in its own right, and the model library, palette and convergence hardening stay beneficial and funded by #305; **recommended**;
- (c) ask #368 whether `blocked_by: [331]` is over-declared — whether a bridge needs the whole of FEAT-049 or only the terminal-admission part.

Ordering `#351 → #331 → #368` already declared on the feature side and mirrored in this issue's DoD ("#331 closed as landed before #368 closes"). |

5161298914.justification: REPLAN roster resolution bookkeeping. Content fully absorbed: the body now shows requires_features with all ten filed issue numbers and discusses each feature. The planning-to-filing resolution is implicit in the current machine block.
5161298914.body:
`REPLAN:` roster resolution — all ten `planned_features` scopes resolved to filed issues; `planned_features` is now **empty**; DAG re-walked outward against the filed features; mermaid regenerated from the corrected machine block.

**Why this REPLAN exists.** This capstone was filed when no feature issue existed, so it carried `requires_features: []` and its closed required set as ten one-line scopes in `planned_features`. All 57 features are now filed as #314-#370. Rule E makes a roster change a REPLAN, not a quiet edit. This REPLAN is also the trigger for Open Question 1's mirror obligation to #59, since #59's #61 and #62 now have numbered feature-tier successors.

## 1. Resolution — scope → filed number

Every number verified **against the issue title**. That check is not ceremonial here: **FEAT-019 is #321 while FEAT-020 is #320**, and **FEAT-037 is #327 while FEAT-038 is #326** — adjacent FEAT numbers mapping to non-adjacent issue numbers in *reversed* order. Position in the range is not evidence.

| planned scope | resolves to | verified title prefix |
|---|---|---|
| FEAT-018 hierarchical instance structure in the HDL IR | **#358** | "FEAT-018: a decomposed design exports — the HDL IR carries more than one module and an instantiation statement…" |
| FEAT-020 Yosys JSON read, mapper parity with the validator | **#320** | "FEAT-020: an imported Yosys netlist runs — every cell the validator accepts becomes a drawn element, and hierarchy survives" |
| FEAT-023 (RESIDUAL) external toolchain differential oracle | **#359** | "FEAT-023 (RESIDUAL): an emitter that produces valid-but-wrong output fails a build — the open toolchains become required behavioral witnesses…" |
| FEAT-019 Yosys JSON write | **#321** | "FEAT-019: a circuit drawn in JLS is readable by the open synthesis ecosystem — JLS writes the netlist Yosys reads" |
| FEAT-004 shared net-partition IR + stable net naming | **#336** | "FEAT-004: exactly one net partition in JLS, and a synthesized net name that survives an unrelated edit" |
| FEAT-001 (RESIDUAL) registry-keyed table totality | **#315** | "FEAT-001 (RESIDUAL): a thirty-sixth element type cannot ship until every registry-keyed table has a row for it" |
| FEAT-021 bidirectional ports | **#339** | "FEAT-021: JLS can declare a bidirectional port — the third direction exists in the IR…" |
| FEAT-026 four-state value core with a resolution fold | **#322** | "FEAT-026: a signal can say \"unknown\" and \"undriven\" per bit, and contention resolves as a property of the driver set…" |
| FEAT-037 reset semantics, clock and domain architecture | **#327** | "FEAT-037: a drawn register has an honest reset that exports as a reset, and every clock-domain crossing in a design is reported" |
| FEAT-022 (RESIDUAL) readability rubric + hierarchy placement | **#342** | "FEAT-022 (RESIDUAL): every cell the mapper realizes places and routes, hierarchy instances arrive as instances, and the readability rubric is reported at core scale" |

**Ten scopes in, ten numbers out. No scope failed to resolve, none was dropped, and no membership changed** — so §2's sufficiency argument carries over unaltered and the Cost section's 67-101 mw standalone sum is unmoved. `requires_features: [358, 320, 359, 321, 336, 315, 339, 322, 327, 342]`; `planned_features: []`.

**Document cross-check (no disagreement found).** `docs/plan/capstones/CAP-15-hdl-toolchain-parity.md` re-read at `2d0ca9dcd9db78b36c3caf4c6c57dd8701862cc7`: its feature table (lines 61-73) grades all ten **required** and FEAT-024, FEAT-016, FEAT-044 **beneficial** — identical to this issue's partition. Nothing to adjudicate here.

## 2. The DAG walk, per feature, outward — required before adding each feature

Walked each feature's **own machine block** `blocked_by` outward, transitively, until every branch terminates.

- **FEAT-001 (#315)** — `blocked_by: []`. Terminates. No path to #310.
- **FEAT-021 (#339)** — `blocked_by: []`. Terminates. No path to #310.
- **FEAT-026 (#322)** — `blocked_by: []`. Terminates. No path to #310.
- **FEAT-004 (#336)** — `blocked_by: [315]` → #315 `blocked_by: []`. Closure `{315}`. No path to #310.
- **FEAT-019 (#321)** — `blocked_by: [336]` → #336 → #315. Closure `{336, 315}`. No path to #310.
- **FEAT-037 (#327)** — `blocked_by: [336]` → #336 → #315. Closure `{336, 315}`. No path to #310.
- **FEAT-020 (#320)** — `blocked_by: [339]` → #339 `blocked_by: []`. Closure `{339}`. No path to #310.
- **FEAT-022 (#342)** — `blocked_by: [320]` → #320 → #339. Closure `{320, 339}`. No path to #310.
- **FEAT-018 (#358)** — `blocked_by: [315, 336]` → #336 → #315. Closure `{315, 336}`. No path to #310.
- **FEAT-023 (#359)** — `blocked_by: [317, 358]` → FEAT-007 (#317) `blocked_by: [353, 354]` → FEAT-005 (#353) `[]`, FEAT-006 (#354) `[]`; #358 → {#315, #336}. Closure `{317, 353, 354, 358, 315, 336}`. No path to #310.

**Union of all ten closures: `{315, 317, 320, 336, 339, 353, 354, 358}`. It contains no capstone number (#295-#313) and does not contain #310.**

**The cross-tier arm, checked directly rather than assumed.** Every `tier:feature` issue in the tracker was read and its `blocked_by` inspected: **no filed feature declares a `blocked_by` entry naming any capstone**. There is no feature→capstone ordering arc anywhere for a cycle to close through, and `blocks:` stays empty because nothing declares `blocked_by: [310]`. **Result: no cycle. The ordering graph remains a DAG.**

## 3. A real scheduling finding: FEAT-023 sits behind a CI feature this roster never named

**FEAT-023 (#359) is `blocked_by [317, 358]`**, and **#317 is FEAT-007** — CI long-run lanes, timeouts and cross-platform parity — which is **not** in this capstone's required set. #317 is itself `blocked_by [353, 354]` (FEAT-005, FEAT-006). So the differential oracle of §1 step 2, and AC-1 and AC-6 with it, are ordered behind three features this plan never mentioned. §3 risk 5's "make the legs required rather than skippable" now has an owner outside this set.

**Recommended disposition, argued rather than assumed:** accept the ordering and re-sequence; do **not** add #317 to `requires_features`. §1 states no observation that FEAT-007 alone owns, so adding it would fail the minimality test rule E imposes on every row. Recorded as §3 risk 9, as arm (ii) of Open Question 8, in AC-6's text, and as a Completion Criteria line. #317, #353 and #354 are added to `related` (reference-only, no arrow) — **not** to `blocked_by`, because that field mirrors a feature-side edge naming this capstone and none of them declares one.

## 4. Eight graph edges withdrawn, three added — including one that was pointing at the wrong feature

Restricted to this set, the filed features declare **eight** intra-set edges. The graph as filed drew **thirteen**. Only five coincide.

- **Kept:** #315 → #358, #336 → #358, #336 → #321, #358 → #359, #320 → #342.
- **Added (declared by the features, absent from the filed graph):** **#315 → #336** (`#315 blocks [.., 336, ..]` / `#336 blocked_by [315]`), **#336 → #327** (`#336 blocks [321, 327, ..]` / `#327 blocked_by [336]`), **#339 → #320** (`#339 blocks [320, ..]` / `#320 blocked_by [339]`).
- **Withdrawn (neither endpoint declares them):** **#336 → #359**, **#358 → #321**, **#358 → #320**, **#358 → #342**, **#321 → #320**, **#339 → #359**, **#322 → #359**, **#327 → #359**.

**One of those is not a near-miss — it named the wrong feature.** The filed graph drew `F019 --> F020`, i.e. FEAT-019 before FEAT-020. But #320 (FEAT-020) is `blocked_by [339]`, and **#339 is FEAT-021**, not FEAT-019. FEAT-019 is #321. The two adjacent FEAT numbers map to non-adjacent issue numbers in opposite order, and the filing-time edge took the wrong member of the pair. The corrected edge is **FEAT-021 → FEAT-020**, which is also more sensible on the merits: an importer that must realize tri-state cells needs the third port direction to exist first. This is precisely the transposed-pair hazard, caught by checking titles rather than trusting adjacency.

Withdrawn rather than mirrored, per rule A — the same test this issue already applied at filing when it removed three unmirrored cross-capstone edges (CAP15 → CAP07, F004 → CAP05, F020 → CAP08). **The substance is preserved as Open Question 8**, which flags **#336 → #359 as the one most likely to be genuinely real** (§3 risk 1 says in terms that the comparator keys on names the partition IR produces — a landing-order claim), reads #339/#322/#327 → #359 as joint-invariant obligations rather than sequencing (§3 risk 6), and leaves the #358 → {#321, #320, #342} trio genuinely open. Whichever way it resolves, each edge is written onto **both** endpoints in one REPLAN before it is redrawn here.

## 5. Mermaid regenerated from the corrected machine block

Nodes = this capstone + the ten issues in `requires_features`, nothing else. Edges = the eight declared intra-set ordering edges + ten composition edges. Checked by construction: same set in the graph, the machine block and the §2 roster; **no node the machine block does not hold**; **no arrow at an issue carried only in `related`** — #59, #298, #302, #304, #307, #317, #353, #354 and the rest appear nowhere in the graph; **no direct capstone-to-capstone ordering edge**; **no beneficial feature drawn with an arrowhead** (FEAT-024 #360, FEAT-016 #340, FEAT-044 #328 are named in §2 and drawn nowhere).

## 6. Filing-pass sentences retired; two obligations explicitly NOT discharged

Removed or rewritten as now-false: the §2 preamble "None of these is filed yet; the roster is `planned_features` above and each row resolves to a number by REPLAN when filed"; every "planned — absent at `2d0ca9d`" status, now "filed as #NNN; scope absent at `2d0ca9d`"; the ordering note's "None of the ten is filed, so no feature-side `blocked_by` naming this capstone exists"; §5's "A required feature is filed" clause, replaced by a clause governing **additions** to a now-closed, fully-numbered set. Open Question 4 said "Blocks filing FEAT-023" — it is filed as #359, so it now blocks that feature's **execution**. Open Question 1's mirror obligation to #59 is restated with the numbers it now has: #61 → #320, #62 → #342.

**Not discharged, and said plainly:**

1. **The marginal band of 12-22 mw is still unverified.** It was conditioned on "treat 12-22 as unverified until at least FEAT-023 and FEAT-020 are filed with that split priced". All content fully absorbed into body §2 (Required Feature Set & Sufficiency), machine block (requires_features, blocked_by with inline comments), mermaid graph, and §3. 5161369861.body:
REPLAN: `planned_features` resolved to filed issues; `requires_features` populated; ordering re-derived from the filed feature machine blocks; mermaid graph regenerated; five filing-pass edges withdrawn.

**Trigger.** This capstone was filed when no feature existed, so it carried `requires_features: []` and its required set as six one-line scopes in `planned_features`. All 57 features are now filed as #314-#370. Rule E makes a roster change a re-plan, so this is recorded here rather than made as a quiet edit.

## 1. Resolution — every scope to a filed number

Read through `search_issues` with `body` among the requested fields (the lossless path; `issue_read` deletes tag-shaped runs and a rewrite driven off it would bake the artifact into storage). **Every number below was checked against the issue TITLE, not against numeric order** — the feature numbering is not monotonic in FEAT order.

| `planned_features` scope | Resolves to | Title check |
|---|---|---|
| FEAT-025 — Logisim-Evolution `.circ` importer and migration report | **#323** | *"FEAT-025: a course's existing Logisim-Evolution material opens in JLS with its structure intact and every loss named, located and explained"* |
| FEAT-002 — fail-loud loader and attribute dispatch | **#314** | *"FEAT-002: a saved attribute no element declares becomes a named diagnostic instead of vanishing at load"* |
| FEAT-053 (RESIDUAL) — test-vector front end and autograding at scale | **#369** | *"FEAT-053: 'this design was exercised' becomes 'this design passed or failed, on this vector, on this signal' …"* |
| FEAT-001 (RESIDUAL) — registry-keyed table totality discipline | **#315** | *"FEAT-001 (RESIDUAL): a thirty-sixth element type cannot ship until every registry-keyed table has a row for it"* |
| FEAT-016 — subcircuit type identity, VLNV and the circuit-library format | **#340** | *"FEAT-016: a subcircuit definition has an identity that means something outside the file it lives in, and a library of circuits is a distributable artifact with provenance"* |
| FEAT-022 (RESIDUAL) — readability rubric and coordinate preservation | **#342** | *"FEAT-022 (RESIDUAL): every cell the mapper realizes places and routes, hierarchy instances arrive as instances, and the readability rubric is reported at core scale"* |

**Six scopes in, six numbers out. `planned_features` is now `[]`. Nothing was dropped and nothing failed to resolve.**

**Independent confirmation, not asserted from this end.** Each of the six declares this capstone in its own machine block: #314 `serves_capstones: [296, 299, 304, 311]`; #315 `[296, 297, 298, 307, 309, 310, 311]`; #323 `[311]`; #340 `[300, 304, 311]`; #342 `[304, 310, 311]`; #369 `[300, 306, 311]`. Filtering all 57 filed features for `311` in `serves_capstones` returns exactly `{314, 315, 323, 340, 342, 369}` — the same six, derived from the other end without reference to this issue's roster. The composition edge is therefore mirrored on both ends already, with no feature-side edit owed.

The filing-pass sentence *"None of these is filed yet; the roster is `planned_features` above, and each row resolves to a number by REPLAN when filed"* is now false and has been removed from §2.

## 2. The DAG walk, per feature, before adding it

Walked outward along `blocked_by` to fixpoint, on each feature's **filed** machine block. The walk recorded at filing was against scopes nobody had written down; this one is against declared edges.

| Feature | `blocked_by` as filed | Transitive prerequisite closure | #311 reached? |
|---|---|---|---|
| FEAT-001 #315 | `[]` | ∅ | no |
| FEAT-002 #314 | `[315]` | {#315} | no |
| FEAT-016 #340 | `[319]` | {#319 FEAT-013, #334 FEAT-003, #315 FEAT-001} | no |
| FEAT-022 #342 | `[320]` | {#320 FEAT-020, #339 FEAT-021} | no |
| FEAT-025 #323 | `[314, 349]` | {#314 FEAT-002, #349 FEAT-040, #315 FEAT-001} | no |
| FEAT-053 #369 | `[316, 321, 347]` | {#316, #321, #347, #315, #317, #319, #325, #334, #335, #336, #337, #343, #353, #354} — 14 | no |

**No path from any of the six returns to #311.** No cycle.

**The cross-tier check the template asks for, done at corpus scale rather than locally.** A cycle here would need a feature to be `blocked_by` a capstone. Scanning the `blocked_by` list of all 57 filed features for any number in 295-313 returns **zero hits** — no feature in the corpus is blocked by any capstone. So `blocks: []` on this issue is empty *on evidence*, not for want of anything being filed, and the cross-tier back-edge that makes cycles possible does not exist anywhere yet. It can appear later, which is why §5 now requires the walk to be redone on every REPLAN.

## 3. Five edges drawn at filing are withdrawn, and one is added

The filing graph asserted six ordering edges among scopes. Now that the features are filed, each edge has an authority — the feature's own machine block (rule A) — and five of the six are not recorded there. An edge the feature side does not carry is unmirrored, which is the silent lapse the tier model names, so they are withdrawn rather than left drawn.

| Edge drawn at filing | Authority now | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `F002 --> F025` | #323 `blocked_by: [314, 349]`; #314 `blocks: [323]` | **kept** — recorded on both ends |
| `F001 --> F025` | #323 `blocked_by: [314, 349]` — 315 absent | **withdrawn.** The ordering survives transitively as F001 → F002 → F025; nothing is lost |
| `F016 --> F025` | #323 `blocked_by: [314, 349]` — 340 absent | **withdrawn.** FEAT-016 is required for the *outcome* (a migrated library must stay a library) but does not gate the reader. Required ≠ prerequisite |
| `F001 --> F016` | #340 `blocked_by: [319]` | **withdrawn and replaced.** FEAT-016 waits on FEAT-013 #319, not on FEAT-001 |
| `F025 --> F022` | #342 `blocked_by: [320]` | **withdrawn.** The rubric work is gated by the Yosys import path #320, not by the `.circ` reader. "Needs a corpus to run against" is a convenience, not an ordering dependency — and #342 can run its rubric against the netlist-import corpus that already exists |
| `F025 --> F053` | #369 `blocked_by: [316, 321, 347]` | **withdrawn**, same reason |

Added, all read off a required feature's own `blocked_by`: `F040 --> F025`, `F013 --> F016`, `F020 --> F022`, `F008 --> F053`, `F019 --> F053`, `F034 --> F053`.

**Consequence for `blocked_by` on this issue.** Six features outside the required set gate features inside it, so each must land before this capstone can close: **#316 FEAT-008, #319 FEAT-013, #320 FEAT-020, #321 FEAT-019, #347 FEAT-034, #349 FEAT-040.** `blocked_by` was `[]` and is now those six. This is ordering, not composition — the required set stays at six (rule E) and the sufficiency argument is unchanged.

**Three of those six (#316, #319, #349) are named as *beneficial* in §2, and that is not a contradiction.** Beneficial-versus-required is a grade on the *sufficiency argument*: does this feature own an observation in §1? None of the three does. `blocked_by` is a statement of *order*: must it land first? Each does. Keeping them in separate keys is precisely what stops the required set from quietly growing from six to nine on the strength of a scheduling fact.

## 4. Graph regenerated, agreement by construction

Rebuilt from the machine block under a stated construction rule rather than edited: every node is an issue the machine block holds (six `requires_features`, six `blocked_by`, this capstone — nothing else); every composition edge runs required-feature → CAP16 and there are exactly six; every ordering edge is read off a required feature's own machine block; no arrow touches an issue carried only in `related`; no beneficial feature has an arrowhead at CAP16 (F008, F013, F040 appear only as ordering prerequisites of required features and point at those, never at the capstone); no capstone-to-capstone edge. §2's roster now carries the filed number on every row.

## 5. Required-versus-beneficial: checked, and this capstone has no disagreement

The link pass found the capstone issues and the corpus documents disagreeing in three places elsewhere. Checked here explicitly at `2d0ca9d`, because the absence of a disagreement is only worth stating if it was looked for:

- `docs/plan/capstones/CAP-16-logisim-evolution-migration-parity.md:62-67` grades FEAT-025, FEAT-002, FEAT-022, FEAT-053, FEAT-001, FEAT-016 **required** — the same six this issue requires.
- `:68-73` grades FEAT-013, FEAT-003, FEAT-040, FEAT-011, FEAT-008, FEAT-050 **beneficial** — the same six this issue calls beneficial.
- Each required feature's own document agrees from its side: `FEAT-001 …:28`, `FEAT-002 …:23`, `FEAT-016 …:24`, `FEAT-022 …:21`, `FEAT-025 …:19`, `FEAT-053 …:22`, each `| CAP-16 | required |`.

Twelve gradings, three sources, no conflict. **Nothing to resolve and nothing papered over.**

## 6. What did not change, and why

No cost band moved. Resolving scopes to numbers attaches issue numbers to rows that already existed; the sums are indifferent to it, and adjusting a band to fit a bookkeeping change would be exactly the thing the Cost section forbids. The standalone band stays **30-50 mw** and the marginal band stays **12-18 mw** (higher FEAT-025 estimate, per this issue's own standing instruction until the two-day measurement runs).

One Cost claim did get *stronger* without moving: the marginal band rests on FEAT-025 being the only row nothing else funds. That was a corpus assertion at filing; it is now checkable from the filed issues, and it holds — #323 declares `serves_capstones: [311]`, alone among the six, while the other five each name three to seven capstones.

`related` gained the six beneficial features by number (#316, #319, #330, #334, #349, #355), which §2 already promised and could not deliver before they were filed. `related` is reference-only and never blocking; no arrow was added for any of them.

## 7. Obligations this REPLAN creates

- A new Completion Criteria line: every `blocked_by` entry closed as landed, or the ordering edge withdrawn by a REPLAN that re-reads the required feature's own `blocked_by` and shows the prerequisite gone from it.
- A new §5 trigger: if a required feature's `blocked_by` changes, this capstone's `blocked_by` is re-derived from the six features' machine blocks in the same REPLAN and the graph regenerated. The ordering list here is a projection of theirs, not an independent list, and it will drift the moment that is forgotten.
- The five withdrawn edges are *withdrawn, not refuted*. If any is genuinely wanted — the most defensible is a corpus-availability argument for `F025 --> F053` — the route is to record it on **both** issues in one REPLAN, not to redraw it here.

5161405953.body:
REPLAN: eleven `planned_features` scopes resolved to filed issues; `requires_features` populated; ordering re-derived from the filed machine blocks; graph regenerated; five edges withdrawn and two added; the FEAT-005 required-versus-beneficial disagreement DECIDED.

**Trigger.** Filed with `requires_features: []` and the required set as eleven one-line scopes, because no feature existed. All 57 are now filed as #314-#370. Rule E makes a roster change a re-plan.

## 1. Resolution — eleven scopes, eleven numbers

Read through `search_issues` with `body` requested (the lossless path). **Every number checked against the issue TITLE**, never inferred from ordering — FEAT-037 is #327 while FEAT-038 is #326, and FEAT-043 is #329 while FEAT-044 is #328, so ordinal inference produces wrong edges in this roster.

| Scope | Number | Title check (abbreviated) |
|---|---|---|
| FEAT-005 (FIRST) quadratic and materializing I/O paths | **#353** | *"FEAT-005: a long batch run costs linear time and bounded memory — the stimulus parse, the load-time net walk and the waveform dump stop being superlinear"* |
| FEAT-055 partitioned model and streaming elaboration | **#332** | *"FEAT-055: a circuit exists as parts that load independently …"* |
| FEAT-056 distributed transport and barrier protocol | **#333** | *"FEAT-056: partitions on separate hosts exchange boundary events, and the result is byte-identical to running the design whole"* |
| FEAT-057 campaign execution and artifact aggregation | **#350** | *"FEAT-057: many independent runs dispatch across cores or hosts and aggregate into one report …"* |
| FEAT-054 flat, compact element representation | **#370** | *"FEAT-054: a circuit's runtime state lives in flat primitive arrays indexed by element …"* |
| FEAT-004 net-partition IR with stable net naming | **#336** | *"FEAT-004: exactly one net partition in JLS, and a synthesized net name that survives an unrelated edit"* |
| FEAT-014 (RESIDUAL) stable addressing and per-view geometry | **#318** | *"FEAT-014 (RESIDUAL): nets, groups and nested instances get names that survive sharing, and geometry becomes one record per view"* |
| FEAT-006 simulation capacity and long-run ergonomics | **#354** | *"FEAT-006: an hours-long batch run has no unannounced ceiling …"* |
| FEAT-030 engine constant factors | **#362** | *"FEAT-030: every retired event costs measurably less and the entire golden corpus stays byte-identical …"* |
| FEAT-009 (RESIDUAL) measurement gate and calibration fixture | **#335** | *"FEAT-009: every wall-clock claim in the plan divides by a measured constant, taken on a tracked fixture, under a ratchet …"* |
| FEAT-035 checkpoint and simulation-state serialization | **#363** | *"FEAT-035: a running simulation can be written to disk and resumed as the byte-identical continuation …"* |

**`planned_features` is now `[]`. Nothing dropped, nothing unresolved.**

**Confirmed from the other end.** Filtering all 57 filed features for `312` in `serves_capstones` returns exactly `{318, 332, 333, 335, 336, 350, 353, 354, 362, 363, 370}` — the same eleven, derived without reference to this issue. The composition edge is already mirrored on both ends; no feature-side edit is owed.

The filing-pass sentence *"None of these is filed as a GitHub issue yet …"* is now false and has been removed from §2.

## 2. The DAG walk, per feature, before adding it

Walked `blocked_by` outward to fixpoint on each feature's **filed** machine block.

| Feature | `blocked_by` as filed | Closure size | #312 reached? |
|---|---|---|---|
| FEAT-005 #353 | `[]` | 0 | no |
| FEAT-004 #336 | `[315]` | 1 | no |
| FEAT-006 #354 | `[353]` | 1 | no |
| FEAT-009 #335 | `[353]` | 1 | no |
| FEAT-030 #362 | `[335]` | 2 | no |
| FEAT-035 #363 | `[319]` | 3 | no |
| FEAT-014 #318 | `[319, 337]` | 4 | no |
| FEAT-054 #370 | `[322, 335, 362]` | 4 | no |
| FEAT-057 #350 | `[354, 363]` | 6 | no |
| FEAT-055 #332 | `[319, 336, 353, 370]` | 9 | no |
| FEAT-056 #333 | `[318, 332, 348, 363]` | 14 | no |

**#312 appears in none of the eleven closures.** No cycle.

**Cross-tier check at corpus scale.** A cycle here requires a feature `blocked_by` a capstone — the mechanism the template names. Scanning `blocked_by` across all 57 filed features for any number in 295-313 returns **zero hits**. No feature in this corpus is blocked by any capstone, so `blocks: []` is empty on evidence, not for want of filing.

**A side result worth recording:** #353 is the only required row with `blocked_by: []`, and #354, #335, #332 name it directly. "FEAT-005 first" is now a property of the filed edges, not only of the wall measurement that motivated it.

## 3. Five edges withdrawn, two added

The filing graph asserted seventeen ordering edges among scopes. Each now has an authority — the feature's own machine block (rule A). Five are not recorded there and are withdrawn rather than left drawn unmirrored.

| Withdrawn | Authority | Why it is safe to drop |
|---|---|---|
| `F005 --> F054` | #370 `blocked_by: [322, 335, 362]` | survives transitively: F005 → F009 → F054 |
| `F005 --> F057` | #350 `blocked_by: [354, 363]` | survives transitively: F005 → F006 → F057 |
| `F009 --> F056` | #333 `blocked_by: [318, 332, 348, 363]` | survives transitively: F009 → F054 → F055 → F056 |
| `F014 --> F055` | #332 `blocked_by: [319, 336, 353, 370]` | **substantive correction.** FEAT-014 gates FEAT-056 (#333 `blocked_by` names 318), not FEAT-055. Addressing is needed to *compare* across a boundary, not to *write* the partition files. The filing graph put it one node too early |
| `F055 --> F035` | #363 `blocked_by: [319]` | **substantive correction.** Checkpointing is a single-host capability first; it does not wait on partitioning. This one was inverted at filing — #333 `blocked_by` names 363, so F035 precedes F056, and F055 → F035 → F056 is the real chain rather than F055 → F035 alone |

Added, both recorded on the feature side: `F005 --> F009` (#335 `blocked_by: [353]`) and `F014 --> F056` (#333 `blocked_by` names 318).

**Consequence for `blocked_by` on this issue.** Five features outside the required set gate features inside it, so each must land before this capstone can close: **#315 FEAT-001, #319 FEAT-013, #322 FEAT-026, #337 FEAT-015, #348 FEAT-051.** `blocked_by` was `[]` and is now those five. Ordering, not composition — the required set stays at eleven and the sufficiency argument is untouched.

**#348 is the finding.** §3 risk 4 argued in prose that FEAT-056 must reuse `src/jls/collab/net/Transport.java` rather than stand up a second networking stack. #333's filed `blocked_by: [318, 332, 348, 363]` names #348 FEAT-051 — the shared-session feature that owns that transport. The risk is now a hard ordering edge, not advice, and it was invisible while the features were unfiled. §3 risk 4 and Open Question 4 both record it.

## 4. The FEAT-005 disagreement — decided, not papered over

The link pass flagged that `docs/plan/features/FEAT-005-quadratic-and-materializing-io-paths.md:26` grades CAP-17 `beneficial` while this issue and `docs/plan/capstones/CAP-17-distributed-execution.md:65` make it required and first. **Decided here: FEAT-005 is REQUIRED, and first. The feature document is the wrong one.**

Three sources, one dissenter:

1. `FEAT-005-quadratic-and-materializing-io-paths.md:26` → `| CAP-17 | beneficial |`
2. `CAP-17-distributed-execution.md:65` → *"**PROMOTED TO REQUIRED AND TO FIRST** on measurement … Nothing in this capstone is reachable until it lands"*, graded `required`
3. **the filed issue #353 itself** → `serves_capstones: [296, 301, 295, 300, 306, 312]`, and its own mermaid draws `F5 --> C312["#312 CAP-17"]`

**The tie-break is not two-against-one.** It is that (1) records a judgement made *before* the wall ordering was measured, while (2) and (3) record it *after*, and the measurement is what moved it. The substance: `Circuit.finishLoad`'s O(W²) wire-end partition stops any `.jls`-borne design at ~165,000 runtime elements, and every other required feature here reads a design that must exist first. A prerequisite without which nothing else is reachable is not "beneficial" under any reading. Independently, the live artifact on the feature side — #353's machine block — already carries the composition edge to this capstone, so the two live artifacts agree and only a document dissents.

**Repair owed:** `docs/plan/features/FEAT-005-quadratic-and-materializing-io-paths.md:26` from `beneficial` to `required`. That file is outside this issue's ownership, so it is carried as an obligation in Open Question 8 and in the Completion Criteria rather than assumed done. Open Question 8 is downgraded from "which is right" to "the file edit is outstanding".

## 5. Graph regenerated; agreement by construction

Rebuilt from the machine block under a stated rule: every node is an issue the machine block holds (eleven `requires_features`, five `blocked_by`, this capstone — nothing else); eleven composition edges, one per required feature; every ordering edge read off a required feature's own machine block, hence pre-mirrored; no arrow at an issue carried only in `related`; no arrowhead at CAP17 from a beneficial feature (#317 and #325 appear nowhere in the graph); no capstone-to-capstone edge. §2's roster carries the filed number on every row.

## 6. What did not change

**No cost band moved, and none was adjusted to fit.** Required sum stays **83-137 mw**, standalone **83-137**, marginal **38-62**, demo slice **6-8** (19-30 unshared). Resolving scopes to numbers attaches numbers to existing rows; the sums are indifferent.

Three Cost claims got *stronger without moving*, because the filed issues now confirm what the corpus asserted:

- Marginal 38-62 rests on FEAT-054/055/056/057 being funded by no other capstone. #370, #332, #333 and #350 each declare `serves_capstones: [312]` — this capstone and nothing else. Confirmed from the feature side.
- The demo slice's 19-30 mw unshared figure rests on FEAT-057 having exactly two prerequisites, FEAT-006 and FEAT-035. #350's filed `blocked_by: [354, 363]` names exactly those two and no third.
- "FEAT-005 is the cheapest useful thing and can start now" rests on nothing preceding it. #353's `blocked_by: []` confirms it.

Two open questions moved from "blocks filing" to "blocks starting", since the features they gate are now filed (OQ 2, 3, 4). **Open Question 6 is worse than it was:** the recommended default was to re-home the spatial-index rebuild into FEAT-005's scope *at filing time*. #353 is filed and its `planned_tasks` name TASK-0009, TASK-0010 and TASK-0008 — none of them the spatial index. The re-homing did not happen. It now blocks #353 *closing*, and §3 risk 6 and the Completion Criteria both say so.

## 7. Obligations created

- Every `blocked_by` entry (#315, #319, #322, #337, #348) closed as landed, or its edge withdrawn by a REPLAN that re-reads the required feature's own `blocked_by`.
- The `blocked_by` list re-derived from the eleven features' machine blocks at close — it is a projection of theirs, not an independent list, and drifts silently otherwise.
- A new §5 trigger firing whenever a required feature's own `blocked_by` changes.
- The FEAT-005 document correction, tracked but not performed here.
- The five withdrawn edges are *withdrawn, not refuted*. If any is wanted, record it on both issues in one REPLAN rather than redrawing it here.

5161610951.body:
ADJUDICATED: the five edges drawn at filing and removed on 2026-08-03. **All five removals are confirmed. Nothing is added to a feature's machine block and nothing is redrawn here.**

**Method.** Every mermaid ordering edge in all nineteen capstones (#295–#313) was checked against the two endpoint features' own filed `blocked_by`/`blocks`, both directions: **0 graph-asserted edges the features do not hold, 0 feature-held edges a graph omits**, 0 asymmetries across the 57 machine blocks. Each feature's filed `blocked_by` was then diffed against its own corpus `## Prerequisite features` table under `docs/plan/features/`: they agree on every row of all 57 features except FEAT-031 (#325), whose corpus row itself instructs the omission.

| Removed edge | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **#353 → #370** (FEAT-005 → FEAT-054) | confirmed — **already ordered** | Filed tier carries **#353 → #335 → #370**, and the routing is the substantive point rather than a technicality: FEAT-054's corpus prerequisites are FEAT-009, FEAT-026 and FEAT-030, so a footprint claim reaches the linear-I/O work *through* the measurement gate. A per-element footprint reduction asserted without a measured constant is arithmetic on a guess. |
| **#353 → #350** (FEAT-005 → FEAT-057) | confirmed — **already ordered** | Filed tier carries **#353 → #354 → #350**. FEAT-057's corpus prerequisites are FEAT-006 and FEAT-035; a dispatcher needs runs that can be suspended and resumed, which is FEAT-006's scope, and FEAT-006 is where the linear-parse dependency is declared. |
| **#335 → #333** (FEAT-009 → FEAT-056) | confirmed — **already ordered** | Filed tier carries **#335 → #370 → #332 → #333**, the four-hop path the note names. FEAT-056's corpus prerequisites are FEAT-055, FEAT-051, FEAT-035 and FEAT-014 — the partition, the transport, the checkpoint and the addressing — none of which is a measurement. |
| **#318 → #332** (FEAT-014 → FEAT-055) | confirmed | The note's distinction is the right one and it holds on the merits: FEAT-055's corpus prerequisites are FEAT-054, FEAT-004, FEAT-013 and FEAT-005 — writing partition files needs a flat representation, one net partition, section framing and linear I/O. Instance-path addressing is what lets a boundary event be **compared** across hosts, which is FEAT-056's problem and is declared there (`#333 blocked_by [318, …]`). |
| **#332 → #363** (FEAT-055 → FEAT-035) | confirmed | Direction of dependency runs the other way in the corpus: FEAT-035's prerequisite is FEAT-013 alone, and FEAT-056 lists FEAT-035 as *its* prerequisite. Checkpointing is a single-host capability first; a partitioned checkpoint is the later increment. |

The two edges the same re-derivation added — `#353 → #335` and `#318 → #333` — are both correct against the corpus tables (FEAT-009 ← FEAT-005; FEAT-056 ← FEAT-014) and are left as drawn.

No cost band, acceptance criterion or roster row was changed by this comment.

| §2 requirement | Issue | Status |

| FEAT-009 (RESIDUAL) measurement gate + calibration fixture | #335 | **EXISTING** — open, title matches |

Ordering prerequisites in `blocked_by` — #315, #319, #322, #337, #348 — all open, titles match. Beneficial (outside required set, correctly not in `requires_features`): #317, #325 — both open. **No requires-row, blocked_by entry, or related beneficial points at a closed issue.** Nothing filed: no REQUIRED row lacks an issue.

### Split recommendation (per #508)

#508 defers CAP-17 with: **split — campaign axis → CAP-06 (#300) / CAP-09 (#306); fund FEAT-005 (#353) now.** Noting, not executing:

- FEAT-057 #350 currently declares `serves_capstones: [312]` **only**, with #300/#306 as beneficial in `related`. Executing the split means #350 re-homes to #300/#306 — its own §7 re-planning clause already provides for exactly this ("if #312 descoped … re-homed to whichever of them adopts it"), and this issue's Open Question 7 provides the composition route.
- That REPLAN would remove FEAT-057 from `requires_features` here (ten rows remain on the capacity axis), move AC-2 with it, and re-derive the marginal band (38-62 mw currently includes FEAT-057's 6-8).

1. `docs/plan/features/FEAT-005-quadratic-and-materializing-io-paths.md:26` still says `beneficial` against three live artifacts saying required-and-first. Already tracked (Open Question 8, Completion Criteria); still outstanding.
2. The body's corpus counts ("all 57 filed features", "checked against all 57") are stale: FEAT-058 #486, FEAT-059 #490, FEAT-060 #487 and FEAT-C05-1 #523 now exist. The eleven-row roster is unaffected, but the next REPLAN's `blocks: []` / `serves_capstones` corpus scans must run over the enlarged set.
3. Spatial-index rebuild (Open Question 6) remains unowned — #353's `planned_tasks` still omit it. Task-tier scope; not filed in a verify-only run under #508's planning ratchet, but it must not ride unowned into FEAT-055.
4. #508 hygiene flags #348/#433 as a near-pair. #348 (FEAT-051) carries the ordering edge into #333 (FEAT-056's transport reuse, §3 risk 4); #433 is TASK-0108, tier:task. Whatever resolves that pair must preserve the feature-side edge.
