5161460457.body:
REPLAN: five of eight `planned_features` scopes resolved to filed issues; three CANNOT resolve and are recorded as a gap, not dropped; ordering re-derived from the filed machine blocks; graph regenerated; the cumulative cost band moved because `blocked_by` stopped being empty. **Trigger.** Filed with `requires_features: []` and the required set as eight one-line scopes, because no feature existed. All 57 features are now filed as #314-#370. Rule E makes a roster change a re-plan. ## 1. Resolution — five of eight Read through `search_issues` with `body` requested (the lossless path; `issue_read` deletes tag-shaped runs, and this body carries `
`, `` generics and XML-shaped text, so a rewrite driven off it would bake the artifact into storage). Every number checked against the issue TITLE. | Scope | Resolves to | Title check (abbreviated) | |---|---|---| | FEAT-047 physical time base and real-time scalar | **#367** | *"FEAT-047: a circuit can declare what one tick means in physical time, once, and everything that reports time reports it in that unit …"* | | FEAT-042 KiCad/gEDA emitters + manufacturability gate | **#366** | *"FEAT-042: a drawn circuit leaves JLS as a schematic and netlist a real PCB tool opens without hand editing …"* | | FEAT-004 net-partition IR + stable net naming | **#336** | *"FEAT-004: exactly one net partition in JLS, and a synthesized net name that survives an unrelated edit"* | | FEAT-013 per-section versioning, must-understand | **#319** | *"FEAT-013: a saved file stops being accepted or refused as one unit — unknown optional sections are skipped and preserved …"* | | FEAT-014 (RESIDUAL) stable addressing + per-view geometry | **#318** | *"FEAT-014 (RESIDUAL): nets, groups and nested instances get names that survive sharing, and geometry becomes one record per view"* | | **FEAT-058** edge rate, length, electrical-length lint | **NO RESOLUTION** | see §2 below | | **FEAT-060** SI constraint authorship + PCB export | **NO RESOLUTION** | see §2 below | | **FEAT-059** closed-form T-line + reflection lab | **NO RESOLUTION** | see §2 below | **Confirmed from the other end.** Filtering all 57 filed features for `313` in `serves_capstones` returns exactly `{318, 319, 336, 366, 367}` — the same five, derived without reference to this issue. The composition edge is mirrored on both ends for those five; no feature-side edit is owed. ## 2. THE THREE THAT DO NOT RESOLVE — stated explicitly, not silently dropped **FEAT-058, FEAT-059 and FEAT-060 sit outside the closed 57-feature roster. They have no filed issue, no feature document and no REGISTRY row. They remain in `planned_features` with the reason attached, and a new Open Question 8 states what must happen.** No number was invented for any of them. Measured at `2d0ca9d`, not assumed: ``` $ git ls-tree --name-only 2d0ca9d docs/plan/features/ | wc -l 57 $ git ls-tree --name-only 2d0ca9d docs/plan/features/ | sed 's/.*FEAT-\([0-9]*\).*/\1/' | sort -n | tail -1 057 $ git ls-tree --name-only 2d0ca9d docs/plan/features/ | grep -cE "FEAT-0(58|59|60|61)" 0 $ git show 2d0ca9d:docs/plan/REGISTRY.md | grep -cE "FEAT-0(58|59|60|61)" 0 ``` **Where they do exist:** only as rows inside `docs/plan/capstones/CAP-18-net-that-stopped-being-a-wire.md` — *this capstone's own planning document*, i.e. the thing that consumes them — at `:99-101` and `:333-335`, minted by decision **D-H16**. They have no specification independent of their consumer. That document's own registry-delta line claims *"61 features (FEAT-001..FEAT-061)"*; **the corpus does not support the count**: 57 documents exist, so four of the claimed features were never written. That discrepancy is now a Completion Criteria item. **Are they genuinely required?** Yes, all three, and the §2 minimality test is the reason — not that a document listed them: - **FEAT-058** owns §1 step 1 in its entirety and supplies the two declared attributes steps 2-5 all consume. Without it there is no way to say a net has a length or a driver has an edge rate, and nothing else here is assessable. - **FEAT-059** owns §1 steps 2-4 — the reflection, the ring, the termination that fixes them, the edge-rate collapse. Without it step 1's verdict has no demonstration. - **FEAT-060** owns §1 step 5, the only claim in this capstone with an external adjudicator. **Nothing in the filed 57 substitutes.** The closest candidates are FEAT-046 #351 (analog solver) and FEAT-049 #331 (analog device models); §2 already grades both beneficial with the reason — they upgrade a line the closed form delivers exactly, at 28-41.5 mw instead of 2-3.5, which is Open Question 2's recorded decision. **The scopes are neither re-homeable into a filed feature nor descopable without re-quoting §1.** **What must happen** (Open Question 8, and it BLOCKS CLOSING): file three feature issues against the feature template, add three feature documents and three REGISTRY rows so the specification stops living inside its consumer; move them to `requires_features` by REPLAN and record their ordering edges on both ends; reconcile the "61 features" count. It does **not** block the demo slice from being scoped — the demo slice *is* FEAT-058, and filing it is the first step of doing it. ## 3. The DAG walk, per row, before adding it For the five filed rows the walk is against `blocked_by` as declared, to fixpoint. For the three unfiled scopes there is no machine block, so their edges stay this capstone's assertions and the walk runs against those. | Row | `blocked_by` | Closure | #313 reached? | |---|---|---|---| | FEAT-047 #367 | `[]` filed | ∅ | no | | FEAT-004 #336 | `[315]` filed | {#315} | no | | FEAT-013 #319 | `[334]` filed | {#334, #315} | no | | FEAT-014 #318 | `[319, 337]` filed | {#319, #337, #334, #315} | no | | FEAT-042 #366 | `[336, 349, 365]` filed | {#336, #349, #365, #315} | no | | FEAT-058 | asserted: {#367, #336, #319} | + {#315, #334} | no | | FEAT-060 | asserted: {F058, #336, #366, #318, #319} | + {#337, #349, #365} | no | | FEAT-059 | asserted: {F060, #367} | all of the above | no | **#313 appears in no closure, filed or asserted.** No cycle. **Cross-tier check at corpus scale.** Scanning `blocked_by` across all 57 filed features for any number in 295-313 returns **zero hits** — no feature in the corpus is blocked by any capstone. `blocks: []` is therefore empty on evidence. **This is the capstone where that could most plausibly change:** FEAT-058/059/060 are exactly the kind of feature that might legitimately be `blocked_by` CAP-04 #297 or CAP-05 #298, so the REPLAN that files each of them must redo this walk rather than copy it. ## 4. Graph regenerated, with dashed edges marking what cannot be mirrored Rebuilt under a stated construction rule: every node is something the machine block holds (five `requires_features`, three `planned_features`, five `blocked_by`, this capstone); eight composition edges into CAP18, exactly the eight-row required set; every edge **between filed issues** read off a required feature's own machine block, hence pre-mirrored; no arrow at a `related`-only issue; no beneficial feature with an arrowhead at CAP18 (F041 #365 appears only as an ordering prerequisite of F042 and points at F042); no capstone-to-capstone edge. **Edges touching F058/F059/F060 are drawn dashed.** They cannot be mirrored — there is no feature side to record them on — and drawing them solid alongside verified edges would misrepresent their status. Drawing nothing would leave three required rows as isolated nodes, which misrepresents the plan differently. Dashing marks the distinction and the Completion Criteria now require **no dashed edge to survive to close**. **One edge withdrawn:** `F013 --> F060`. It duplicated `F013 --> F058` — both asserted the same must-understand dependency — so it is kept once, at F058, where the SI attribute block is first written; F060 inherits it through `F058 --> F060`. **`blocked_by` populated:** five features outside the required set gate features inside it — **#315 FEAT-001** (gates #336), **#334 FEAT-003** (gates #319), **#337 FEAT-015** (gates #318), **#349 FEAT-040** and **#365 FEAT-041** (both gate #366). Ordering, not composition; the required set stays at eight. **#365 is also graded beneficial in §2** — not a contradiction: beneficial/required grades the sufficiency argument, `blocked_by` states order, and both can hold of one feature. ## 5. 5171345451.body:
REPLAN: D13 applied — the one remaining "beneficial *but also* a prerequisite" tension in the §2 roster is retired. No required set, cost band, acceptance criterion, kill criterion or machine-block key moved.

**The ruling, verbatim (D13):**

> A dependency system simply listing prerequisite completed issues is sufficient. I don't think that these require such fuss. Just make something that works.

D13 retires the treatment of "a feature graded beneficial is a hard `blocked_by` prerequisite of a required feature" as a rule-E defect. A prerequisite is a prerequisite; the sufficiency grading is a separate and lesser question, and the two need not agree.

**What changed — one row**

§2's beneficial table, the **FEAT-041 #365** row, previously read:

> filed, beneficial — **but also an ordering prerequisite**: #366 FEAT-042 declares `blocked_by: [336, 349, 365]`, so it is in `blocked_by`

The bolded *"but also"* is the tension D13 retires: it frames a plain prerequisite as something that stands in opposition to the grading. It now reads:

> filed, beneficial — and an ordering prerequisite: #366 FEAT-042 declares `blocked_by: [336, 349, 365]`, so it is in `blocked_by`. Beneficial states the sufficiency argument (it owns no §1 observation); `blocked_by` states the order (it must land first anyway). Both are true.

That is the form #311 and #312 already carry, and it is now the form this row carries too.

**What was already correct and is untouched**

This issue was searched end to end for the same shape, and the row above is the only instance. Everything else was already in D13's form before this REPLAN and is left byte-identical:

- The machine block's `blocked_by` comment already said it: *"#365 FEAT-041 is ALSO named as beneficial in §2. Not a contradiction: beneficial/required grades the SUFFICIENCY argument (does it own a §1 observation); this key states ORDER (must it land first). Both hold."*
- §2's five-prerequisites paragraph already said it: *"neither situation is a contradiction … A feature can be both, or neither-yet-still-ordering. Keeping the two facts in different keys is what stops the required set drifting from eight to thirteen on a scheduling fact."*
- The `related` comment already annotates #349 and #365 as *"(also an ordering prerequisite)"* without editorialising.
- The mermaid construction rule already handles it factually: *"no beneficial feature has an arrowhead at CAP18 (F041 #365 appears only as an ordering prerequisite of F042 and points at F042, never at CAP18)"*.
- No Open Question here asks whether a prerequisite should be adopted into the required set, and §3 carries no risk of that shape. Nothing was deleted, so nothing renumbers: §3 keeps eight risks, the Open Questions keep all eight, and every cross-reference resolves.

**Facts kept, unchanged**

`blocked_by: [315, 334, 337, 349, 365]` and every edge behind it — #315→#336, #334→#319, #337→#318, #349→#366, #365→#366 — all still read off the required feature's own machine block. #365 is still beneficial, still out of `requires_features`, still not drawn with an arrowhead at CAP18, and still a hard prerequisite of the required #366. The DoD still requires every `blocked_by` entry (#315, #334, #337, #349, #365) to close as landed or have its ordering edge withdrawn by a `REPLAN:` that re-reads the required feature's own `blocked_by`.

**Nothing numeric moved, and that is checked rather than asserted.** `requires_features` is the same eight (#318, #319, #336, #366, #367, #486, #487, #490); `blocked_by`, `blocks` and `related` are byte-identical. §1's five steps and every voltage in them, §4's eight acceptance criteria, and all seven kill criteria (K18-1…K18-6 and K9) are byte-identical. The Cost section is untouched: required sum 3+5.5+2+0.5+2+5+2+4+11 = **35** and 6+9.5+3.5+1+3+10+3+7+17 = **60**; marginal **11–20**; cumulative **51–89**; demo slice **3–6 mw**. A numeric diff over the whole body shows exactly one token changed count — "1", from the added phrase "owns no §1 observation".

Membership is unchanged, sufficiency is unchanged, minimality is unchanged. Only the framing of an ordering fact moved.

5175691158.body:
## Feature deduplication, pass 1 — boundary note (NOT a merge)

Checked #314 against **#319 (FEAT-013, per-section internal versioning)** as a duplicate candidate: both are forward-compatibility machinery on the load path, at two granularities. **Not a duplicate. No merge, both stay open.**

**The boundary, stated so it is not re-litigated:**

- **#314 owns the granularity of an *attribute name inside a known element block*.** Mechanism: the four `Element.setValue` overloads (`src/jls/elem/Element.java:344,359,374,389`) change `void` → `boolean`, the 26 overrides across 17 files follow, and the five `Circuit` loader arms (`:1067,:1078,:1089,:1105,:1116`) turn a miss into a diagnostic naming **file, line, element identity, attribute name**. Acceptance: the `test/resources/silent-loss/` corpus asserting the diagnostic *text* (not a flag), plus aggregation so a file with a thousand stale attributes produces a summary rather than a thousand lines.
- **#319 owns the granularity of a *named, independently versioned section*.** Mechanism: a section frame carrying `(id, version, must-understand, hash-participation)`; unknown **optional** → skip, preserve verbatim, informational diagnostic; unknown **required** → refuse by name with the section id and version. Acceptance: I1 section-to-section byte independence, I2 preserve-without-reordering, I3 refuse-by-name, I4 raw-section digest validation.

Neither delivers the other's outcome. #319's frame is silent about an attribute name a known element does not declare — that item sits *inside* a section #319 fully understands and hands to the element loader. #314's `boolean` dispatch is silent about a section id this build has never heard of. `docs/file-format.md:141` already asserts that unknown attribute *names* inside a known element are "handled"; #314 is what makes that assertion observable, and #319 is what makes an unknown *section* survivable. Different failure modes, different fixtures, different diagnostics.

**One genuine coupling, already recorded on both sides, and not a merge basis:** #314 Open Question 1 (reject vs. load-and-report on a miss) and #314 §5 criterion 5 defer the **format-epoch policy** to #319, and #314 §7 obliges the two features to *agree* on it rather than each deciding. That is one decision two features share — rule 3(b), a shared prerequisite, not a shared outcome.

**Also checked #314 against its own declared prerequisite #315 (FEAT-001 RESIDUAL).** They share TASK-0001 (the registry-keyed-table inventory) and #315 → #314 is a mirrored ordering edge. Distinct outcomes: #315 makes *every registry-keyed table* total by build rule; #314 makes *the attribute dispatch* total by compiler and the loader loud on a miss. Shared task, rule 3(b) again — no merge.

**Why it is not a duplicate (rule: a task that implements PART of a feature is the intended hierarchy).** This feature's `planned_tasks` names **four** children, and #404 is one of them:

| Child | Filed as | Owns |
|---|---|---|

That is TASK-0004's deliverable; this task ships only the three acceptance tests below so the diagnostic text exists for TASK-0004 to assert against."* §12: *"The parent feature #314 states the scope; this issue does not restate it."*

## Adversarial review, core-format slice — the `blocked_by: [315]` edge is narrowed, one stale number in the DAG walk, and the code claims re-pinned to master

Nothing in §1–§5 changes: the capability, the four-overload mechanism, the aggregation requirement and
the six integration criteria are all correct and all still absent on master. Three corrections to the
machine block and its prose.

### 1. ORDERING: `blocked_by: [315]` over-constrains, and this issue's own §6 says so

The machine block declares a hard block on #315 (FEAT-001). Read literally, that holds **#404**
(TASK-0003, the `boolean` dispatch and the five loader arms) and **#408** (TASK-0004, the fixture
corpus) behind a feature whose own Open Question 1 prices it at 2.1 maintainer-weeks and whose scope
boundary is still undecided.

This issue contradicts that reading itself, in §6:

> TASK-0001 is **independent** of TASK-0003 and safe to execute concurrently by a separate agent; its
> inventory is an input to the *judgement* about which misses are element-declaration bugs rather than
> file bugs, not to the code change. **Sequencing TASK-0001 first is convention, not necessity, and a
> scheduler may break it knowingly.**

and #404, as filed, agrees in its own machine block: `blocked_by: []`, with the comment *"nothing must
land first; see Related Work for the TASK-0001 sequencing convention, which is convention and not a
prerequisite (FEAT-002 §6 says so in terms)"*.

**What is genuinely required is narrower than #315.** §5 **criterion 2** — *"add a new element type
whose `savedAttributes()` omits one attribute it saves, then run the corpus. Observe: red"* — names
its own pinning as "the same corpus plus TASK-0001's totality test", and says outright that it is *"the
criterion neither task asserts alone"*. That is one task (**#372**), gating one criterion, at
**close-out**.

> **Corrected edge:**
> ```yaml
> blocked_by: []          # was [315]
> requires_at_closeout: [372]   # TASK-0001 — §5 criterion 2 only; see below
> related: [315, ...]
> ```
> #404 and #408 may be scheduled at any time. The cost of scheduling them before #372, priced so a
> scheduler can take it knowingly: some early `UNCONSUMED_ATTRIBUTE` diagnostics will trace back to an
> under-declaring `savedAttributes()` rather than to a bad file. #404's **H3** already covers that case
> — *"if any tracked fixture warns… the warning is real evidence that some element's
> `savedAttributes()` is incomplete. Record it, fix the declaration, and note it to FEAT-001 (#315) —
> do not suppress the warning"* — so the risk is caught by a falsification criterion rather than by
> silence. §11's "savedAttributes() completeness is assumed, not proved" threat is the same risk and
> is likewise already recorded.

The mirror half of this correction is posted on #315, whose `blocks:` list is corrected there in the
same pass, so no half-edge is left (§7's Link-pass obligation).

### 2. STALE REFERENCE in the DAG walk: #352 is closed

The DAG-walk paragraph states: *"Walking outward from #315: its `blocked_by` is empty and its `blocks`
set is {#314, #334, #336, **#352**, #358}"*. **#352 was closed as a duplicate of #170 in the Phase C
dedup.** #315's `blocks:` is corrected there to `[314, 334, 336, 358]`; the DAG walk here should be
read against that set. The walk's conclusion is unaffected — removing a node from a set that already
contained no path back to #314 cannot create one — so this is a citation fix, not a re-derivation.

### 3. EVIDENCE RE-PINNED: every code claim in §1 verified on master `07a0bea`

Per #493, `2d0ca9d` lives only on a branch scheduled for deletion and its citations are unreliable;
#488 measured some of them on master and refuted others. **The claims this feature rests on are in the
surviving set. Re-verified at master `07a0bea`:**

| Claim (§1) | At `2d0ca9d` | At master `07a0bea` |
|---|---|---|
| Four `Element.setValue` overloads return `void` | asserted | **holds** — `src/jls/elem/Element.java`, `int` / `long` / `BigInteger` / `String`, all `public void` |
| `git grep -n "public void setValue" -- src/jls/` → 26 | asserted | **holds — 26** |
| The `boolean` form does not exist | implied | **holds** — `grep -c "public boolean setValue" src/jls/` → **0** |
| `test/resources/silent-loss/` absent | asserted | **holds** — `test/resources/` contains `hdl/` and `orientation-geometry.txt` only |
| `docs/registry-keyed-tables.md` absent | asserted | **holds** — not in `docs/` |
| `src/jls/imp/` absent (the `.circ` reader) | asserted | **holds** — no `imp` package under `src/jls/` |

So the final Definition-of-Done line — *"`git grep -n "public void setValue" -- src/jls/` returns
zero: the totality is compiler-enforced, not conventional"* — is an evaluable, currently-false, and
therefore good criterion, and the whole feature is confirmed unshipped. **Line numbers have shifted;
re-derive by content, not by the `2d0ca9d` line numbers in §1.**

One correction of detail while re-pinning: §1 says the ripple is "26 declarations across 17 files… all
in `src/jls/elem/`". On master that is still 26, but the grep is scoped `src/jls/` — an executor should
re-run it unscoped before assuming `elem/` contains them all, because `Element` being `sealed`
(#404 O7) bounds *subclasses*, not the set of files that happen to declare a `setValue` overload.

5175850547.body:
Boundary note (feature deduplication, pass 1) — #316 versus #337. **Overlap noted; not merged.**

Both issues make claims of the form "mutation stops being a GUI-only act", and on a skim they read as the same feature. They are not: this is a feature and its downstream consumer sharing one seam (rule 3(b)), and both issues already state the boundary themselves — this comment only puts it on the record so a later generation does not re-fuse them.

**The boundary.**

- **#337 owns the mutation seam being headless.** `CircuitOp.apply` loses its `java.awt.Graphics` parameter in favour of `jls.core.TextMetrics`, `jls.collab` enters the headless-core ratchet, and a programmatic construction verb set replaces the emit-save-text-and-reparse idiom. Its criterion 1 is a JVM started with `-Djava.awt.headless=true` and no display producing byte-identical canonical saves.
- **#316 owns the editor's own testability.** The nine-state interaction machine becomes a constructible class whose transition table can be asserted in a plain JUnit test with no display substrate, and `jls.edit` gains a live JaCoCo floor — the one package in the tree with none, exempted in prose at `pom.xml:408-409` by a sentence that names this feature's own precondition. Plus dialog **validation** coverage, the two Wayland-rig placeholders, and the palette's view dimension.

**This issue's own § Scope Boundary already says so:** *"**Removing `Graphics` from `CircuitOp.apply`.** That is FEAT-015's (#337). This feature consumes the result and must not fork a second abstraction; the pattern to converge on is `jls.core.TextMetrics`."* And #337's mirrors it: *"**The nine-state mouse machine and the `source ==` dispatcher.** **#316** and **#84** own those. This feature owns the mutation vocabulary and the entry point. Moves that shrink #316's surface are welcome but must not be *required* here, **or a weeks-scale feature is gated behind a months-scale one.**"*

**The relationship is an ordering edge, already mirrored.** This issue carries `blocked_by: [317, 337]` and #337 carries `blocks: [..., 316, ...]`, with the stated reason: *"the op layer is the mutation seam the decomposition extracts **to** — a gesture that ends in `OpSink.submit` is testable headlessly, one that mutates inline is not."* A prerequisite relationship is the strongest possible evidence that two issues are **not** duplicates.

**Distinct outcomes, restated as the tests that separate them.** #337's criterion 1 can pass with `SimpleEditor.java` untouched at 5,852 lines and `jls.edit` still unfloored; this issue's criteria 1 and 2 can pass with `CircuitOp.apply` still taking a `Graphics`, since the state objects are asserted against the transition function, not against op application. Neither subsumes the other, and the coverage floor is this issue's alone.

**One coordination hazard, recorded on both sides rather than resolved here:** #282 and #283 touch the same `SimpleEditor` handlers this extraction relocates, and #337's TASK-0037 bundles those same four inline commit paths. Coordinate per step — #167 owns the op-layer commits, this feature owns the state structure, and #337 owns the signature.

No merge is recorded. Both remain open with distinct scope.

## Roster reconciliation: all six `planned_tasks` are filed, and TASK-0020's issue number just changed

Recorded during the feature-to-task deduplication pass (cluster D), which closed the issue this feature's TASK-0020 row pointed at. **No body edited, nothing closed here.**

### Every row says "not filed"; every row is filed

§2's decomposition table marks all six children **not filed**, and `planned_tasks` carries them as prose scope statements rather than issue references. Re-derived by title search:

| Roster row | Filed as | State |
|---|---|---|
| TASK-0019 — decomposition plan + `jls.edit` JaCoCo floor | **#440** | open |
| TASK-0020 — the nine-state machine becomes a class; last `getSource() ==` becomes an `Action` | **#84** (see below) | open |
| TASK-0021 — dialog **validation** + mouse assertion surface | **#470** | open |
| TASK-0018 — fail-closed JBR digest pin + lane registration | **#411** | open |
| TASK-0069 — transcript capture, replay, console pane | **#455** | open |
| TASK-0105 — view dimension on the palette contract | **#482** | open |

The Completion Criteria require *"`planned_tasks` empty (each resolved to a filed issue or descoped)"* — that condition is already materially satisfied for all six and only the bookkeeping is outstanding.

### TASK-0020 specifically — read this before following the roster

TASK-0020 was filed as **#441**. **#441 is now closed as a duplicate of #84.** Both were `tier:task` and owned the same outcome (the nine-state machine leaves `EditWindow` and becomes headlessly assertable); #441's own § Related Work said *"This task closes that residual"* of #84. Lower number wins, so **#84 is this feature's TASK-0020** and #441 is a tombstone.

Full migration record: [#84#issuecomment-5181489241](https://github.com/anadon/JLS/issues/84#issuecomment-5181489241).

Two consequences for this feature:

1. **#84 declares `part_of_feature: none`.** It is this feature's child by TASK-0020's row and by this body's own Related-issues section (*"This feature's TASK-0020 is #84's scope"*), but the field on #84 does not say so, so a landing there will not automatically produce the `STATUS:` comment this feature's Completion Criteria expect. Flagged on #84 three times now; it needs a field edit on that issue, not here.
2. **#84's `blocked_by` is `[]`, but TASK-0020 is blocked by TASK-0019 (#440)** — this feature's own §6 critical path is *TASK-0019 → TASK-0020*, and the reason is measurability: moving several hundred lines between classes changes JaCoCo attribution, and `jls.edit` is unfloored at [`pom.xml:408`](https://github.com/anadon/JLS/blob/2d0ca9dcd9db78b36c3caf4c6c57dd8701862cc7/pom.xml#L408), so "the suite is still green" is compatible with a real coverage loss. #441 carried that edge; #84 does not. The edge is recorded in #84's absorbing comment §A and must survive the field reconciliation.

### Open Question 1 is answered by the merge

> **1. Does `enum State` survive as identity tags?** … recommended default … keep the enum as lightweight identity and logging tags

#441's answer, now on #84: the promoted top-level `InteractionState` **is** the identity tag and the nested `SimpleEditor.State` is removed — it is package-private, so nothing outside `jls.edit` can name it and the compiler finds every in-package reader. Recorded as *rides along* there too, so this is not a REPLAN trigger; it is one fewer open question.

### ESCALATED to this feature, because §7's re-planning protocol owns it

The merge left **#84 carrying two incompatible designs for the same class** — this issue's §3 *"Provides"* paragraph and #84's §7.4 both specify a GoF state interface with per-event handlers and `enter`/`exit` hooks and nine package-private implementations, while #441's absorbed contract specifies a behaviourless `enum InteractionState` plus a `public final class MouseMachine` returning a `Transition` record. They collide on the class name, on visibility, and on whether a `switch` survives (this feature's Completion Criteria demand `grep -c "switch (currentState)"` → 0; #441's H2 makes an exhaustive `switch` **expression** the mechanism that turns a tenth state into a compile error).

Stated in full on [#84#issuecomment-5227061320](https://github.com/anadon/JLS/issues/84#issuecomment-5227061320) with three options. **It blocks TASK-0020's execution**, and because this feature's §3 *"Provides"* states the GoF form as the feature-level contract, choosing option (b) or (c) is a **contract deviation requiring a `REPLAN:` here**, not a silent choice inside the task. This feature's §7 already names the shape: *"Contract deviation (the extracted state contract drags a Swing type into a headless package): §3 is stale until reconciled"* — the same clause covers a contract that changes design, and the AWT-free invariant in §4 survives either way.

5227451900.body:
## ORDERING — MIRROR (round-2 review, slice: ordering-coherence): the #571 edge into this issue is narrowed to two criteria; this issue is now a measured chokepoint

Half-edges are the defect the mirror discipline exists to prevent, so this records the other end of a correction made on **#571** (FEAT-C30-6, *the two developers this repo bounced hear back…*). Nothing in this issue's scope, criteria or ordering changes.

### What changed on the other endpoint

#571 declared `ordering_after: [567, 568, 316]` at feature scope. Behind that gate sat its AC-1 — post a reply on the two bounced 2026 external PRs (#4/#5, #187) and invite the authors back — which is #508 §3 item 1, the review's highest-leverage move, priced at ≈0 mw.

The gate is genuine but criterion-scoped: #571's **AC-2** states in its own text that invitations to Digital's rejected-PR authors *"go out only after #567, #568, and #316 have landed."* That is the right constraint and this issue is a legitimate part of it — cold-recruiting outside contributors into a codebase whose nine-state mouse machine is still undecomposed and untestable without a display is how a second cohort gets bounced. But the feature-scoped edge also caught AC-1, AC-3 and AC-4, none of which touch the editor.

**Corrected:** #571's `ordering_after` becomes `[]` at feature scope; `[567, 568, 316]` survives on **AC-2 and AC-5 only**. This issue's status as a prerequisite for the cold-outreach half is unchanged and was not weakened.

### Why this is worth a comment here rather than only there

This issue is now the most frequently cited chokepoint in the ordering graph, and two of the three citations found so far were over-broad:

| Cites #316 | Scope of the citation | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| **#369** (FEAT-053, verdict/report) | `blocked_by: [316, 321, 347]` | Genuine for #369's TASK-0112 half; round 1 verified it and left it standing. But three downstream issues (#524, #686, #757) had inherited it transitively via `ordering_after: [369, 466]` when their real prerequisite is #466 alone — corrected in round 1. |
| **#571** (FEAT-C30-6, contributor outreach) | whole feature | Over-broad; narrowed to AC-2/AC-5 in this pass. |

The pattern is the same both times: a real, narrow dependency on this issue gets recorded at a coarser scope than the criterion it came from, and then everything downstream of that issue silently inherits a 12–20 mw editor refactor as a prerequisite. #508 prices FEAT-008's decomposition at 12–20 mw and holds it *to its own 3.5-week checkpoint*, so an accidental edge into it is not a scheduling nuisance — it is an indefinite deferral of whatever inherited it.

**Requested of anything that adds a `blocked_by`/`ordering_after` entry naming this issue in future:** name the criterion, not the issue. "AC-2 waits on #316" is checkable; "this feature waits on #316" propagates.

### Not changed here

No claim is made about this issue's own ordering, scope, band or criteria. Its prerequisite #440 (the `jls.edit` coverage floor, recorded on #804) and its relationship to the #84 mouse-machine residual are untouched by this pass.

5175738169.body:
## Boundary note: #317 / #568 (feature deduplication, pass 1)

#568 (FEAT-C30-2) was seated in this pass's CI cluster because its substance is CI gating, and it must be read against this issue's required-check policy. **Verdict: no merge (rule 3c) — different outcomes on the same workflow files.**

**#568 AC-3** asks that CI workflows *run at all* for an outside contributor: a first-time contributor pushes to **their own fork** and gets a green/red verdict **with no maintainer approval step**. That is a workflow-trigger and permissions concern (fork-PR approval gating, `pull_request` vs `pull_request_target`, secret-less runs), and its beneficiary is an outsider with no write access. Its other three criteria — a shelf of ≥15 `good first issue` items, a written restocking rule, and the constraint that a curated issue not require touching `SimpleEditor` internals — are tracker curation and have nothing to do with this feature.

**This issue** decides which checks **block a merge on the default branch**, that every job carries a `timeout-minutes`, and that an hours-long run has a lane that is *not* the required gate. Its beneficiary is a maintainer protecting master.

**The boundary:** #568 is about a check *executing* for a stranger; #317 is about a check *gating* for everyone. They touch the same files and can collide there, so one coordination point is worth recording rather than discovering: TASK-0015's timeout lint scans the whole `.github/workflows/` directory, so any workflow #568 adds or re-triggers for forks is subject to it, and a fork-triggered lane must carry a timeout like every other job. That is a shared constraint, not shared scope.

## Boundary with #265 and #111 (feature/task deduplication pass, cluster C)

**Three features over overlapping CI ground, none a duplicate of another.** Recorded rather than merged, per the pass's instruction to draw the line where scope overlaps but outcomes differ.

Four clauses: every job carries an explicit `timeout-minutes` (TASK-0015 / **#374**); a scheduled long-run lane exists distinct from the required gate, with a stated gate budget and a large-fixture policy (TASK-0016 / **#378**); all three platforms block a merge (TASK-0017 / **#406**); the Wayland rig's two acknowledged placeholders are finished (TASK-0018 / **#411**).

#319 is the largest attractor in this cluster: seven features gate on it and three sibling issues touch the same save/load path. It was checked against each and **nothing merges into it, and it merges into nothing.** Recording the boundaries so a later pass does not absorb work that is not #319's.

**vs. #334 (FEAT-003, canonical text + stable-id references) — separate outcomes on the same serializer.**
#334 changes *what a reference names*: `r_old(e)` = the element's rank in the canonical order (a function of the whole element set) becomes `r_new(e)` = `sid(e)` (a function of `e` alone), via a new `sref` grammar item, and flips the default container from XZ to plain canonical text. Its acceptance is a **diff ratchet** — one element inserted into a ~1,000-element circuit changes ≤12 lines in ≤2 hunks for all three replica-id classes — plus `sha256sum <file>` == `Circuit.stateHash()`.
#319 changes *how the file is divided and versioned*: named sections with per-section versions and must-understand flags. It does not touch reference form and it does not touch the container default.
The edge is already recorded and mirrored: **#334 blocks #319**, because doing the section frame before the reference form changes means rewriting every golden and every fixture twice. That is an ordering dependency (rule 3(b)), not a shared outcome.

**vs. #363 (FEAT-035, checkpoint and resume) — separate outcomes on the same serializer.**
#363's outcome is the commuting square: `deser(ser(Σ_t)) = Σ_t` and `step^k(deser(ser(Σ_t))) = step^k(Σ_t)` byte-identically, with the observable corollary that a resumed run's waveform **tail** is byte-identical to the uninterrupted run's. That requires the event queue with its total order *and its duplicate-check state*, `now`, `maxTime`, the stopping flag, `SimEvent`'s sequence counter made per-`Simulator`, and every stateful element's *running* contents written back rather than rebuilt from init text.
#319 provides the **carrier** — an optional, independently versioned section that a checkpoint rides and that an older reader skips or refuses honestly — and nothing else. It builds no simulator state, no round-trip property, no refusal list, no element-kind state mapping. #319's own §1 out-of-scope says this explicitly ("the *content* of any section other than the raw image … belongs to the feature that defines it"), and #363 is recorded as `blocked_by: [319]` with the mirror in #319's `blocks`. Rule 3(b).
Note the two are not even guaranteed to compose: #363 Open Question 1 may resolve the checkpoint to a **sidecar or a directory** rather than a section, in which case #363 stops consuming this frame entirely and the edge is removed by REPLAN on both sides. A feature that may not use #319 at all is not a duplicate of #319.

**vs. #314 (FEAT-002, fail-loud loader).** Full boundary recorded on #314. Summary: #314 is unknown *attribute name inside a known element*; #319 is unknown *section*. The shared item is the **format-epoch policy** (#314 OQ-1 / §5 criterion 5 defer it here), which is one decision two features must agree on — rule 3(b).

**Also noted, no action:** #340 (FEAT-016) considered #319 as the owner of its import-to-subcircuit scope and explicitly rejected it — "consuming a mechanism is not owning a capability … nothing in #319's scope is about what a subcircuit instance *means*." That determination stands and is not revisited here.

5175699964.body:
## Feature deduplication, pass 1 — boundary note (NOT a merge)

Checked #322 against **#341 (FEAT-027, net kinds and driver strength)** as the closest duplicate candidate in this cluster. Both issues contain the sentence "multi-driver resolution stops depending on draw order", both rewrite `WireNet.propagate`'s tri-state block (`src/jls/elem/WireNet.java:454-485`), both share **TASK-0057**, and both assert a permutation-invariance property test. The question asked was whether the resolution lattice is one outcome owned twice — specifically, whether #341 subsumes #322's per-bit encoding. **It does not. Not a duplicate, no merge, both stay open.**

**The boundary, on the algebra rather than on the prose:**

- **#322 owns the *value*: what a bit can say.** `Σ ⊇ {0, 1, X, Z}` per bit, replacing `s ∈ ({0,1}^w) ∪ {⊥}` where `⊥` is a `null` reference meaning the *whole signal* is HiZ (`docs/simulation-semantics.md:55-56`: "There is no per-bit HiZ"). Its migration is 338 `BitSet` references across `src/jls/elem/*.java`, 27 `react` implementations each needing a recorded keep-or-propagate decision for its HiZ input, and `Put.currentValue` (`src/jls/elem/Put.java:385`) ceasing to be `@Nullable BitSet`. Its fold is `⊕ : Σ × Σ → Σ` with `Z` as identity and `0 ⊕ 1 = X`, proven commutative, associative and idempotent.
- **#341 owns the *second axis*: how hard a driver drives.** `S = (HIGHZ < WEAK < PULL < STRONG < SUPPLY)`, each driver contributing `(s_i, v_i)`, resolving per bit as `Z` if `s* = HIGHZ`, `v` if `V* = {v}`, `X` if `|V*| > 1` where `s* = max_i s_i` and `V* = {v_i : s_i = s*}`. Plus drawable `PullUp`/`PullDown` elements, driver kinds (open-drain, technology-dependent floating-input behaviour), and **net kind as saved, versioned, must-understand state**.

The subsumption test fails in both directions. #341's lattice is *defined over* #322's alphabet — its own §3 states "strength is meaningless over a two-state value", and its §1 out-of-scope hands the value domain to #322 by name. 5227613305.body:
## Cross-reference — the N-ary program's reservation, and why it does not land on this feature

Source: **PR #887**, maintainer design discussion 2026-08-08. **This feature's scope is unchanged**; this comment exists so the N-ary sequencing is visible from here.

**What the N-ary program needs from the value migration.** Interval accessors (`lo()`/`hi()`, returning `0`/`1`) and a frozen field list naming the generic-tier extension point must be reserved *inside* the value-representation migration, not bolted on after — otherwise the remaining N-ary work becomes a second value migration.

**Where that landed, and why not here.** TASK-0056 (#475) left this feature when it closed into #232 (recorded in this issue's earlier comment); its replacement is **#878** (the type + frozen field list) and **#879** (the plumbing). The reservation is on **#878**, because it is a field-list decision. This feature relates to that work as an **ordering dependency, not a parent**.

**What this feature still supplies to the N-ary program.** X/Z/U as per-position sentinel states orthogonal to the alphabet. The proposal builds directly on them (`nary-01` §3), with one rule worth reading here because it constrains this feature's coercion sites:

> There is **no `zeroFill()` analogue for non-binary nets**. The binary zero-coercion sites are a compatibility behaviour being preserved for binary, not a rule to generalize. `lo` is *not* "the default value"; nothing makes 0 (or `lo`) special at initialization. Uninitialized state is **U** where this feature's stage machinery enables it, else X.

So a floating non-binary input reads **Z** and propagates **X** — making the classic first-year mistake visible on N-ary nets from day one. Any decision here that generalizes a binary zero-coercion into the shared machinery would break that, and should be raised on #888 before it lands.

**New downstream beneficiary:** CAP-39 (#888), which requires this feature alongside the replanned #344 and amended #361.

**Why they are not the same outcome.**

- **#323 (this issue) owns one importer and its semantics.** A `.circ` parser producing a construct model, hardened as untrusted input per attack vector; the geometric connectivity replication `δ(k, n, s)` whose failure mode is *silently disconnected* circuits; the partition-equality assertion `P(imp(f)) ≅ P_src(f)` over a corpus of public files; the name-collision reject rule with the recorded `ShiftRegister`/`HdlExporter.java:84` case; the through-hole part data with its licence audit (TASK-0055); and the corpus accept/reject tables as the measurement that replaces the estimate (I6). Its consumers are #558 (.dig), #559 (.cv) and #561 (Falstad text). Its band is 1-2 mw — it is refactoring-and-documentation scope, not importer scope.

**This issue's § 1 explicitly disclaims the generalization.** "A second migration source" is out of scope here, with the stated reason: *"The scaffolding makes a second source cheap, which is exactly why it should be a separate decision with its own trigger rather than an assumed continuation."* #556 is that separate decision. | Roster row | Filed as | Owns |

| TASK-0054 | **#451** | the `.circ` reader — a parser producing a construct model (circuits, components as library+name+attribute set, wires, appearance), hardened as untrusted input per attack vector, plus the written construct map and the migration report, with a test asserting the dropped set equals the reported set |

§2 rejects merging the first two by name: *"the part data is a transcription-and-licence exercise with an audit as its gate; the reader is a parser-and-semantics exercise with a corpus run as its gate. Different skills, different reviewers, different failure modes."* And §6 records that ordering as necessity, not convention: *"The part data the imported designs reference has to exist as data before an importer can bind to it."*

**What this feature owns that #451 does not:**

1. **§5 I1** — import each file in a corpus of **public** `.circ` files and compare net counts and net membership against the source's own computed nets, mechanically per file. A rule-B criterion: no child asserts partition-preservation over a real corpus.
2. **§5 I5** — a licence audit over the absorbed part data. #450's.
3. **§5 I6** — publish the accept and reject tables from the corpus run, with the corpus named and its representativeness argued. Marked in the body as **this issue's close-out**, and §6 states why it is the gate rather than a follow-up: *"No converter from this format to any other format exists anywhere… nobody has data on how much of a real corpus maps… the result could reorder everything after it."*

**#556** (FEAT-C29-1: *every importer tells its losses in one voice — the `.circ` report becomes a format-agnostic contract of construct, disposition, location and explanation*) generalises this feature's report contract across `.dig` (#558), `.cv` (#559), Falstad (#561) and Digital test vectors (#562). Neither closes into the other. Both stay open. A boundary note recording the same relation from the task side has been posted on #451.

5175747945.body:
## Boundary note: #324 / #369, and #324 / #354 (feature deduplication, pass 1)

#324 was pulled into pass 1's grading/batch cluster because "the exchange replays without the human" reads as a batch-reproducibility claim. **Verdict: no merge** — the phrase names a different mechanism than it appears to.

**#324's replay is transcript replay of a byte door.** A transcript is an ordered sequence $(t_i, d_i, b_i)$ of stamped bytes with $t_i$ drawn from a retirement index or simulated time and **never** a wall clock, and the claim is $\mathrm{run}(C, \mathrm{in}(T)) = \mathrm{out}(T)$: feeding a recorded run's *input projection* back through the same circuit reproduces its recorded output with nobody typing. "Without the human" is literal — it is the removal of an interactive keyboard from the loop. The surrounding scope is a sealed `HostBytePort` with an enumerated permit set, an invocation-time grant that no `.jls` file can obtain, a polled three-address `Console` element with no interrupt output, a ring the host thread offers into and the simulation thread drains at the `beforeEvent` boundary, and a CI ratchet refusing any golden produced while a live door was granted.

**#369's determinism is grading reproducibility.** Its claim is that an aggregate report over a set of submissions is invariant under permutation of that set — a property of a report assembled from many runs, not of one run's I/O stream. No verdict, no expectations file, no report schema appears in #324; no host handle, permit set, or thread-confinement invariant appears in #369. Rule 3(c).

**Where they genuinely meet, recorded so it is not mistaken for overlap later:** #324 §1's audience note ("Grading a submission on what it printed needs a transcript, not a screenshot") means a console-bearing design's *observable* is a transcript, so a future grading run over such a design would consume #324's artifact as its input. That is a producer/consumer relationship at most, and #369 does not currently name it.

**#324 ↔ #354:** already a mirrored ordering edge, not an overlap. #354 removes the 1e8-tick ceiling and supplies pause/heartbeat/clean-interrupt; #324's §6 states the consequence of proceeding without it plainly — *"the port works and the session ends mid-conversation"* — and drains inside that loop rather than building it.

**Two entries are unaffected and should not be touched:** #332 (FEAT-055) and #363 (FEAT-035) were examined in this pass and neither merged; #318 is outside this cluster and was not examined.

### 2. #333 versus #332 — overlap noted, NOT merged

Adjudicated in pass 1 with the boundary comment posted on #332; mirrored here so both sides carry it. These two carry a real skim-level duplicate risk — both phrase the win as *"the single-machine ceiling stops being the limit"*, both were filed the same minute, both serve only #312, and both carry unnumbered `planned_tasks` because the plan registry's task space closed at TASK-0112. **#332 makes the design exist as parts.** N partition files plus a boundary description; each part elaborating without the others resident; boundary net identity across a cut; uncuttable constructs refused **by name at partition time**. Its central measurement is a memory bound `M(load(D)) <= max_i M(D_i) + M(B) + c`, **measured rather than asserted**, whose named failure mode is any convenience index of size `Θ(Σ_i |D_i|)`.

## Boundary with the C28 benchmarking features #554, #555, #557, #560 (feature/task deduplication pass, cluster C)

**Not duplicates.** The pass flagged C28 as a coverage-and-duplication risk against this feature, since both ship numbers, fixtures and a ratchet. On reading, they are a **producer and its consumers** over two different audiences, and no merge is made.

**The line: an internal denominator versus a public claim.**

- **#335 (this feature)** measures the constants the *plan's own arithmetic* divides by — the per-cycle active fraction α, the calibration constant k, CPI, events per retired instruction, levelized ns/node — records them in `docs/machine-calibration.md` §6/§7, commits the CPU-scale anchor, deletes `riscv/`, and installs the standing gate (TASK-0026 / **#442**: one event-count equality, two ceiling-only bands, one byte-identity over the golden corpus). Its audience is the maintainer, the six serving capstones' budgets, and anyone funding engine work against #232. It ships no product code and publishes no competitor-facing number.
- **#554** ships a committed, documented **benchmark suite** — one command emitting events/s and cycles/s per fixture with each fixture's clocking regime recorded (**#726**), fixtures tracked in-tree outside `riscv/` including at least two below CPU scale (**#728**), and machine-readable output (**#730**).
- **#555** publishes **`docs/performance.md`** with the full method — hardware, JDK, flags, node counts — naming at least one place a competitor is faster (**#732**), and makes the README's single performance line cite it (**#733**).
- **#557** keeps a published number from going stale: a **scheduled lane** re-running the published workloads (**#735**) and a red lane that names which published number is now a lie (**#738**).
- **#560** runs **JLS, Digital and Logisim-Evolution** on the same workloads on the same machine with a published harness (**#740**), and publishes a table including at least one workload a competitor wins (**#742**).

**The consumer relationship is explicit in C28's own text.** #557's title and #735's outcome both name *"TASK-0026's ceiling bands"* — that is this feature's #442. C28 does not re-derive the bands; it re-runs published workloads under them. And #560's cross-tool comparison appears nowhere in this feature's scope at any tier. Absorbing C28 here would destroy the entire competitor-facing half (#732, #740, #742) and the public-doc-staleness gate; absorbing this feature into C28 would destroy α, k, CPI, the `riscv/` deletion ordering constraint and §4 invariant 4.

**Two real overlaps, recorded so they are not built twice.**

1. **Fixtures.** This feature's TASK-0025 (**#413**) commits the CPU-scale calibration anchor and deletes `riscv/`; #554's TASK-C554-2 (**#728**) tracks benchmark fixtures in-tree outside `riscv/` "including at least two circuits below CPU scale". These must be **one fixture set with two consumers**, not two sets. A separate boundary comment is posted on #413. Both are downstream of TASK-0016 (**#378**)'s fixture-size policy and Open Questions 1 and 2 here — where a tens-of-megabyte fixture lives, and which circuit is the CPU-scale anchor — which block #413 and should be answered once for both.
2. **Ratchet versus lane.** #442 asserts inside the required gate against the committed fixtures; #735 re-runs the *published* workloads on a schedule. Same band vocabulary, different lanes and different workloads. A boundary comment is posted on #442.

**Prerequisite that governs every number on both sides, carried forward.** This feature's one `blocked_by` is **#353 (FEAT-005)**: measuring per-event cost through a quadratic stimulus parse measures the parse, and the corpus records that defect as ~80% of wall clock. Any C28 number taken before #353 lands measures the same parse. C28 should record that dependency rather than rediscover it.

**Invariant both sides must honour.** §4.5 here: no number is published without its clocking regime, and no ns/node figure without node count and pass count. #554's per-fixture clocking-regime requirement is the same rule, restated for the public suite — they must not diverge into two conventions. Note also §5 criterion 4: the TestGen-versus-internal-`Clock` events-per-cycle disagreement (121.5 vs 245.5 on element-for-element identical circuits, vs 388.4 on the anchor workload — a 3.2x spread, `docs/machine-calibration.md:870-871`) must be explained or explicitly bounded, **not averaged away**, before any public throughput figure rests on it.

**Disposition: no merge, no closure. All five features stay open with the ownership above.**

Removing one obliges the same `REPLAN:` to remove the mirror; a half-edge is the defect this Link pass exists to prevent."* Both edges below survive the merge in substance — only their far endpoint moves.

| Current entry | Becomes | Why the edge itself survives |
|---|---|---|
| `blocks: [… 348 …]` — #348 FEAT-051 | **#169** | #348 closed as a duplicate of **#169** (Shared session v1). The dependency was never on #348's identity — it is that *a session synchronises a circuit by exchanging ops, and until every editor mutation is an op that applies without a drawing context there is nothing headless to send and nothing to apply on receipt.* #169 now carries that scope, and its absorbing comment records `blocked_by: [337]` as **real and gating its TASK-0109 replica loop**, citing `src/jls/collab/op/CircuitOp.java:51` still reading `void apply(Circuit circuit, Graphics g) throws OpRejected;` at `2d0ca9d`. |
| `blocks: [… 352 …]` — #352 FEAT-052 | **#171** | #352 closed as a duplicate of **#170**, with **#171** as co-survivor for the replication half. The dependency is the replication half's: *the op vocabulary must be complete and headless before it can be closed; an op set with four gestures still inline cannot be a closed vocabulary.* That is #171's premise, so the edge lands on #171. (#170 inherits the same closure as a **sequencing** consequence for its cap work — the caps would otherwise be specified against a moving target — but that is recorded on #170 as sequencing, not as a second `blocks` edge here.) |

**Resulting list:** `blocks: [316, 318, 326, 345, 169, 171]`. Per the maintainer's rule this is recorded by comment; the machine block is the maintainer's to edit, and the mirrors on #169 and #171 are recorded in their own absorbing comments.

The §6 sentence *"Six features are held behind this one: #316, #318, #326, #345, #348 and #352"* re-reads as **#316, #318, #326, #345, #169 and #171** — still six, none dropped.

**One coupled measurement, recorded on both sides:** #167's inventory-closure criterion and this issue's criterion 2 (the deferral list over the 13 mutation-marking call sites at `SimpleEditor.java:749, 1402, 2560, 2819, 2873, 2929, 3439, 4964, 5105, 5244, 5552, 5569, 5754`) are **the same measurement taken from two sides**. 5181632672.body:
## Boundary record (feature/task deduplication, cluster E) — #443 is NOT a duplicate of this feature, and neither is #471

Recording this explicitly because the title overlap is strong enough that a later pass will otherwise re-open the question, and a merge here would destroy information irreversibly.

### The near-verbatim title is an artifact of a feature title enumerating its children

This feature's title has three clauses:

1. "every installer leg is a required check"
2. "its runtime is pinned by digest"
3. "each format's reproducibility is either proven or bounded in writing"

#443 (TASK-0027) reproduces the first two nearly word for word: *"all five installer legs become required checks, the bundled Wayland runtime is pinned by digest, and every OS asserts the .jls association README already claims."* The dedup sweep flagged that as a duplicate signal. **It is not one.** #443's own §12 draws the split, and this feature's own §2 roster agrees with it:

> "**#338 (FEAT-010 RESIDUAL)** — the owning feature. **Scope split:** this task owns acceptance criteria 1 (no leg experimental), 2 (association asserted per platform) and 3 (every runtime input pinned by digest). Criteria 4 (reproducibility), 5 (signing) and 6 (BOM guard) are **TASK-0028's** and must not be silently upgraded here."

So the decomposition is exactly what a feature-and-slices hierarchy is supposed to look like:

| | criteria 1, 2, 3 | criteria 4, 5, 6 |
|---|---|---|
| **#443** (TASK-0027) | owns | explicitly disclaims |
| **#471** (TASK-0028 RESIDUAL) | — | owns |
| **#338** (this feature) | integrates both, plus IC-1…IC-6 which neither child asserts alone | |

**#338 = #443 + #471.** Absorbing #443 would leave this feature with a single child covering half its criteria and the other half recorded only in a comment — a strictly worse structure than the one already filed. Rule: a task that implements *part* of a feature is the intended hierarchy, never a duplicate. Boundary recorded, no merge.

### The feature-level criteria that genuinely belong to neither child

Keeping these visible so they are not mistaken for slice scope and quietly dropped:

- **IC-1** — parse `release.yml` with a YAML parser and count matrix entries with `experimental: true` plus jobs carrying `continue-on-error` in the installer path; observe **0** against **4 of 5** at `2d0ca9d`. The count spans both children's edits.

- **IC-3** — five formats, five verdicts, one-to-one. **The criterion no single child covers**: #443 does not touch records, and #471 alone cannot assert totality over a format list it does not own.

> **#338** — *"every installer leg is a required check, its runtime is pinned by digest, **and each format's reproducibility is either proven or bounded in writing**"*
> **#443** — *"all five installer legs become required checks, the bundled Wayland runtime is pinned by digest, **and every OS asserts the .jls association README already claims**"*

Triage flagged this as a merge candidate on the title overlap. **It is not one, and merging would delete this feature's decomposition.** Recording the boundary so a later pass does not repeat the mistake.

**#443 and #471 *are* this feature's two planned children.** § 2's roster names TASK-0027 and TASK-0028; #443 is TASK-0027 and #471 is TASK-0028. Both were filed and both declare `part_of_feature: 338`. That is the intended feature→task hierarchy, not duplicate ownership.

**The six acceptance criteria of § 1 split cleanly, and both children say so in their own text:**

| § 1 criterion | Owner |
|---|---|
| 1. No installer leg is advisory | **#443** |
| 2. `.jls` association asserted per platform | **#443** |
| 3. Every runtime input pinned by digest (no `UNVERIFIED-PLACEHOLDER`) | **#443** |
| 4. Per-format reproducibility: byte-identical, or a published bound | **#471** |
| 5. Windows signature verified by a check that can fail | **#471** |
| 6. Bill-of-materials guard fails on an unrecorded dependency change | **#471** |

#443 § 12: *"**Scope split:** this task owns acceptance criteria 1, 2 and 3. Criteria 4 (reproducibility), 5 (signing) and 6 (BOM guard) are **TASK-0028's** and must not be silently upgraded here."* #471 § 12 mirrors it: *"**#443 owns the delivery half** (required checks, pinned runtime digest, file association); this owns the trust half."*

**The third clause of this feature's title is exactly what #443 excludes.** "Each format's reproducibility is either proven or bounded in writing" is #471's whole subject — #471's `blocks: [338]` names that clause verbatim as its reason. So the titles that look near-identical are in fact complementary: #443 covers clauses 1–2 of three, #471 covers clause 3.

**What only this feature owns — the reason it cannot collapse into either child:**

- **IC-1** (zero advisory legs, counted with a YAML parser across *both* children's edits — #338 § 5 says explicitly *"the count is a feature-level assertion across both children's edits"*).
- **IC-2** (`grep -rn "UNVERIFIED\|PLACEHOLDER" scripts/ .github/workflows/` returns nothing — spans the script *and* the workflow; built by this issue's close-out).
- **IC-3** (five formats ↔ five verdicts, one-to-one — *"the criterion no single child covers: TASK-0027 does not touch records and TASK-0028 alone cannot assert totality over a format list it does not own"*).
- **IC-4** (the clean-machine walk on all three platforms; also CAP-00 AC-8 and CAP-06 AC-6).

5181330220.justification: Absorbing/planning comment documenting #474 integration for superseded Pin-element approach; all relevant content absorbed into narrowed-scope body using attribute-based grouping instead
5181330220.body:
## Absorbing #474 (feature/task deduplication)

**Verdict.** #474 (TASK-0049) and this issue own the **same outcome**, not a slice of it. Two independent confirmations:

- This feature's `planned_tasks` roster has exactly **one** entry — TASK-0049 — and §3 says so out loud: *"Internal handoffs. N/A — single-child roster, so there are no sibling handoffs."*
- #474's own Related Work table says of this issue: *"**Owning feature (FEAT-021).** This is the feature end to end: the IR case, the element, and every emitter's handling of it."*

That is a duplicate under the dedup rule (same outcome owned twice), not the intended feature→task hierarchy. **Survivor is #339**, the lower number. #474 is superseded and will be closed in the verification stage; **do not close it yet**.

**Tier consequence.** The survivor is the feature and the absorbed issue is the task, so no tier relabel is needed. But the consequence is that this feature now has **no filed child**: its `planned_tasks` entry resolves to an absorbed issue. Either this feature is executed directly against the method below, or a successor task is filed against it — a later pass must not read the empty roster as "unplanned".

Everything below is carried forward from #474 because after its closure this comment is the only record. Evidence commit `2d0ca9dcd9db78b36c3caf4c6c57dd8701862cc7` ("`2d0ca9d`"); #474 records `git diff --stat 2d0ca9d HEAD -- src test pom.xml` as empty, so its compile probes observe that commit's code.

---

### 1. Scope this feature did not already state

**The sealed `Pin` hierarchy is a hard obstacle this issue never names.** `src/jls/elem/Pin.java` L18-L20:

```java
public abstract sealed class Pin extends LogicElement
		implements Watchable, Rotatable
		permits InputPin, OutputPin {
```

A third pin kind does not compile: `class is not allowed to extend sealed class: Pin (as it is not listed in its 'permits' clause)`. #474 flags this as the trap that bites first — *"a reviewer who does not know the class is sealed will read that error as unrelated"* — and hypothesises (H1) that widening `permits` is the single change that makes the rest compile, everything else being additive.

**There are exactly FOUR silent-fall-through sites, and two of them are in one file.** This issue says "every switch over the direction set"; #474 enumerates them, and the count is the point:

| site | code |
|---|---|
| `src/jls/hdl/VerilogEmitter.java` L110-L115 | `port.direction() == HdlModel.Direction.INPUT ? "input" : "output"` |
| `src/jls/hdl/VhdlEmitter.java` L126-L131 | `port.direction() == HdlModel.Direction.INPUT ? "in " : "out "` |
| `src/jls/hdl/board/PcfEmitter.java` L73-L76 | direction string for the constraint line |
| `src/jls/hdl/board/PcfEmitter.java` L190-L195 | direction string in the unknown-port error text |

Four ternaries, zero diagnostics. **Converting three of four produces a build that emits a legal Verilog module and an unusable constraint file** — this is threat T1 below and it is the single most likely partial failure.

**The three direction enums stay separate.** `YosysNetlist.Port.direction()` (the netlist's), `HdlModel.Direction` (the model's) and `ScannedPort.Direction` (the scanner's) are three enums. **Do not unify them in this task** — unifying is a different, larger change that would break the importer's and the scanner's independent evolution — **but make all three switches total.**

**A fourth `HdlModel.Port` construction site is needed** in `HdlExporter`, beside the three existing ones at L278, L292 and L301, each of which hard-codes a direction.

**The registration tax, measured.** `ElementRegistry.all().size() = 35`, `Palette.entries().size() = 32`; `InputPin` and `OutputPin` are registered and there is no third pin kind. A new element costs a registry row, a palette row and an export-policy row — and **zero `FORMAT` version** by `docs/file-format.md`'s own rule.

**The export ratchet is the mechanism, and it must not be edited.** `test/jls/hdl/HdlPolicyTest.java` L391-L400 (`exportPolicyIsTotalOverTheElementRegistry`) against the `EXPORTED` bucket at `src/jls/hdl/HdlExporter.java` L428-L435. `InoutPin` goes in `EXPORTED`. If the test needs editing, the element was added without an export decision — make the decision, do not edit the test.

**The readback substrate already exists and is normative.** `docs/simulation-semantics.md` §9 (L409-L421) covers tri-state nets, driver disabling, deterministic conflict resolution and the one-time conflict warning; **pins are already `TriProp` implementors**, which is why the element half is a *widening* rather than a new mechanism. This issue's Open Question 1 is thereby answered in #474's favour of option (a): ship over HEAD's two-state semantics and read the existing resolution. **No change to §9 is permitted by this work.**

---

### 2. Interface & data contract carried forward

```java
package jls.elem;

public final class InoutPin extends Pin implements TriProp { ... }
```

- One `Input` put, one `Output` put, one **1-bit enable input**.
- Enable non-zero → the `Output` drives the pin's value onto the net after `propDelay`. Enable zero → the `Output` drives `null` (HiZ) and the `Input` reads the net's **resolved** value. Both halves are the existing `TriState.react` semantics applied to a pin.
- Implements `TriProp` as `InputPin` does, so tri-state-ness propagates at edit time.
- `save(PrintWriter)` writes `ELEMENT InoutPin` with `name`, `bits`, `watch`, `orientation` — the `InputPin.save` shape.
- `HdlModel.Direction` gains `INOUT` with a javadoc sentence matching its two siblings' style.

**Rendering, as total functions replacing partial ternaries:**

$$v(\mathrm{INPUT}) = \texttt{"input"},\ v(\mathrm{OUTPUT}) = \texttt{"output"},\ v(\mathrm{INOUT}) = \texttt{"inout"}$$
$$h(\mathrm{INPUT}) = \texttt{"in "},\ h(\mathrm{OUTPUT}) = \texttt{"out "},\ h(\mathrm{INOUT}) = \texttt{"inout "}$$

and the two `PcfEmitter` renderings likewise. **Totality is enforced by the compiler, not by review: no `default` arm, so a fifth constant makes each of the four a compile error.** The absence of the default arm *is* the mechanism (H2).

**Importer realization** replaces the `default:` arm at `NetlistImporter.java` L184-L189:

$$m(\mathrm{INPUT}) = \text{InputPin} + \text{driver}, \quad m(\mathrm{OUTPUT}) = \text{OutputPin} + \text{reader}, \quad m(\mathrm{INOUT}) = \text{InoutPin}$$

The `builder.problem(...)` arm is **deleted, not left unreachable**.

**Forward-compatibility with the strength lattice (H4).** The element must be written so that a later strength lattice (#341) changes **resolution only**, not the element: rendering, drive and importer realization are untouched by strengths; only the readback's $\mathrm{res}$ gains strength ordering. That is the design constraint that makes shipping over HEAD's two-state, no-wired-AND/OR semantics safe rather than a decision that must be revisited.

**Migration.** No `FORMAT` bump. An older JLS refuses a file containing `InoutPin` loudly with *"no element type named InoutPin"* — a detectable refusal, not a misparse, which is exactly the property the bump rule is written around. `docs/file-format.md`'s element table gains the row.

**Concurrency.** `react` on the simulation thread, posting through `Simulator.post`, touching no shared state — identical to `InputPin` and `TriState`. Edit-time tri-state propagation (`WireNet.setTriState` through `TriProp`) is synchronous, EDT-only. No new thread, no lock, no new shared mutable state.

---

### 3. Acceptance criteria carried forward (named tests)

- `anEnabledInoutPinDrivesTheNet()` / `aDisabledInoutPinDrivesNothing()` — assert the net's resolved value and that the disabled pin contributes no driver.
- **`aDisabledInoutPinReadsWhatAnotherElementDrives()` — the load-bearing assertion.** This is the one that fails if the element is built as an output-only pin with a second name. **Write it first.**
- `twoEnabledInoutPinsWithDifferentValuesReportOneConflict()` — reuses §9's conflict contract: deterministic winner, warning reported **once**.
- `anInoutPinRoundTripsThroughSaveAndLoad()`.
- `verilogDeclaresInout()`, `vhdlDeclaresInout()`, `theConstraintFileLabelsTheDirectionAsInout()` — **one assertion per converted switch**, so none of the four can regress to a ternary.
- `HdlPolicyTest.exportPolicyIsTotalOverTheElementRegistry` stays green **without being edited**.
- `NetlistImporterTest.anInoutModulePortImportsAsAnInoutPin()`.
- `test/resources/hdl/board/blinky_icestick.pcf` is **unchanged** — it contains no inout port, so if it moves the direction switch was written wrong.
- Existing saves and export goldens byte-identical for circuits with no inout port; `DeterministicSaveTest`, `AllElementsRoundTripTest` and `CapabilityInterfaceTest` green **unregenerated**.
- `IverilogCompileTest` and `GhdlCompileTest` accept the new goldens, with their output recorded — the external oracle is what makes "honestly" checkable rather than asserted.

Pre-change red state to reproduce at pickup: `HdlModel.Direction.INOUT` does not compile, and a third `Pin` subclass does not compile.

---

### 4. Threats to validity carried forward

- **T1 — three of four ternaries converted.** Verilog and VHDL are the visible surfaces; the two `PcfEmitter` sites are easy to miss, and the result is a legal module with an unusable constraint file. The one-assertion-per-site structure exists for this.
- **T2 — an output-only pin with a second name.** Such an element passes the drive, conflict and round-trip assertions and fails **only** the disabled-readback one. That is why that assertion is load-bearing and is written first.
- **T3 — the goldens do not cover inout.** No existing fixture has a bidirectional port, so "the goldens did not move" proves the *no-inout* path is intact and **nothing** about the new path. New goldens plus the external compile oracles are the only evidence for the new path.
- **T4 — strength-model creep.** #341 owns driver kinds, pull elements and the lattice. A diff that starts adding strengths here is out of scope. (This matches §4 invariant 7 of this issue and gives it a concrete tripwire.)
- **T5 — stale line numbers.** All citations pinned to `2d0ca9d`. Landmark anchors for re-derivation: `permits InputPin, OutputPin {`, `/** Port direction. */`, `/** Element classes with a direct HDL rendering. */`, and the importer string `is an inout (tri-state bus)`.

**Falsification moves.** If widening `permits` is not sufficient (some exhaustive switch over `Pin` the compiler does not flag), find every switch over the pin hierarchy, make each total, and **report the count — it changes the shape of the work**. If a `default`-less switch still compiles with an unhandled constant, the site is a statement switch rather than an expression switch: convert it, or add an explicit `throw` arm and record why the compiler could not help. If a disabled pin does not read the resolved net value, either the pin is not a `TriProp` participant or its `Input` is not on the same net as its `Output` — fix the element, **do not** modify `docs/simulation-semantics.md` §9. If the element cannot be written so a later lattice changes only resolution, record precisely what couples it to two-state resolution and report it on #341, because it becomes scope there.

---

### 5. Materials

**Existing and sufficient:** the tri-state substrate and its tests (`SimulationSemanticsRegressionTest`, `VcdExportGoldenTest.testVectorStimulusVcdMatchesGoldenAndCoversHiZ`), `HdlPolicyTest`, `PcfGoldenTest` and `blinky_icestick.pcf`, `NetlistImporterTest`, `AllElementsRoundTripTest`, `CapabilityInterfaceTest`, `IverilogCompileTest`, `GhdlCompileTest`, `ElementRegistry`, `Palette`.

**Must be built:** `src/jls/elem/InoutPin.java` plus its renderer and dialog; `test/jls/elem/InoutPinTest.java`; `test/jls/hdl/InoutPortExportTest.java`.

**JDK dependency:** JDK 25 sealed classes and exhaustive switch expressions — the whole mechanism depends specifically on a `default`-less switch over an enum being a compile error when a constant is unhandled.

---

### 6. Dependency edges #474 carried that this issue's machine block lacks

`related` here is `[59, 63, 264, 292, 315, 321, 322, 341, 359]`. #474 additionally carried, with its stated reason:

- **#387 (TASK-0058)** and **#391 (TASK-0057)** — under FEAT-027; they change the resolution function this element reads back through. **This work must not pre-empt either.**
- **#448 (TASK-0047)** — realize every cell the validator accepts. **#448 owns cell realization; this owns the inout *module port* refusal.** Adjacent, not overlapping.
- **#372 (TASK-0001)** — the registry-keyed-table inventory; the registration tax here is that ratchet working as designed.
- **#78** — element descriptor and registry; the shipped registry half is exactly what forces the registration tax.
- **#61** — this removes one of the importer's remaining structural refusals, **and does not close #61**. Likewise it gives #63's shipped scanner a consumer and **does not close #63**.

---

### 7. Open questions carried forward

1. **Is the enable an explicit drawn input, or derived from an attribute?** Recommended default: an explicit 1-bit enable input matching `TriState`'s shape, so a student sees the same idiom twice and no new concept is needed. The attribute alternative makes direction static per instance and **cannot express a bus turnaround**. **Blocks execution** — it is the element's shape.
2. **Default palette view now, or wait for a view dimension?** Recommended default: default view now, because an inout pin is logic-course material and #482 (TASK-0105)'s per-view palette is not a prerequisite. Rides along, but **say which was chosen so #482's palette-count ratchet expects to move by one**.
3. **Not open**, and recorded as settled: the readback substrate (§9 settles it), whether the export ratchet may be edited (no), and whether the three direction enums unify (no).

This issue's own Open Questions 2 (which constraint formats express bidirectional), 3 (per-instance output-enable vs structural) and 4 (format bump) are unaffected; #474 answers 4 in the negative for the new-element route and answers 1 as described above.

---

Adding one costs a registry row, a palette row and an export-policy row — **zero format version** by `docs/file-format.md`'s own rule.

### 2. The element's shape

`src/jls/elem/InoutPin.java` — `public final class InoutPin extends Pin implements TriProp`:

- **One `Input` put, one `Output` put, one 1-bit enable input.**
- Enable non-zero → the `Output` drives the pin's value onto the net after `propDelay`. Enable zero → the `Output` drives `null` (HiZ) and the `Input` reads the net's **resolved** value. Both halves are existing `TriState.react` semantics applied to a pin.
