## Boundary note: #353 / #354 (feature deduplication, pass 1)

Adjudicated together in pass 1 because both read as "long runs stop falling over." **Verdict: no merge (rule 3c) — one is complexity, the other is capacity and control flow, and they are already correctly ordered.**

**#353 (this issue) is about cost.** Three superlinear sites with re-derived anchors: `SigSim.initSim`'s per-token and per-line string concatenation, the $O(\text{signals} \times \text{elements})$ signal-name scan, `Circuit.finishLoad`'s $O(W^2)$ identity removal from a `LinkedList`, and `BatchSimulator.toVcd()` materializing the entire dump three times over at peak. Its gate is a scaling curve plus **byte-identity of every waveform golden** — the value of the computation is explicitly unchanged ($P_{\text{after}} = P_{\text{before}}$), only its cost.

**#354 is about ceilings and supervision.** Four sites that are not slow at all: `defaultTimeLimit = 100000000` with no `NO_TIME_LIMIT` sentinel, `pause(boolean)` being byte-for-byte identical to `stop()`, an event dropped from `dupCheck` before the limit test (a possible **correctness** defect, which is why TASK-0011 is an adjudication before it is a fix), and `DENSE_CAPACITY_LIMIT` meeting the 16 MiB guest-RAM figure with zero headroom. Its gate is a run that exceeds `defaultTimeLimit`, is paused and resumed byte-identically, and survives SIGINT with a parseable transcript.

**The two are complementary, and the corpus already says so in both directions.** #353 `blocks: [… 354]` with the reason stated verbatim — *"a long run is not expressible while the stimulus parse is quadratic and the dump is materialized: raising the time limit without fixing those converts a fast failure into a slow one"* — and #354 carries the mirror `blocked_by: [353]`. Each issue also names the other in its out-of-scope list. That is a mirrored ordering edge between distinct outcomes, which is exactly the shape rule 3 protects; merging them would collapse a prerequisite into its dependent and lose the "fast failure vs slow failure" argument that motivates the ordering.

**Non-overlapping files, for the record:** #353 touches `SigSim.java` (parse), `Circuit.java` (`finishLoad`), `BatchSimulator.java` (the dump path) and `HdlExporter.java`. #354 touches `Simulator.java` (the event loop, the sentinel, `beforeEvent`), `BatchSimulator.java` (`pause`/`stop`), `JLSStart.java` (flags, shutdown hook) and `Memory.java` (the byte budget). The single shared file is `BatchSimulator.java`, at disjoint methods.

## Boundary note: #353 / #350

Related but further apart: #350 (FEAT-057) distributes **many whole runs** across cores or hosts. It consumes the batch surface unmodified and needs no change to any of this issue's three sites; making one run cheaper (#353) and running many runs at once (#350) are independent axes. No ordering edge is declared between them and none is implied.

§2's decomposition table marks both children **Not filed**, and `planned_tasks` carries them as prose scope statements rather than issue references. Re-derived by title search:

| Roster row | Filed as | State |

### 2. This feature is NOT a duplicate of #75, #76 or #73 — recorded rather than merged

This issue's Abstract, its §1 *"Related issues"* and its Completion Criteria all state that it **closes** #75, #76 and #73. That phrasing invites a later pass to read it as a merge candidate. It is not one, under rule 3, and the reasoning is worth having on the record so it is not re-litigated:

- **Merging any of them into this issue violates lower-number-wins.** #73, #75 and #76 are all lower than #355.
- **Merging this issue into any one of them destroys the other two.** This is a *three-way* residual: #75's assistive-tech pass, #76's dark variant and scaling matrix, and #73's welcome state and samples, re-cut by **verification substrate** rather than by lineage — §2 says so explicitly and records rejecting "one task per originating issue (#75, #76, #73)" as the wrong shape, because #76's dark variant and #73's welcome state share the same `Theme`/`UserPrefs` plumbing and the same screenshot evidence while #75's residual shares nothing with either. **What this leaves open is a disposition, not a merge.** This issue's own Completion Criteria already name it: *"#75, #76 and #73 each either closed or updated with the scope this feature did not absorb."* That is a maintainer action and it is currently unperformed — all three remain open `tier:feature` issues with their own bodies, while #380 and #381 implement their residuals under this feature. **The hazard is double-filing**, and it is already live: pass 1 recorded on [#73](https://github.com/anadon/JLS/issues/73#issuecomment-5175804376) that #73's `planned_tasks` are unfiled while **#381, #545, #548, #550 and #552 all declare they consume them**. - **vs. #334 (FEAT-003).** #334 delivers the *reviewable artifact* — canonical plain text plus references that name their referent — with a diff ratchet and `sha256sum` == `Circuit.stateHash()` as acceptance. #356 decides which *merged results of that artifact* are legal at all, with a nine-row merge-safety matrix and totality over record kinds as acceptance. **#334 blocks #356** (mirrored), and the two share **TASK-0005** (now filed as **#436**), which is one task claimed by two rosters — rule 3(b), a shared prerequisite, never a shared outcome. 5227479126.body:
ROSTER ADDITION (round-2 chain check) — a parentless task attached to this feature.

**What happened.** **#491** (*`ElementId.parse` never advances the creation counter, so the second run of one install saves a circuit JLS then refuses to open*) is `tier:task` with `part_of_feature: none`. Nothing in the tier walk reached it, despite it being a data-loss-class defect with a reproducer.

**Adopted roster addition: #491**, given the matching `part_of_feature: 356` correction.

**Why here.** `ElementId` is the permanent-identity mechanism the stable-id discipline rests on, and this feature depends on it more sharply than any other: merge safety is vacuous if two elements from two sessions of one install can collide, or if an id can be minted that the loader will not accept back. It sits beside **#436 (TASK-0005)** — every reference naming a permanent id instead of a save-time position — and **#409 (TASK-0031)** — a file that parses but is structurally corrupt reported by name, which this defect currently evades by failing as a plain load error rather than a named structural report.

**Stated as a judgement, not a claim about the body.** #491 declares no parent at all, so this is an assignment. The alternatives considered were **#334** (FEAT-003, reviewable text artifact) and **#319** (FEAT-013, per-section versioning); I chose this feature because the failure is about identity uniqueness and round-trip acceptance rather than diff size or section-version negotiation. If the maintainer prefers #334, re-point by `REPLAN:` rather than filing a second issue.

**Two consequences:**

1. **Do not read `part_of_feature: 356` as `blocked_by: 356`.** #491 is a shipped bug that should land well ahead of this feature. Roster membership is a reachability fact, not a schedule.
2. **#491 and #436 must agree on what a valid `ElementId` is, before either lands.** The round-1 pass resolved #436 by making the `id` base attribute conditional on the reference form — a format-level decision. Any change to how ids are minted or parsed has to be made once, consistently with that, not twice. That coordination is recorded on both issues; note that #436's resolution was flagged for maintainer ratification with **#319** in the room, since #319 owns format-epoch policy.

5170941279.body:
`REPLAN:` **Considered as the owner of D15's import-to-subcircuit scope and NOT chosen. No change to this issue's body, roster, band or edges — recorded here so the question is not re-opened.**

**The ruling, verbatim** (`docs/plan/evidence/BRIEF.md`, section 14, landmark heading `### D15. The guest image is a FILE. Files require import-to-subcircuit.`):

> **File. Files will also require 'import to subcircuit' to nest systems.**

The second sentence is a scope addition: a system carried as a file must be nestable inside another design as a subcircuit, or files compose only at the top level. This issue was one of three candidates for owning it (with #340 FEAT-016 and #319 FEAT-013). **It landed on #340**, for three reasons taken on the merits:

1. **Subject.** This issue's own scope boundary hands "definition identity itself — the digest, the version strings, the library container and its provenance" to #340, and says an instance's reference "resolves *against* it and this feature does not mint it". A cross-**file** reference is resolved by identity, which is #340's subject.
2. **Demonstrability.** This feature's observable capability is stated intra-file — "a file containing N instances of one definition serializes the definition **once**" — and lands complete with every definition still inside one file. An import-to-subcircuit row here would be the one item no other part of the feature needs.
3. **Cost visibility.** This issue already carries a band of 25–36 mw against 4 wk of named task rows, which its own Cost section calls "the largest such gap in the plan". Adding a new row into that gap is the one place in the plan where a new cost would be least visible — and D15's scope must not be absorbed silently. This is a statement about *where a cost can be seen*, not about whether the work is wanted.

**What this feature does contribute, recorded on #340 rather than claimed here:** once the definition/instance split lands, a file imported N times resolves to **one** shared definition instead of N independent references each elaborating separately. That is a real compounding benefit and it is why the existing ordering edge — `#340 blocks #357`, mirrored in this issue's `blocked_by: [318, 319, 340]` — is the right direction and **does not move**. No edge is added, removed or reversed by this ruling on either side.

**Nothing on this issue changes.** No new scope row, no re-priced band (25–36 mw stands), no machine-block edit. See the REPLAN on #340 for the capability statement, the observable criteria, the new open question about reference resolution, and the 3–6 mw price with its basis; and the REPLANs on #301 and #343 for the first half of D15 (the guest image is a sidecar file with a recorded digest).

5227549143.body:
## Re-ranked as competitive parity, not only CAP-02 spine — discharging #510 row 39

**Completeness review, 2026-08-08.** #510's gap→owner table assigns *"subcircuit parameterization / library catalog (Digital generics, Issie v6)"* to this feature and #447, and attaches a directive that was never carried out:

> *"adversarial phase should re-rank it as competitive parity, not only CAP-02 spine."*

That phase has run. **The re-rank is adopted.** This comment records it; nothing in this feature's scope, criteria or roster changes.

### What changes is why this feature is scheduled

This feature's chain is healthy — #447 (one definition stored once, N instances with bound parameters) and #473 (one elaboration pass, every unresolvable binding a coded diagnostic naming the instance path) are both open with `part_of_feature: 357`. What was wrong was the *reason* a scheduler would reach for it. Read as CAP-02 infrastructure, this is a storage-efficiency improvement on the path to booting Linux on a drawn CPU — a long-dated capstone. That framing is what the survey is correcting.

**The competitive reading, from #510's own evidence:**

- The score matrix puts JLS at **2/5 on hierarchy/reuse**, against Digital at 5 and Issie at 5. It is JLS's equal-worst dimension alongside learning on-ramp and scale/perf, and unlike those two it is not a presentation problem.
- §3's **Digital row lists parameterization in the minimum bar** for winning their users — in the same clause as the .dig importer and FSM/synthesis parity, not in a later tier. The successor play named in §5 depends on it.
- §2 names it explicitly as a place JLS *loses today*: *"no parameterization vs Digital's generics and Issie v6's parameter/library catalog."*
- Issie v6's parameter/library model is called out in §3 as an idea to steal outright.

So the scheduling weight comes from row 39 and the Digital verdict, and it does not wait on CAP-02 being scheduled. **This feature is worth landing even if CAP-02 is never funded** — that is the substance of the re-rank, and it was not previously written anywhere.

### One consequence a scheduler should see

#510 row 39's second half is the **library catalog**, which is #340 (FEAT-016: a subcircuit definition has an identity that means something outside the file it lives in) and its task #446. Parameterization and the distributable library are one competitive story in Digital's and Issie's telling, and two features here. Neither is blocked on the other, but landing #357 alone answers half of what the row describes — worth knowing before this feature is scheduled as if it closed the gap by itself.

Also unchanged and worth restating so it is not re-litigated: the premise this feature rests on was independently verified against master earlier today — `SubCircuit.save` calls `getSubCircuit().save(output)` inside each element's own block, so N instances really do write N full copies of the definition. The problem is real and is measured, not assumed.

5181347234.justification: Defends keeping #385 and #384 separate with 'No merge performed. Both issues stay open.' This intermediate planning position was explicitly overruled later the same day (2026-08-08) by comment 5227280109, which closes both as duplicates of #292. The current body reflects the later decision.
5181347234.body:
## Boundary with #385 (feature/task deduplication pass) — NOT a duplicate

#385 (TASK-0043) was carried into this pass as a near-verbatim duplicate candidate: this feature's title clause *"the HDL IR carries more than one module and an instantiation statement"* is almost exactly #385's title, *"the HDL IR gains an instantiation statement and more than one module, and the exporter walks the subcircuit hierarchy instead of refusing it."*

**The title match is real; the outcome match is not.** This feature's §2 roster has **two** entries and this comment records the boundary rather than merging.

`#358 = #385 (TASK-0043) + #384 (TASK-0044)`

- **#385 — TASK-0043.** The IR instantiation statement carrying legalized module name, legalized instance name and ordered port bindings; the multi-module design container; the recursive hierarchy walk with cycle detection; port-to-net binding; reject propagation carrying the instance path.
- **#384 — TASK-0044.** *"Both HDL printers render module instantiation, and the hierarchical goldens compile under iverilog and analyze under ghdl with no new skip."* Verilog named-port instantiation and VHDL component-declaration-plus-port-map, with committed hierarchical goldens cross-checked against the external compilers.

This feature's own Abstract states the pair is not separable in outcome: *"No single child delivers this: the IR statement without the printers is unobservable, and the printers without the IR statement have nothing to print."* That is the definition of a union of slices, not a duplicate — the second half is the observable half.

The §6 critical path also treats the edge as **necessity, not convention**: adding the statement to a sealed visitor breaks both emitters until they handle it, so the two land in one branch. A scheduler cannot parallelise them; that coupling is why #384 exists as its own issue with its own external-compiler evidence, and why absorbing #385 here would have silently orphaned the rendering half.

**Both issues stay open with their scope intact.** Beyond the two children, this feature retains integration criteria no child asserts alone: the deep-fixture deterministic-uniquification test (≥4 levels, two instances of one circuit at different paths, byte-identical across runs, every emitted module identifier distinct), the nesting-cycle path report, reject propagation carrying the instance path, simulation parity on shared stimulus, and the reject-list entry's removal with its policy test re-pointed rather than deleted.

### Related: #292's ownership is still undecided

This feature's Related section already records that **#292** (*HDL export: hierarchical SubCircuit — module per subcircuit type with instantiation, lifting the reject-list entry*) is *"the same scope as TASK-0043 + TASK-0044, already filed at task tier."* #292's machine block reads `part_of_feature: 59`, which is not an open tier:feature — see the separate note posted on #292. With #385 and #384 now both filed, the roster question this feature's DoD raises (*"#292's ownership resolved by a recorded decision"*) is sharper, not softer: three task issues now claim overlapping scope, and Open Question 1 (uniquified vs deduplicated) is the axis that separates them. That reconciliation is deliberately **not** made here — it needs the maintainer's answer to Open Question 1, which this feature says must be answered on both issues in the same breath.

This intermediate analysis was reversed hours later by comment 5227280109 (17:29 UTC) on the same day, which closes #385/#384 as duplicates of #292. The current body reflects the later decision.
5226960892.body:
## Boundary with #385 — overlapping, NOT a duplicate (feature/task deduplication)

#385 (TASK-0043) was flagged as a duplicate candidate of this feature: the title clause *"the HDL IR carries more than one module and an instantiation statement"* is verbatim in *"the HDL IR gains an instantiation statement and more than one module"*. **Examined and declined.** #385 is the IR-and-walk half of a two-task roster; #384 (TASK-0044) is the printers-and-goldens half. That is the intended hierarchy.

**The evidence.** #385 §1 opens *"#358 carries the capability statement, the uniquified-versus-deduplicated decision, the cost basis and the five serving capstones; none of that is restated here."* Its §13 lists as out of scope *"the two printers and their goldens (TASK-0044)"*. Most decisively, #385 §11 states *"`mvn verify` **cannot be green for this task alone**"* and its §14 requires the combined branch run — because adding a twelfth arm to the sealed `StatementVisitor` stops both emitters compiling until #384 handles it. A task that cannot produce a green build by itself has not delivered this feature's outcome: *a decomposed design exports*.

**The line:**

| owner | scope |
|---|---|
| **#385** (TASK-0043) | `HdlModel.InstanceStatement` + the `StatementVisitor` arm; `HdlDesign`; `HdlEmitter.emit(HdlDesign)` as a default method; `buildModel` → `buildDesign`; port binding through the existing `groupOf` path; per-module `HdlNames` scopes plus a design-level module-name scope; cycle detection with a named path; reject propagation as a fold carrying the instance path; moving `SubCircuit` from `REJECTED` to `EXPORTED`. |
| **#384** (TASK-0044) | Verilog named-port instantiation and VHDL component-declaration-plus-port-map rendering, with committed hierarchical goldens that compile under `iverilog` and analyze under `ghdl` with no new skip. |
| **#358** (this issue) | The five §5 integration criteria none of the children assert alone — a compiling artifact from a drawn circuit (criterion 1), **deep-fixture determinism at four-plus levels with two instances of the same circuit at different paths** (criterion 2, named as the criterion the identifier legalizer is most likely to fail), the cycle-path report (3), instance-path reject propagation (4), and simulation parity on shared stimulus (5). Plus Open Question 1 (uniquified vs deduplicated), the cost basis and the five serving capstones. |

The two tasks land in **one branch by necessity**, not by convention — a scheduler cannot parallelise them and should not try. That compile-time coupling is exactly what makes them two slices of one feature rather than one issue filed twice.

**#385's measurements and rules worth holding at this level:**

- **The `REJECTED` map is `Map.of`, capped at ten pairs**, and lives at `HdlExporter.java:460-477` (the planning corpus says `:461-478` — corrected at `2d0ca9d`). Removing an entry is free, but a later author adding past ten gets a compile error with an unhelpful message.
- **Synthesized net names are per-`CIRCUIT`-block dense** (`HdlExporter.java:353` derives `net_` from `el.getID()`), so **two modules will both contain `net_3`** — the collision criterion 2's fixture needs is guaranteed, not hypothetical. A test that passes because two modules happened not to collide certifies nothing. **Net-name derivation is not touched here; TASK-0008 owns that.**
- **The natural implementation loses the instance path.** Catching and re-throwing per level is the obvious way to write the walk and is exactly what destroys criterion 4. `model.addWarning` messages must carry the path too — today they name the element only, so two `Display`s in two instances produce two identical warnings.
- **Jump aliasing must be asserted circuit-scoped**: a `JumpStart` in a parent and one in a child with the same name are two nets. The fused-net `Group`/`UnionFind` at `HdlExporter.java:1146-1200` is built once per walk, which gives each definition its own — correct, but unpinned.
- **A `Clock` inside a subcircuit** gains a synthesized `clk` port its parent must drive; leaving it unbound produces a module that **analyzes and does not run**, which a green external-compiler check would not catch. This issue's Open Question 3 owns it and #385 marks it as blocking execution.
- **`subCircuitIsRejectedCleanly` (`HdlPolicyTest.java:82`) is replaced, not deleted** — removing a policy assertion instead of re-pointing it is how a policy silently stops being tested. `exportPolicyIsTotalOverTheElementRegistry` (`:392`) must keep passing **unchanged**, which is the proof the policy stayed total while an entry moved buckets.
- **#315 is `related`, not `blocked_by`, on #385** — re-derived rather than inherited: at `2d0ca9d` the rejected bucket is already pinned total by `HdlPolicyTest:392` (added by `b54e6ee` for exactly this purpose), and FEAT-001's residual is an inventory and a standing lint that #385 does not read. This issue keeps the edge; the divergence is deliberate and recorded on both sides.

No merge performed. Both issues stay open. **Separately, see the #292 ownership question** — that is a live task-vs-task overlap flagged by both this issue and #385, recorded in a boundary comment on #292.

5227611264.justification: Bot-generated amendment documentation folded into body and explicitly superseded; all content (kernel design, task roster, beneficiary, invariants) is absorbed into body sections; no genuine discussion or decision trail
5227611264.body:
## Amendment — kernel ops restated over intervals; bridge element added; new beneficiary

Source: **PR #887** (`nary-01` §§4, 7, `nary-03` §3), maintainer design discussion 2026-08-08. Amend in place — the element-family shape survives.

### Kept unchanged

The element family shape; the coverage-batch discipline; the **TASK-0105 palette-view prerequisite** (it must land first so the default palette is unchanged); the default-palette invariant; export lowering with the encoding named in the emitted header; the radix manifest; the `-t` token-rewrite pre-pass.

### Amendments

1. **Kernel ops restated over intervals** (`nary-01` §4). The only structure the kernel uses is the integer **ordering** of the interval:
   - `min(a,b)` / `max(a,b)` — MVL conjunction/disjunction (Łukasiewicz/Post style).
   - `reflect(v) = lo + hi - v` — complement by reflection. At `[0,1]` this is NOT; at `[-1,+1]` it is balanced-ternary negation.
   - `cycle(v, k)` — cyclic successor, wrapping within `[lo, hi]`.
   - `literal(v, [a,b])` — Allen–Givone interval literal: `hi` if `a ≤ v ≤ b`, else `lo`.
   - equality/comparison over values, X-propagating.

   Each collapses **exactly** to today's binary operation at `[0,1]` — the bit-for-bit identity this issue's invariant 3 already requires, which is what lets the kernel be adopted without moving a golden. Arithmetic beyond this (adders with carry, saturating vs wrapping) is **element-level**, and each arithmetic element states its own semantics.

2. **Balanced ternary becomes the native `[-1,+1]` interval**, not a rendering over `{0,1,2}`. Balanced *rendering* (`-`, `0`, `+`) stays, now as the natural display rather than a translation layer.

3. **Bundle numerals.** A width-`w` bundle over `[lo,hi]` reads as `sum(v_i * N^i)`. Because the digit set is `N` consecutive integers this is injective (a shifted base-`N` system; classical balanced-radix for symmetric intervals). One rule gives display, `-t` literals and `Constant` values a well-defined signed interpretation for every interval, with two's-complement display remaining a *presentation* option at `[0,1]` exactly as today.

4. **New element: the bridge** (generalized Splitter/Binder across alphabets). Converts between `(interval A, width w)` and `(interval B, width u)` bundles whose numeral ranges are compatible — one `[0,255]` digit ↔ eight `[0,1]` digits; a `[-1,+1]`-width-5 bundle ↔ its binary encoding. X/Z on any consumed position makes the affected produced positions X. **This is what makes mixed-alphabet drawings compose** and what keeps large-N bus-as-symbol wires usable next to gate-level logic. Add to the family roster.

5. **Large-N notes.** `TruthTable` is `N^inputs` rows and **refuses above a stated budget with the arithmetic printed**; `Display` renders any N; `Constant` is interval-aware. `Splitter`/`Binder` subset positions of a bundle with the interval preserved; **`Extend`'s replication stays binary-only** until a signed-extension semantics is decided (open question 3 on #888).

6. **TASK-0083 (the CAP-03 drawn-CPU census) is dropped or re-homed.** CAP-03 (#295) is closed and stays closed. The element roster's completeness census is now defined by **CAP-39 (#888)'s walkthrough** — a mixed-alphabet drawing, not a drawn CPU. If TASK-0083 carries anything the new walkthrough needs, re-home that content; otherwise drop it.

7. **New beneficiary: CAP-39 (#888).** Add to `serves_capstones`, resolving the dangling-beneficiary state #295's closure left.

### Unchanged and load-bearing

**Invariant 1 stands: no existing element type gains an interval attribute.** Every pre-existing type reports `[0,1]`, asserted over the registry. New capability arrives as **new element types, default-hidden in the palette**. A binary user's correct experience of this entire feature is that nothing happened.

5227396593.body:
## REPLAN: the roster is stale, one planned task no longer exists, the link pass never ran, every evidence citation resolves to a deleted branch, and § 6's parallelism claim is contradicted by a document on master

Sim-engine adversarial review, 2026-08-08. This comment supersedes the `planned_tasks` block, the § 2 Decomposition table's Status column, the § 6 Sequencing paragraph on parallelism, and the "Basis for the band" citations at the end of § Cost. § 1's scope boundary, § 4's invariants and K3 stand unchanged.

### 1. The roster — every task is filed, and the table says none is

§ 2's Status column reads "planned / not yet filed" for all five. Four have been filed since:

| body's name | filed as | state |
|---|---|---|
| TASK-0023 | **#379** | open |
| TASK-0026 | **#442** | open |
| TASK-0063 | **#476** | open |
| TASK-0064 | **#393** | open |
| TASK-0056 | **does not exist — see below** | — |

### 2. TASK-0056 is dead and this feature's critical path points at nothing

**#475 (TASK-0056) was closed 2026-08-08 as a duplicate of #232.** The value-representation leg is owned by **#232** (`tier:feature`), whose contract absorbed #475's in full. #232 had zero filed children; the same review has now filed them:

- **#878 — TASK-C232-1**: the immutable width-carrying value type lands in `jls.core`, nothing else changes.
- **#879 — TASK-C232-2**: the plumbing widens, the 61 clones are deleted, the golden corpus is byte-identical, the k2000 gate is measured.

**Read `planned_tasks`' "TASK-0056" as #878 → #879 from now on**, and § 6's "two agents can run TASK-0056 and TASK-0063 concurrently" as being about #878/#879 and #476 — subject to § 4 below, which disputes the concurrency itself.

### 3. The link pass named in the LINK PASS note never reached the task tier

The note of 2026-08-02 records ordering edges written with both mirrors at the *feature* tier. The task tier was never done, and the tasks say so themselves:

- **#393** carries `blocked_by: []` with the body text *"Three sibling tasks are being filed concurrently … A link pass adds all three edges."* The edges were never added.
- **#476** carries `blocked_by: [410]` only — #442's byte-identity gate, which § 6 of this issue calls **necessity under K3**, is absent from its machine block.

So this feature's declared critical path — TASK-0023 → TASK-0026 → TASK-0063 → TASK-0064 — **exists only in this issue's prose**. Every task in it is independently pickable today, and a scheduler reading machine blocks would run them in any order. The corrected edges, mirrored onto each endpoint by this review:

- **#379 → #442** — necessity: the bands need measured denominators.
- **#442 → #476**, **#442 → #393**, **#442 → #879** — necessity under K3: the byte-identity gate decides whether each change may land. Landing a speedup and then building the gate that would have rejected it inverts the safety argument.
- **#476 → #393** — necessity: the closure's marker *is* #476's intrusive flag, and measuring the closure against the priority queue attributes the queue's cost to the closure.
- **#410 → #476** — already declared on #476, and correct: the calendar queue must encode the past-limit behaviour and cannot encode an unadjudicated one.

### 4. § 6's parallelism claim is contradicted by a document on master, and the contradiction is mechanism-dependent

§ 6 states: *"TASK-0056 is independent of TASK-0063 and TASK-0064 — it touches the value plumbing and the react bodies, they touch `jls.sim`. Two agents can run TASK-0056 and TASK-0063 concurrently."*

`docs/capability-roadmap/keystone-c-performance.md` § 7.2, on master, says the opposite, twice:

> **Replace the global `dupCheck` with per-element pending-event slots** … **Sequence this after the value type lands**, because an immutable value with a cached hash makes the interim cost bearable and because the new coalescing rule wants to compare values, not events.

> **Levelize the zero-delay plane.** Wants (3) done and the value type landed.

and its revised sequence table places the value type at stage 0, the dedup replacement at stage 0.5, the zero-delay closure at stage 1.

**Do not resolve this by picking the document you like.** The two are not disagreeing about scheduling; they are describing **two different mechanisms**:

- **#476's mechanism** is a time-bucketed calendar queue plus an intrusive queued flag reached from the `(callBack, todo)` identity. It never inspects a value, so it genuinely is independent of the value leg — § 6's claim is sound *for that design*.
- **keystone-c's mechanism** is per-element pending-event slots extending the `toBeValue` pattern that `Gate.react` and `TriState.react` already use, whose coalescing rule **compares values**. That one is not independent of the value leg at all.

**#476 does not cite keystone-c's alternative anywhere**, and its Open Question 1 ("bucket store shape") offers three variants of the calendar queue and not the in-tree recommendation. **The mechanism decision is upstream of the ordering decision and is currently unmade.** § 6's "every edge above is load-bearing" is therefore not true today: one of them is conditional on a choice nobody has recorded. Recorded on #476 as a blocking open question.

5175750535.body:
Boundary note vs #523 (feature deduplication, pass 1) — **overlap, not a duplicate; no merge.**

#523 (*FEAT-C05-1: the netlist KiCad receives is provably the circuit JLS simulated — a stable-id net-partition isomorphism gates the export*) was adjudicated against this issue in the deduplication pass. Both concern "a gated netlist export a real PCB tool accepts", so the pair was seated together deliberately. They are **not** the same outcome, and the boundary is:

- **This issue owns the artifact and its buildability gate.** Emit a schematic and a netlist a real PCB tool opens without hand editing (TASK-0085 package schema and footprint binding, TASK-0089 netlist emitter, TASK-0090 schematic emitter), plus TASK-0091's manufacturability gate answering *"can this be built"* per named rule. Its § 5 criteria assert import with zero hand editing, byte determinism across platforms, pin order against a published pinout, disposition totality over the element registry, and that the gate refuses before the artifact is written.
- **#523 owns one proof obligation over that artifact.** A standing headless `NetPartitionIsomorphismTest` that **re-parses the emitted `.net` from the file bytes**, induces a partition over `(refdes, pin)`, and compares it to the one shared partition JLS simulated from, **matched by stable id, not by name string** — plus the discipline of narrowing the parity claim in writing wherever the isomorphism cannot be proven. It turns *"it exported"* into *"it exported the circuit I simulated"*.

**Why this is not a merge under rule 3.** #523 is a narrower slice with distinct acceptance criteria (3(a)) and it sits **downstream** of this issue, not beside it: its machine block reads `ordering_after: [336, 365, 366]`, consuming this issue's emitted artifact as the far side of the comparison. #523's own Outcome section states the gap it fills against this issue explicitly — *"#366's evidence plan asserts import, byte determinism, pin order and the gate, but not the partition comparison; TASK-0089's golden is a byte comparison, which cannot distinguish a structurally wrong netlist from a right one once the golden itself is wrong."* That is a real coverage gap, not a restatement: a byte golden and a partition isomorphism fail on different defects. Merging would destroy the distinction and re-open the gap.

Three coupling points to keep in view rather than let drift:

1. **#523's criterion 3 depends on where the cascade rule lives.** The synthetic inter-slice nets #365's cascade creates must appear in **both** partitions, which holds only while the cascade rule lives in the shared IR. If that rule migrates into an emitter owned here, #523's check stops being well-defined and its KC-05-2 fires — and per #523 the isomorphism *"is never weakened to an approximate match to accommodate an emitter-side rule."* This issue's § 4 invariant 1 ("no fourth copy of the net partition") is the same constraint from the other side.
2. **The route decision belongs to CAP-13 (#307).** #523 records that #307's G-1 embedded-symbol falsification and the schematic-vs-netlist route decision ride with **this** issue (its Open Question 1 and § 6), not with #523. So the embedded-symbol premise — the afternoon's work in § 6 — stays here.
3. **The readback direction has no owner.** #523 explicitly excludes it (#307's claim 3: a KiCad `.net` read back into JLS with a migration report enumerating every unmapped construct), and this issue carries no reader task, so **neither issue owns the reader half**. When readback is scheduled its partition must equal #523's check's, per #307's AC-3. Recorded here so it is not assumed covered.

No content was migrated in either direction and neither issue closes on account of the other.

5175958918.body:
## Boundary note vs #368 (feature deduplication, pass 1)

Examined as a duplicate candidate against **#368 (FEAT-048, A2D/D2A bridges and A-STEP synchronization)** and found **distinct — not merged**.

**Why they look like duplicates.** Both introduce a notion of physical time into a tree whose `docs/simulation-semantics.md:26` is normative that simulation time is dimensionless, and #368's headline promises "an exact crossing time," which sounds like it requires this issue's declared unit.

**Why they are not.**

- **#367 (this issue) is a declaration and a conversion.** One optional per-circuit `TimeBase` record in `jls.core` carrying the waveform standard's `$timescale` grammar, a rejecting parse, a non-accumulating `seconds(ticks)`, the version-refusal policy, and the normative documentation amendment. Its acceptance is a tree-wide *negative* — every existing golden byte-identical when nothing is declared — plus the `2^53` exactness assertion and the one-conversion-tree-wide grep. It changes no semantics.
- **#368 is a crossing mechanism and a domain alphabet.** Two one-bit bridge elements with thresholds, hysteresis and a publication-delay floor; the ownership inversion that makes the event loop own time so no rollback machinery is needed; the three step-cap regimes; and the port/net domain descriptor with its four unconditional enforcement sites above the width check (`SimpleEditor.java:4014, :4141, :4246, :4357`, defeating the zero-bits rule at `Put.java:34`).

**#368's exact crossing time does not actually consume this issue.** Its § 3 defines the published transition as `t* = min{ t ∈ ℤ ∩ [t₀,t₁] : v(t) ≥ V_hi }` — located by bisection and **terminated by the integer tick lattice**, not by a declared physical unit. That is why #368's `blocked_by` is `[331, 351]` and does **not** name #367, and why this issue's `blocked_by`/`blocks` are both empty as a recorded Link-phase finding rather than a deferral. The relationship is 3(c): adjacent features in one programme with different outcomes and no ordering edge between them.

**What is real, and is already written down here.** This issue's § 1 names FEAT-046 (#351) and FEAT-045 (#346) as *consumers* of the declared time base, and the residual row is exactly "carrying the declared unit through every consumer that reports time," including the solver step and the sample rate. #368's bridges would become such a consumer if a bridge's publication delay is ever stated in seconds — but that is the residual's sweep, not a merge, and § 2 records why folding this attribute into a larger programme is the failure mode: "a cheap, high-leverage declaration gets priced as an order-of-magnitude-larger change and therefore never lands."

**Related but separate consumers of this issue in the same cluster:** #486 (FEAT-058) carries `blocked_by: [367, 336, 319]` and #490 (FEAT-059) carries `blocked_by: [487, 367]`, both because a critical length multiplies a time by a velocity and a `Td` of 345.6 ps is a number in seconds. Those are prerequisite edges, not overlaps.

No content migrated; both issues stand as filed.

5181525358.body:
## Absorbing #431 (feature/task deduplication)

#431 (TASK-0101, `tier:task`) is this feature's **sole planned child** and its own machine block says so: `part_of_feature: 367 # FEAT-047 — this IS the feature's substance: the declared unit and the recompute-from-integer rule`. The two own the same outcome — one optional per-circuit time base, VCD's own `$timescale` grammar, a conversion recomputed from the integer tick with no accumulating field, a mandatory version bump, and byte-identical behaviour when nothing is declared. Per the lower-number-wins rule, **#367 survives** and #431 is absorbed.

**Tier consequence — a later pass must act on this.** Survivor is `tier:feature`, absorbed is `tier:task`. After closure this feature has **no filed child** while `planned_tasks` still names TASK-0101. Either relabel this issue `tier:task` and execute from the contract below, or file a fresh task carrying this comment verbatim. Do not leave the roster naming a child that does not exist.

**The residual is unaffected and stays here.** This feature's second roster row — carrying the declared unit through consumers that do not exist yet (the analog solver's step in #351, the audio sample rate in #346) — was never #431's and remains this issue's, along with §5's tree-wide golden sweep and the one-conversion-tree-wide grep. That residual is exactly why the 2-3 mw band exceeds TASK-0101's 1.5 wk row, and Open Question 5 still owns the gap.

---

### Scope carried forward from #431 (everything this issue did not already state)

**The loader trap — the observed failure, and the reason the version bump is mandatory rather than optional.** `Circuit.loadCircuit`'s token loop (`src/jls/Circuit.java:886-900` at `2d0ca9d`) accepts exactly `ELEMENT` or `ENDCIRCUIT` and calls `failLoad(MALFORMED, ...)` on anything else:

```java
                if (!str.equals("ELEMENT")) {
                    return failLoad(LoadError.Category.MALFORMED,
                            "expected ELEMENT or ENDCIRCUIT here, but "
                                    + "found '" + str + "'",
                            TRUNCATED_HINT);
                }
```

Measured, with `TIMEBASE 1ps` inserted after the `CIRCUIT` line of the tracked fixture `test/fixtures/headless-canary-gate.jls`:

```
load(TIMEBASE 1ps) = false
  category = MALFORMED
  message  = malformed file (line 2): expected ELEMENT or ENDCIRCUIT here, but found 'TIMEBASE'. The file may be truncated - recover from the .jls~ checkpoint or a backup, or re-save the circuit from a working copy.
jls.core.TimeBase ABSENT
```

**A version-2 reader given a `TIMEBASE` line reports *"not a JLS circuit"* — telling the user their file is corrupt — instead of *"needs a newer JLS"*. The `TIMEBASE` arm and the `FORMAT_VERSION` bump therefore land in the same commit.** This is a stronger and more concrete statement of §6's argument than this issue currently carries: the format's silently-ignore-unknown-*attributes* valve never even applies, because a circuit-level record is a change to the **block structure**, which `docs/file-format.md` §9's no-bump-needed list does not cover.

**The concrete type.** `src/jls/core/TimeBase.java`, a record `(int mult, Unit unit)` where `mult ∈ {1, 10, 100}` and `Unit ∈ {S, MS, US, NS, PS, FS}`. Methods: `parse(String)` (**rejects, never repairs** — a `.jls` file is hostile input, and an unrecognised magnitude or unit is a typed load error naming the token, not a coerced nearest value), `toString()` emitting the canonical `1ps` spelling, `exponent()`, and `seconds(long ticks)`. Immutable, therefore trivially thread-safe.

**`Circuit` gains a `@Nullable TimeBase timebase` field with accessors**, and the version predicate becomes

```
formatVersionNeeded(C) = max( max over elements saveVersion(e),  timebase(C) != null ? 3 : 1 )
```

against today's `formatVersionNeeded()` at `src/jls/Circuit.java:1580-1588`, which maxes element versions only. **That equation is the whole of the absent-by-default claim**: a circuit with no timebase yields the value it does today, and therefore the same bytes. `FORMAT_VERSION` moves 2 → 3 (`src/jls/Circuit.java:102`); the refusal path at `:765-770` is unchanged.

**The imported-circuit suppression rule — new, and load-bearing.** `src/jls/Circuit.java:1477-1484`:

```java
        if (subElement != null) {
            out.println("CIRCUIT " + subElement.getName());
        } else {
            out.println("FORMAT " + formatVersionNeeded());
            out.println("CIRCUIT " + name);
        }
```

A nested subcircuit never writes `FORMAT`; **`TIMEBASE` follows the same rule. One timebase per file, owned by the top level** — otherwise two subcircuits could declare different seconds for the same tick. A `TIMEBASE` line inside a nested subcircuit block is **refused by name**.

**`stateHash` hashes the saved text** (`src/jls/Circuit.java:1548`), so a circuit that gains a timebase changes its hash. That is correct and affects only opted-in files — but **`DeterministicSaveTest` and `CircuitRoundTripTest` must be read before relying on it**, because they encode assumptions about hash stability.

**The display seam.** `src/jls/edit/Trace.java:77-78` — `private int scaleFactor = 1;` ("simulation time units per pixel"), read by the tic labelling at `:263` (`int inc = TraceGeometry.ticIncrement(scaleFactor);`) and `:276`. **The stored delay attribute stays an integer tick count; only the label text changes.** Do **not** add a real-number delay attribute here — the optional real form stored as a scaled integer is a separate increment, and mixing it in doubles the format surface and the review.

**`jls.core` is policed from birth.** `test/jls/HeadlessCoreRatchetTest.java:74-79` lists `src/jls/core/` among `CORE_PACKAGE_PREFIXES` with `BASELINE = Set.of()` at `:90`. **`TimeBase` is born AWT-free and stays so, with no baseline entry available.**

**The `$timescale` spelling split.** VCD writes `$timescale 1 ps $end` with a space; the `.jls` record need not. Recommended: **`1ps` in the `.jls` file (no space, one token) and the VCD spelling in the dump**, with `toString()` emitting the former and the emitter formatting the latter.

**`docs/batch-interface.md` §6's stability promise blesses the additive `$timescale` change**, since a conforming consumer reading `1 ns` today keeps reading it for every circuit that declares nothing. `docs/file-format.md` §9's version history gains a `3:` row **stating the block-structure justification for the bump**.

**Prior-work correction.** `docs/capability-roadmap/sweep-02-timing.md` **Change F** is this work's written owner, pricing it at 2-3 mw as a P4 obligation of SDF, Liberty and SDC, **independent of any analog work**. The standards issues that work would unblock (SDF, Liberty, SDC) are cited in `sweep-02-timing.md` by number but **are not among the open issues — do not cite them as open.**

### Acceptance criteria carried forward from #431

Test names are load-bearing; keep them or record the rename.

- **`absentTimebaseSavesAndLoadsExactlyAsAtHead()`** — load **every** fixture in `test/fixtures/`, re-save, assert byte equality with the committed file **and** that the declared `FORMAT` version did not change. The load-bearing negative.
- **`aDeclaredTimebaseRoundTripsAndBumpsToFormatThree()`** — set a timebase, save, assert the file's first line is `FORMAT 3` and the third line is `TIMEBASE 1ps`, reload and assert equality.
- **`secondsIsRecomputedFromTheTickAndNeverAccumulates()`** — assert `seconds(n) == seconds(1) * n` **exactly** for a decade of `n` up to 2^53, **and** that summing `seconds(1)` `n` times does **not** equal `seconds(n)`. **The test states the hazard the rule exists to avoid**, rather than merely avoiding it. If the summed and recomputed values are equal at the tested `n`, the test is at too small a scale — **raise `n` until the inequality holds, and record the scale at which it does**; that number is what the rule is protecting.
- **`aVersionTwoReaderRejectsAFormatThreeFileLoudly()`** — drive `Circuit.readFormatHeader` with `FORMAT 3` against `FORMAT_VERSION = 2` and assert `LoadError.Category.NEWER_FORMAT`, **not** `MALFORMED`. Assert the **category**, and assert the **message text** naming the offending token — not a boolean.
- **`theQuantizationOfFortyFourPointOneKilohertzIsTheDocumentedFigure()`** — assert the tick error of a 44.1 kHz period at a 1 ps base is **within 2 ppb**, pinning the number the audio capstone documentation quotes. 44100 = 2² · 3² · 5² · 7², so it is not exactly expressible on any decimal lattice; the residual is ≈1.7 ppb at 1 ps and ≈11.6 ppm at 1 ns.
- **`VcdExportGoldenTest` gains `vcdTimescaleFollowsTheDeclaredTimebase()`** with a second golden for a timebase-carrying fixture. **The two existing goldens must not change; if they do, the default is not absent, the change is wrong, and every other claim is void — stop.**
- **`FileFormatSpecTest` gains a `TIMEBASE` row**, so the grammar in `docs/file-format.md` and the parser cannot drift.
- **A nested subcircuit never writes `TIMEBASE`**, asserted on a hierarchy fixture.
- **The 2^53 assertion fires** rather than silently losing precision. A limit documented but not enforced is a comment. Both range figures (2^63 and 2^53 at the chosen base) go in `TimeBase`'s javadoc.
- **`jls.core` still has no `BASELINE` entry in `HeadlessCoreRatchetTest`.**
- **There is no accumulating time field** — not in `TimeBase`, not in a consumer, not as a cache — verified by inspection and stated in the PR.

## Consolidated scope after absorbing #431

#431 is closed as a duplicate of this issue. Recording the consolidated scope and boundaries, since the roster no longer matches reality.

### What this issue now owns, in one place

Three layers, and they are not interchangeable:

1. **The declaration and the conversion** — absorbed from #431. `src/jls/core/TimeBase.java` as a record `(int mult, Unit unit)` over VCD's own `$timescale` grammar; a parse that **rejects, never repairs**; `seconds(long ticks)` recomputed from the integer tick with **no accumulating field anywhere**; the `TIMEBASE` arm in `Circuit.loadCircuit`'s token loop **and** the `FORMAT_VERSION` 2 → 3 bump **in the same commit**; the imported-circuit suppression rule; the $2^{53}$ assertion; and the amendments to `docs/simulation-semantics.md` §1, `docs/batch-interface.md` §4.2 and `docs/file-format.md` §9. Full contract at https://github.com/anadon/JLS/issues/367#issuecomment-5181525358 and https://github.com/anadon/JLS/issues/367#issuecomment-5227073034.
2. **The residual** — never #431's, always this issue's. Carrying the declared unit through every consumer that reports time: the waveform axis, the delay displays and dialogs, **the analog solver's step (#351)** and **the audio sample rate (#346)**. It has no task id because the registry's space is closed at TASK-0112, and it is the reason the 2-3 mw band exceeds TASK-0101's 1.5 wk row. **Open Question 5 still owns that gap and is unresolved.**
3. **The five §5 integration criteria** — the tree-wide golden sweep, the exactness assertion firing, the observable refusal, the joint code-and-documentation assertion, and the **one-conversion-tree-wide grep**. Criteria 1 and 5 are marked *"does not exist yet"* in the body and remain so.

### Boundaries that survive the absorption unchanged

- **vs #368 (FEAT-048).** Distinct, per the boundary note at https://github.com/anadon/JLS/issues/367#issuecomment-5175958918. #368's exact crossing time is terminated by the integer tick lattice, not by a declared physical unit, which is why its `blocked_by` is `[331, 351]` and does not name this issue. Both ordering fields here stay empty as a Link-phase finding.
- **vs #319 (FEAT-013).** A two-direction sequencing interaction, deliberately `related` and not `blocked_by`. **Invariant 6 — one version mechanism, not two — is the thing at risk**, and Open Question 2's decision must be recorded on **both** issues. If this lands first and #319 does not adopt the attribute, the tree carries two version mechanisms permanently; that is a `REPLAN:` obligation on #319, not a discovery for later.
- **vs #405 (TASK-0010).** A sibling edge #431 surfaced and this issue did not previously name: **both touch `BatchSimulator`'s VCD header.** #405 owns the streaming writer and the emission loop; this owns the `$timescale` line's **content**. If both are in flight, the second to land regenerates nothing (the header is unchanged for an absent timebase) but **must not lose the other's edit**.
- **vs #351 and #346.** Consumers, not providers. A sample rate is samples per second and this is where the second comes from — but neither is a prerequisite in either direction.

### The tier decision is now blocking

This is `tier:feature` with **zero filed children** while `planned_tasks` still names TASK-0101. Pick one before the work is scheduled:

- **(a) Relabel `tier:task`** and execute from the carried-forward contract — but note this does **not** fit cleanly, because layers 2 and 3 above are genuinely feature-shaped: a residual sweep across consumer features and five integration criteria no single task asserts. Choosing (a) means explicitly descoping or re-homing them.
- **(b) Keep `tier:feature`** and file one fresh task carrying the absorbed contract verbatim, restoring #431's `STATUS:`-report-on-close obligation to it. **Recommended**, because it preserves the three-layer structure the cost band is built on.

Unlike #232 — where the roster genuinely collapsed to a single atomic scope — this feature has real residual substance beyond its absorbed child, so (b) is the better fit here.

### Still unresolved and still blocking

- **Open Question 1** (default precision) — recommended default **picosecond**; **must be recorded in tree with its range arithmetic** (≈107 days and ≈2.5 h at 1 ps; ≈292 years and ≈104 days at 1 ns). Blocks the documentation half.
- **Open Question 2** (whole-file epoch vs per-section flag) — **blocks execution** of the version-policy step, per #431's sharpening: the loader trap makes a must-understand mechanism mandatory either way, so the choice cannot be deferred to a later reader.
- **Open Question 5** (the 2-3 mw band against the 1.5 wk row) — blocks the plan's arithmetic, not the work.
- The canonical spelling (`1ps`, no space, one token in the `.jls` file; the spaced VCD form in the dump) rides along but must be **pinned in `FileFormatSpecTest`**, not left to the parser.

5176187686.body:
## Boundary note vs #367 — mirror record (feature deduplication, pass 2)

Pass 1 examined this issue against **#367 (FEAT-047, the physical time base and real-time scalar)** as a duplicate candidate and recorded the finding on #367 only. Mirroring it here. **Not duplicates — no merge, nothing migrated.**

**The two outcomes are adjacent, not the same.** #367 is a *declaration plus a conversion*: one optional per-circuit `TimeBase` record, the `$timescale` grammar, a rejecting parse, a non-accumulating `seconds(ticks)`, a version-refusal policy and a docs amendment — its acceptance is a tree-wide byte-identity negative plus the 2^53 exactness assertion. **This issue is a crossing mechanism plus a domain alphabet**: two one-bit bridges with hysteresis and an enforced publication-delay floor, the time-ownership inversion that *deletes rollback as a requirement*, the three step-cap regimes, and the domain check placed above the width check at all four `SimpleEditor` connection sites.

**The obvious-looking dependency does not exist, and this issue is the reason.** It is tempting to read #367 as a prerequisite of this feature's "exact crossing time" — seconds sound like they need a time base. **§3 of this issue refutes that**: the published transition time is

`t* = min{ t ∈ ℤ ∩ [t₀, t₁] : v(t) ≥ V_hi }`

defined **on the integer tick lattice**, not in seconds, and terminated by that lattice. That is exactly why `blocked_by` here is `[331, 351]` and does not name #367, and why #367 carries empty ordering fields as a recorded Link-phase finding rather than as an omission. Real consumer edges to #367 exist elsewhere in the same cluster (#486 `blocked_by: [367, 336, 319]`; #490 `blocked_by: [487, 367]`) — this feature is simply not one of them. **Do not add an edge to #367 here without first refuting §3's tick-lattice derivation**, because adding it would make criterion 1 (published stream invariant under timestep-controller parameters) depend on a unit it does not use.

**Recorded forward, unresolved and outside this cluster.** Open Question 2 — who pays for the port descriptor, this issue's *domain* axis, #344's *radix* axis or #341's *strength* axis — is a shared-scope accounting item, not a duplicate. All three answer "what may this terminal carry", all three are checked at the same four sites, and this issue's own Definition of Done requires the decision to be recorded on **#341 and #344** as well as here. Neither of those is in this cluster and neither carries the record yet. Escalated for the maintainer: **without it the descriptor gets built three times and JLS acquires three refusal vocabularies that disagree at the edges** — which §2 already names as the rejected alternative.

5181560763.body:
## Boundary with #434 (TASK-0102) — overlapping but NOT duplicates

A feature/task deduplication pass flagged this pair as a near-verbatim-title merge candidate: *"a drawn design crosses between continuous and discrete in both directions at places the student chose — exact crossing time, no rollback machinery"* against #434's *"two drawable level converters and a lock-step contract … an exact crossing tick, a ramped D-A, and no rollback machinery anywhere."* **Examined and rejected as a merge.** Recording the boundary here so a later pass does not re-litigate it.

**Why it is not a duplicate.** The merge case rests on #434 being this feature's sole child. It is not. This issue's `planned_tasks` carries **two** entries, and the second is a substantial, separately-landing scope that #434 explicitly disclaims:

> the port and net domain alphabet and its four enforcement sites - the descriptor, the unconditional check above the width check at every connection site, the validate-don't-widen rule on load, and the elaboration assertion. No task id: the registry's task space is closed at TASK-0112…

#434's §13 puts it out of scope by name — *"Out of scope: … the domain check above the width check (FEAT-048 criterion 6, shared with #341 and #344 — **build the descriptor once**)"* — and its §12 assigns it explicitly: *"criterion 6 … **is the port-alphabet half**."* Its Open Question 1 states the separability directly: the descriptor question *"**Blocks execution** of FEAT-048 criterion 6 — not of this task's bridges, which is why they are separable."*

So the two are the intended feature→task hierarchy, not one outcome owned twice. #434 is a slice, and slices are supposed to be narrower.

**What each side owns.**

| | #368 (this issue) | #434 (TASK-0102) |
|---|---|---|
| The two one-bit bridge elements, their parameters and refusals | consumes | **owns** |
| The lock-step contract / ownership inversion / `nextEventTime()` | consumes | **owns** |
| The three step-cap regimes and the bisection to the tick lattice | consumes | **owns** |
| The port/net **domain alphabet** and its descriptor | **owns** (second roster row, ~2.5 wk) | out of scope by name |
| The unconditional check above the width check at all four `SimpleEditor` sites (`:4014`, `:4141`, `:4246`, `:4357`) | **owns** (§4 invariant 2, §5 criterion 3) | out of scope |
| Validate-don't-widen on load, and the elaboration assertion | **owns** (§4 invariant 3, §5 criterion 4) | out of scope |
| The release constraint that the check may not ship without the bridges | **owns** (§4 invariant 5) | notes it as a threat |
| The zero-bits trap (`Put.java:34-35`, `bits > 0 &&` guards) that forces the check order | **owns** — the derivation is here | cites it |

**The two-and-a-half-week residual is real and is not double-counted.** §Cost records band 4-6 mw against a printed task sum of 2 wk, and Open Question 1 names the gap as exactly this alphabet scope. Merging #434 into this issue would collapse a filed, executable landing into a comment and leave the alphabet — the *unfiled* half — as the only thing anyone could still act on. That is backwards.

**Consequences that stand.**

1. **Open Question 1 is unresolved and now more pointed.** The alphabet scope still has no id. Recommended default remains **(a) mint an id for it** — it is a separate landing under a separate release constraint (§4 invariant 5), so it wants its own issue. It must resolve to a filed issue or be descoped before this feature can close; it cannot be quietly absorbed.
2. **Open Question 2 (who pays for the port descriptor) is a three-way question across this issue, #341 (FEAT-027, drive strength) and #344 (FEAT-028, radix).** All three answer *"what may this terminal carry"*, all three are checked at the same four connection sites, and all three carry the same validate-don't-widen rule on load. Whichever ships first pays ~2.5 wk and the other two pay a fraction. **Built separately, JLS acquires three refusal vocabularies that disagree at the edges.** This issue's DoD already requires the decision be recorded on #341 and #344 as well as here; that obligation is unaffected by this pass and still outstanding.
3. **#434's `blocked_by` names two unfiled prerequisites** — TASK-0097 (Newton/Trapezoidal/TimestepController, owned by #351) and TASK-0105 (the per-view palette dimension, owned by #330). Neither is filed. The second is not a nicety: `PaletteContractTest` is green at exactly 32/35 and asserts one palette entry per registered type outside three tags, so **registering four analog types forces four buttons onto the first-year toolbar through a *passing* test** unless the view dimension lands first. A passing test is the failure mode there.
4. **The stop-reason change is owned jointly and must not fall between them.** A region always holding one pending self-event makes `Simulator.java:217`'s `!eventQueue.isEmpty()` guard never fail, so `"Simulation: No More Activity"` becomes permanently unreachable for any design containing a continuous region and `-d`/`maxTime` becomes SPICE's `.tran tstop`. #434 owns amending `docs/batch-interface.md` §3.1 **in the same change**; this issue's §5 criterion 6 owns verifying it was documented before it could be discovered. Both halves are pinned — analog fixture changed, digital fixture unchanged.

No merge performed; both issues stay open on their own contracts.

## Boundary note: #369 / #524, and #369 / #562 (feature deduplication, pass 1)

Two pairs adjudicated in pass 1. **Verdict on both: no merge.**

### #369 ↔ #524 (FEAT-C21-1) — create vs. freeze, and the ordering that makes them non-interchangeable

This issue **creates** the surface; #524 **freezes** it. The distinction is load-bearing rather than semantic, because #369's own evidence establishes that the thing #524 promises to freeze **does not exist yet**: the `-t` grammar has four productions and none mentions an output, and `docs/batch-interface.md:36-40` defines exactly three exit statuses, none meaning "the run completed and the answer was wrong."

- **#369 owns** the verdict itself — the expectations channel behind a new flag with the `-t` grammar literally untouched, the PASS/FAIL/UNRUN lattice in which `UNRUN` is absorbing under the join, the per-submission and aggregate report schema, one runner behind both CLI and panel, vacuity detection, and coverage as `(covered, total, metric)`.
- **#524 owns** turning that into a **versioned public promise**: a `CliContractConformanceTest` that exercises every clause, a seeded-violation falsification transcript that fails CI *before any adapter test runs*, a semver-plus-deprecation-window ratchet, and a CLI-queryable contract version so an adapter can refuse an incompatible build by name.

**Status 3 is the sharpest statement of the boundary.** #524's headline names "exit codes including status 3" — a fourth status beyond today's three. That status only becomes definable once #369 has distinguished "ran and failed" from "could not run" (#369 §1 criterion 3, and §5 criterion 1's three-way trichotomy test). #524's exit-code and artifact-path spec therefore **cannot be authored before #369 lands**, which is why #524 records `ordering_after: [369, 466]` rather than restating this issue's scope. Neither the conformance suite nor the compatibility ratchet appears anywhere in #369; neither the expectations file, the verdict lattice, vacuity, nor coverage appears anywhere in #524. Rule 3(a)/3(d) — sequential ownership of one interface at two lifecycle stages.

**One live coupling to watch, recorded rather than merged:** #524's third acceptance criterion explicitly requires the ratchet to keep "FEAT-053-lineage verdict evolution possible without breaking the freeze." If this issue's report schema ships **without** the version field its own DoD requires, #524 freezes an unversioned schema and that criterion becomes unsatisfiable. The version field is #369's obligation and #524's precondition.

### #369 ↔ #562 (FEAT-C29-5) — producer of vectors vs. owner of the runner

#562 translates a `.dig` file's embedded test cases into runnable `-t` vector files with verdict parity against Digital. It is a **consumer** of this issue's engine and says so in its own boundary notes: *"The grading/expectation harness itself is owned by the batch line (TASK-0111 #466, in-editor panel #214) — this feature emits its input format, it does not extend the runner."* Rule 3(b) — shared prerequisite, not shared outcome. #562 owns `.dig` test-language translation fidelity, the named-loss report for untranslatable constructs, and byte-determinism of the emitted vector files; none of that is in scope here.

**Not a duplicate. #466 is one of four planned children, not this feature's whole outcome.** The near-verbatim titles were flagged by #508 and re-examined here against both bodies; the merge is refused on the evidence below.

**Why the titles collide.** Both issues open on the same sentence — the batch engine has no verdict at `2d0ca9d` — because #466 is the child that closes that gap. The headline is shared; the scope is not.

**What #466 covers.** §1 capabilities 1, 2, 3, 4 and 7: the separate expectations file behind `-check`, the single `TestVectorRunner` behind CLI and panel, the byte-deterministic xUnit + plain `GradeReport`, exit status 3, the `TestPanel`, and `examples/autograde/lab-01/`. #466 §13 states its own exclusions verbatim: *"Explicitly out of scope: property checking, equivalence and coverage (TASK-0112), any change to the `-t` grammar, the stdout format or the VCD profile, the UI harness itself (TASK-0021 / #91), the display lane (#162), and new assertion semantics of any kind."*

**What #466 does not cover, and who does.** This feature's `planned_tasks` roster has four entries, now all filed:

| planned task | filed as | scope this feature keeps that #466 lacks |
|---|---|---|
| TASK-0021 | **#470** | the dialog sweep gains validation rather than construct-and-cancel, plus a mouse assertion surface |
| TASK-0073 | **#423** | first-divergence comparator, exclusion set under its own ratchet, verdict lattice where "I don't know" is never a pass |
| TASK-0111 | **#466** | — (this is the pair under examination) |
| TASK-0112 | **#483** | properties with vacuity detection, equivalence with a stated decidable class, coverage as `(covered, total, metric)` |

§1 capabilities **5** (a vacuous pass is detectable) and **6** (coverage reported as data with a stated metric, never a bare percentage) are owned here and discharged by #483, not #466. Absorbing #466 into this feature — or this feature into #466 — would leave those two capabilities, plus §5 integration criteria 3 (panel and CLI agree, asserted not assumed), 4 (aggregate determinism under reordering) and 5 (the vacuity detector has a null), with no owner. That is the information a false merge would destroy.

**The boundary, stated once.** #369 owns the capability statement, the seven §1 criteria, the §4 invariants (in particular invariant 1, the `-t` grammar is literally untouched, and invariant 5, one runner behind both front ends), the §5 integration criteria that no single child asserts, and the three serving capstones #300/#306/#311. #466 owns the verdict channel and its first consumer. Neither closes without the other.

**Also recorded on this pass:** #214 is a separate boundary, not a third copy — see the comment posted there. #466 declares that it closes #214, and #214's outcome is a proper subset of #466's, so #214 is the named GUI-panel slice rather than a duplicate of either.

**Disposition: no merge, no closure. Both issues stay open with the ownership above.**

## CORRECTION: the `HdlExporter` inventory row is credited as already shipped against a commit that does not exist. Treat it as UNCOVERED.

This was found by an earlier review pass working the hdl-physical slice, escalated as out-of-slice, and never acted on. Acting on it now, because it is the failure mode that a "verify the inventory" task can least afford: an inventory row that marks itself discharged on false evidence.

### The measurement

§8 credits `HdlPolicyTest.exportPolicyIsTotalOverTheElementRegistry` as having landed at commit `b54e6ee`. Both halves fail:

```
$ git cat-file -t b54e6ee
fatal: Not a valid object name b54e6ee

$ git grep -n 'exportPolicyIsTotalOverTheElementRegistry\|classifiedElementClasses' origin/master -- src/ test/
(no output)

$ git grep -n 'REJECTED' origin/master -- src/jls/hdl/HdlExporter.java
(no output)
```

`b54e6ee` is not a reachable object at all — not merely branch-only like `2d0ca9d`, but unresolvable — and the symbol it is credited with introducing is **absent from the default branch**. `test/jls/hdl/HdlPolicyTest.java` is one of #493 §3's **seven sharp-edge files**, and `exportPolicyIsTotalOverTheElementRegistry()` sits at branch-only lines `377-409`. Per #493 §4 the correct reading on `master` is that this test is **proposed by #492**, not shipped.

### The consequences, and they are not bookkeeping

1. **This issue's `HdlExporter` inventory row is UNCOVERED.** Do not carry it as satisfied and do not let it close on the strength of that credit. The export policy is **not** total at `828822672fc3a8e2cb6da25192472079f04c29dd`: `HdlExporter` has three policy buckets (`EXPORTED`, `SKIPPED`, `TOPOLOGY`), not four, and an unclassified element is refused with no reason attached. #492 exists precisely because it is not total, and #492 measured four registered element types with no export policy at all — `FieldExtend`, `Memory`, `RegisterFile`, `SubCircuit`.
2. **The false credit propagated.** #492 records that this same "already shipped" claim reached #385 and #384 (both now closed as duplicates of #292), where it was used to justify dropping an ordering edge. An inventory that credits nonexistent coverage does not merely under-report — it authorises downstream ordering decisions built on nothing.
3. **This is #493 case (b) at its sharpest**, and it should be treated as a template rather than a one-off: a *symbol* credited as landed, at a commit label nobody can resolve, in a file where branch-only content and master content interleave. Re-derive by **content**, never by commit label and never by line number.

- Re-run the inventory row against `828822672fc3a8e2cb6da25192472079f04c29dd` by content, and record `HdlExporter` as uncovered with #492 named as the owner that would cover it.
- Re-check every other row in §8 whose evidence is a *symbol credited to a commit* rather than a grep re-run here and now. If Open Question 1 moves from option (a) to option (b) — wire segments as children — #739's traversal cost moves with it. Answering that question is still this task's call, on #355.
- **#741** (TASK-C544-3, signal-state changes announced *as they happen* during simulation) is live announcement, which this task explicitly does not do — this task's tree is a view rebuilt per query (§7.8), with no event stream. **Not a duplicate.** #737 (TASK-C544-1) is the Orca feasibility spike that gates whether Swing can deliver a live announcement at all.
- **#743** (TASK-C544-4, a scripted Orca session in the Wayland CI rig with spoken output asserted) is the automated form of the manual screen-reader pass this task's §9 and Open Question 5 require. **Not a duplicate, and it does not discharge this task's obligation** — this task requires one named pass on one named platform recorded in its PR; #743 is a separate CI capability. - **#756** (TASK-C549-1, "a keyboard-unreachable dialog fails the build") builds `OperabilityRatchetTest`, enumerating dialog and window surfaces from the registry and asserting every focusable control is keyboard-reachable, with the seeded red run recorded first. **Distinct from this task's item 2** (modal accelerator *inertness* — asserting a raised modal dialog does **not** leak window accelerators, `ModalAcceleratorInertnessTest`, this task's P4). Its AC-5 already protects the boundary: *"#75's own residual — the File>Close accelerator, the GUI HDL-export entry, the assistive-tech pass — stays owned there and is not absorbed here."*
  - **Direct interaction with this task, worth coordinating:** this task's §14 requires *"All five deferral paragraphs at `docs/keyboard-a11y-verification.md:121-142` are replaced — each by a passing test or by a recorded bound with its reason and its evidence; **none is left saying 'not added'**."* #758 AC-2 requires *every* row of that document classified automated-or-manual with no unclassified rows, and AC-3 requires each automated row keep a red-on-break mutation — which is exactly this task's O4 discipline generalized to the whole file. **The two tasks edit the same document with compatible rules.** If this task lands first, #758 inherits five newly-classified rows; if #758 lands first, this task's five replacements must arrive already classified.

That limitation should surface as a named exception in #754's generated document rather than being lost.

## ABSORBED — create-audit of #600-#868, 2026-08-08

Two tasks filed by the create stage reproduce scope this task already owns: **#662** (TASK-C111-2, "a Windows run log proves iverilog, ghdl and yosys actually ran") and **#668** (TASK-C265-2, the macOS twin). Both are closed as duplicates of this issue.

They are duplicates because this task's §5 already owns the whole property on all three lanes:
- **P1** — run the four toolchain-gated suites on a lane where arming is demanded and observe **zero skips**, judged by the same surefire `skipped="0"` fields as O2. That *is* "the goldens stop being green by skipping", asserted rather than eyeballed.
- **P4/P5** — the `JLS_REQUIRE_HDL_TOOLS=1` arming assertion, and the workflow assertion that **the required Linux, Windows and macOS build jobs all set it**, so removing it from CI fails a test instead of quietly disarming the suite.
- **P7** — each armed job's summary carries `yosys -V`, `iverilog -V`, `ghdl --version` and `nextpnr-ice40 --version`, pasted into the PR as the recorded drift baseline.

A run log showing the tools invoked is P1 + P7's evidence, on lanes P5 already names. Carrying forward what those two issues added:

### 1. The executed-versus-skipped count must be legible without opening surefire XML
Both slices asked for something this task's §9 does not: the HDL golden suite should **report executed-versus-skipped counts at a glance**, so a zero-executed run is distinguishable from a passing one in the job output, not only in `target/surefire-reports/*.xml`. Add this to §7.6's provided data — the aggregated arming message already has the right shape for it — and to §14. P1 is the assertion; this is the diagnostic that makes a P1 failure readable.

### 2. Record the run-log evidence on the owning feature issues
Windows evidence lands as a comment on **#111** and macOS evidence on **#265**, each citing the run ID and job ID. This task's §14 currently reports landing only on #359. Add: a `STATUS:` comment on #111 and on #265 carrying the armed run's evidence, since those are the issues whose DoD boxes are waiting on it.

### 3. Pin drift is in scope, and must be recorded
- Windows: `OSS_CAD_URL` / `OSS_CAD_SHA256` stay pinned and sha256-gated. **If the pinned asset has drifted, re-pin it in this change and record the drift** rather than working around it.
- macOS: **if a Homebrew formula has been renamed or dropped, adjust the step here and record the drift.** This is the concrete form of H4 and Open Question 1 — §11 already flags that `ci.yml:283` warns about tap/name uncertainty for `icarus-verilog`, and making the install fail-closed converts a drifted name from a silent skip into a red lane on the first run. Say which name was wrong, not just that it was fixed.

### 4. A contradiction that must be resolved out loud, not buried
#662 and #668 each carried an acceptance criterion that the toolchain install **keeps degrading to a self-skip with a `::notice` rather than failing the lane, "while the lane is advisory"**. That is the exact opposite of this task's P9 and of #406's P4/P9, both of which make the install fail-closed.

The two are reconcilable only as a sequence, and the sequence must be written down rather than discovered:

- **While a platform lane is advisory**, a soft install is defensible — it is what §7.12 item 2 already grants the advisory feature-release Linux leg.
- **The moment #406 drops `continue-on-error` on that lane, the soft path becomes the defect this task exists to remove**, because a required check that silently drops `IverilogCompileTest` / `GhdlCompileTest` / the yosys legs changes what "green" means.

So: this task arms Linux fail-closed now (its required LTS leg), and the Windows/macOS install steps go fail-closed **in lockstep with #406's promotion of those lanes**, not before and not after. Whichever of the two lands second owns flipping the remaining `exit 0` / `::notice`-and-continue paths, and says so in the workflow comment beside them. Record the chosen order in the PR; do not let a lane become required while its toolchain install can still degrade silently.

### Boundary
This task owns tool installation, the arming variable, the arming assertion and the recorded versions on every lane. **#406 owns the two jobs' error policy and their promotion**; #111 and #265 are the features that consume the evidence. Nothing here changes what any suite asserts — only whether it is permitted to skip (§7.12 item 4, unchanged).
