5227501233.body:
## Mirror of the #341 ruling — your unnumbered edge has a number, and H3 is refuted before you start

Three corrections, all decided on #341 today (https://github.com/anadon/JLS/issues/341#issuecomment-5227498570) and mirrored here so both endpoints carry them.

### 1. `blocked_by: [391]` — the edge the body could not name

The machine block carries `blocked_by: []` with the note *"TASK-0057 is being filed concurrently; the edge is `blocked_by: [TASK-0057]` in scope and a link pass adds the number."* **The link pass never ran, and TASK-0057 has been filed since 2026-08-03 as #391.** A later review pass on #341 compounded this by stating "TASK-0057 does not appear to be filed."

Read the machine block as `blocked_by: [391]`. The § Method step "Land on TASK-0057's fold" and the DoD line "The `blocked_by` edge to TASK-0057 is written into the machine block by the link pass" both resolve to #391. The mermaid node `T57` is #391.

The edge is real, not conventional, and #391's own O3 says why in the stronger form: `WireNet.propagate`'s operand is `@Nullable BitSet` where `null` means *whole-port* HiZ, so a per-bit fold over it is **inexpressible**, not merely unimplemented. #391 in turn waits on the value type, now filed as **#881** under #232 — so the real chain is `#881 → #391 → this issue`. Your § Method step 1 ("re-verify O1; if reordering no longer changes the answer, TASK-0057 has already fixed it and this task's scope narrows") stays exactly as written and is the right tripwire.

### 2. Ownership settled: this issue is #341's **only** child

#341's Open Question 1 is resolved as its own recommended default — TASK-0057 → #322, TASK-0049 → #339, TASK-0093 → #329, and **TASK-0058 (this issue) is #341's sole exclusive row**. Your `part_of_feature: 341` was already consistent with that and is ratified, not changed. The consequence a scheduler needs: #341's exclusive row sum is now 2 wk against a 6-9 mw band, so funding this issue does not fund that feature.

### 3. H3 is REFUTED for `OPEN_DRAIN` and `OPEN_SOURCE`, and §7.7 / §7.12 are superseded on driver kind

H3 asserts *"`DriverKind` and `NetKind` can be derived from element identity rather than saved, so no format version bump is needed."* Measured at the default-branch head `828822672fc3a8e2cb6da25192472079f04c29dd`:

```
$ git grep -nE 'Strength|OPEN_DRAIN|open-drain|PullUp|PullDown' -- src/
(no output)

$ git grep -n 'triState' -- src/jls/elem/Output.java
src/jls/elem/Output.java:19:	private boolean triState = false;
src/jls/elem/Output.java:59:		p.triState = triState;
src/jls/elem/Output.java:69:		triState = true;
src/jls/elem/Output.java:80:		triState = which;
src/jls/elem/Output.java:94:		return triState;
```

`Output.triState` is a derived *edit-time* field set by `WireNet.setTriState`'s walk (your own O7), present in no `savedAttributes()` set. That precedent carries `PUSH_PULL` and `TRI` and nothing more. `PULL` is carried by the identity of the two elements you ship. **`OPEN_DRAIN` and `OPEN_SOURCE` are carried by nothing** — no element on master is open-drain and **your § Materials ships none**, listing exactly two new `LogicElement` subclasses, both pull elements.

That is a contradiction inside this issue, not merely with #341: **your P3 requires "three open-drain drivers plus one `PullUp`"** and your §7.10 derives `WAND` from `OPEN_DRAIN ∈ K`. Under H3 as written, P3's fixture cannot be constructed — there is no way for a file or a user to mark a driver open-drain.

**Decision, which is your own H3 falsification clause executed rather than discovered:**

- **`DriverKind` becomes a saved, must-understand attribute on the driving element, and this task takes the `FORMAT` version bump knowingly** — *"take the format version bump knowingly, per `docs/file-format.md:470` — do not ship a behavioural attribute as ignorable."* Dropping an `OPEN_DRAIN` marker turns a wired-AND bus into a contention; that is behaviour-changing by any reading of `:470`, which is the very line you cite as the reason derivation is the safe route.
- **`NetKind` stays DERIVED, in `recheck`, from the attached driver kinds, never from geometry, never saved.** You win this half outright, and against #341's §1 criterion 5. The argument is #341's own invariant 3 (*"one arbitration rule, not two … a second resolution path that can disagree with the first is a landing defect"*) applied to classification: your §7.10 makes `netKind` a total function of the attached `DriverKind`s, so a saved copy is a second source of truth that a loader must silently prefer or silently discard when the two disagree.
- **The two new tags still cost zero format versions**, exactly as your §7.1 says, because an unknown tag is already a hard error. The bump is bought by the driver-kind attribute alone.
- **A refusal path is now in scope:** a file carrying a `DriverKind` value this reader does not understand is refused **by name** — not skipped, not downgraded to `PUSH_PULL`. This is where #341's §1 criterion 5 and §5 integration criterion 5 re-target, and it needs a hand-crafted fixture.

**Superseded by the above:** §7.7's "No new saved attributes on existing elements"; §7.12 item 1 ("No format version bump"); the DoD line "No format version bump; `Circuit.FORMAT_VERSION` unmoved". §7.7's *`NetKind` derived* half and the `docs/file-format.md` §7 two-row requirement both survive unchanged.

**Unaffected, checked explicitly:** H4 and P8. A file with no driver-kind attribute loads as `PUSH_PULL`/`TRI` exactly as today, so every historical `.jls` still loads and the byte-identity claim for circuits with no strength diversity stands.

**Scope consequence, stated rather than absorbed:** a saved attribute, its loader and refusal paths, and a `FORMAT` bump were not in this issue's 2 wk row. #341's 6-9 mw band is where that was priced; do not silently swallow it.

### 4. Open Question 2 gains a required answer; Open Question 4 gains one

- **Your Open Question 2 (does `PullUp` implement `TriProp`) is unchanged** — recommended default *no*, pin it with a test either way. Nothing here touches it.
- **#341's Open Question 4 (does net kind bump the format version) is ANSWERED** and the answer is split: no for net kind, yes for driver kind, taken as a global `FORMAT` bump now with migration to #319's per-section versioning as a follow-on rather than a wait.
- **#341's Open Question 2 (which technologies the driver-kind vocabulary covers) is STILL OPEN and now blocks you harder.** Your `DriverKind` has no technology axis; #341 states that modelling a floating TTL input that reads high without a floating CMOS input that reads X *teaches a falsehood*. Since driver kind is now a **saved** vocabulary, adding a technology axis later is a second format decision rather than an enum edit. Answer it before you execute, together with #341 §3's per-driver output-impedance obligation to #490 — both widen the same saved vocabulary and both get cheaper if answered once.

### 5. Evidence pin

`evidence_commit: 2d0ca9d…` does not resolve (`git cat-file -t` → *"could not get object info"*). Per #493 the durable equivalent is `828822672fc3a8e2cb6da25192472079f04c29dd`. Every observation in this body re-derives there unchanged, including O1's experiment, O2's `WireNet.java` block, O3, O4, O5's `docs/simulation-semantics.md` quotations, O7 and O8 — the O2 §2 preamble (`git diff --quiet … && echo IDENTICAL`) is what makes that safe to assert. **Do not re-pin to `07a0bea`**; it is not on master either. See #493.

5227403719.body:
## ORDERING + EVIDENCE CORRECTION: `blocked_by` is still empty, the link pass never ran, TASK-0056 no longer exists — and every observation re-derives on master

Sim-engine adversarial review, 2026-08-08. This comment supersedes the `Status & Dependencies` machine block, the "Unfiled prerequisites, stated as scope" paragraph, the mermaid graph's omitted edges, and § 12's TASK-0056 / TASK-0063 / TASK-0026 / TASK-0023 rows. **§ 7.10's soundness argument, the seq-conservation obligation, O4's `SubCircuit` finding and O5's `Memory`/`Adder` trap stand unchanged** — they are the load-bearing content and nothing below touches them.

### 1. The link pass never happened, and this issue predicted it would

The body says: *"Three sibling tasks are being filed concurrently … A link pass adds all three edges"* and `blocked_by: []`. All three were filed. **No edge was added.** #362's LINK PASS note of 2026-08-02 covered the feature tier only; the task tier was never linked, so this feature's entire declared critical path lives in prose and every task in it is independently pickable today.

**Corrected, and mirrored on each endpoint:**

```yaml
blocked_by:
  - 476   # TASK-0063 — REAL: the cone marker IS its intrusive queued flag (§7.5).
          #   Built against `HashSet dupCheck` the closure hashes a SimEvent per cone
          #   node — the exact cost it exists to remove — and is rewritten when the set
          #   goes away. Second reason (#362 §6): measuring the closure against the
          #   priority queue attributes the queue's cost to the closure.
  - 442   # TASK-0026 — REAL under K3: the byte-identity gate decides whether this may
          #   land at all. P1 extends that gate; it does not own it.
blocks: []
related: [221, 232, 335, 322, 325, 295, 301, 306, 312, 370, 379, 878, 879]
```

**#379 (TASK-0023) is deliberately *not* in `blocked_by`.** It supplies the denominators P7 reports against, and it reaches this task **through** #442, which does declare it. Writing #379 → #393 directly would be a transitive edge dressed as a prerequisite — this task can be executed and its queue-traffic drop measured as a raw before/after without #379's behavioral constant existing at all. Only P7's *band comparison* needs it, and that is #442's obligation. Recorded so the next link pass does not "helpfully" add it.

### 2. TASK-0056 does not exist; the leg it named is #878 → #879

**#475 (TASK-0056) was closed 2026-08-08 as a duplicate of #232.** § 12's row — *"TASK-0056 (value representation; being filed concurrently, shared with #322) — independent of this task; a different leg of the same profile"* — should read **#879** (with #878, the type, ahead of it), children of #232 filed by this review.

**And "independent" is now contested.** `docs/capability-roadmap/keystone-c-performance.md` § 7.2, on master, ends its dependency-ordered list with:

> 5. **Levelize the zero-delay plane** (§ 6.3). **Wants (3) done and the value type landed.**

(where (3) is caching `WireNet`'s driver and sink arrays at elaboration). Its stage table likewise puts the value type at stage 0 and this closure at stage 1.

That is a *preference-shaped* claim as written — it says "wants", not "requires", and gives no mechanism by which the closure would be *wrong* without the value type. **This review does not promote it to a `blocked_by` edge**, because nothing in § 7.10's soundness argument depends on the value representation: the cone is derived from declared delays and the seq-conservation claim is about ordering, not about values. But two consequences are real and are recorded:

- **The `WireNet` driver/sink array caching that keystone-c calls (3) has no filed issue anywhere.** The closure walks exactly those adjacencies to build `C(n)` and `F(n)`. That is a genuine gap in this task's materials list — §6 lists what must be built and does not mention how the cone's adjacency is obtained cheaply. **Either this task builds it and says so, or it is filed.** Recorded as Open Question 6 below.
- Landing this concurrently with #879 makes neither profile attributable, exactly as #476's T5 says for its own pairing. Sequence, or measure separately.

### 3. Every observation re-derives at `origin/master` — the evidence commit is gone, the evidence is not

`2d0ca9dcd9db78b36c3caf4c6c57dd8701862cc7` **is not present in the repository** (`git cat-file -e` fails), and `docs/plan/` has **zero paths** at `origin/master`. Under #493 the citations are nominally unreliable. Re-derived at `origin/master = 828822672fc3a8e2cb6da25192472079f04c29dd`:

- **O1** — `git grep -il 'zerodelay' origin/master -- src/` returns nothing. No closure exists. ✅
- **O2** — `git grep -in 'combinational loop\|zero-delay cycle' origin/master -- src/` returns nothing. **There is still no loop diagnostic anywhere in `src/`.** ✅
- **O5** — `src/jls/elem/Adder.java:261` is still `propDelay = bits * defaultPropDelay;`, and `Memory.java` still carries three `now + accessTime` posts. **Both are still timed and must stay out of the cone.** ✅
- **O6** — `docs/simulation-semantics.md` still describes `todo == null` and *"`TriState.react` uses the string `\"off\"`"*, while `SimEvent.java:23` is `public sealed interface Payload {` and `:30` is `public record PinChanged() implements Payload {`. **The normative section this task edits is still stale, exactly as described.** ✅

The only citation that moved is `BRIEF.md § 13`, and it is recoverable: the same figures are on master at `docs/capability-roadmap/keystone-c-performance.md`. For this task specifically, § 2's event census is the number P7 should report against — **`fired 2,331,793`, of which `PinChanged 1,919,891 (82.3%)`** on `riscv/build/k2000.jls`, and § 6's finding that **"82.3% of all events carry no time"**. That is a far better statement of this task's premise than "a large share of queue traffic models no elapsed time", and it is measured. **Cite the master path in the PR.**

### 4. One acceptance criterion is not evaluable as written

P3's `aZeroDelayCycleIsReportedNotStormed()` asserts the run terminates. T-list already notes the fixture "must storm, not merely oscillate slowly" and needs its own time bound. Sharpen it: **the red state is a genuine non-termination**, so the pre-change half of P3 cannot be a JUnit assertion at all — it is a bounded external run that is killed. Write it as such, with the bound and the kill recorded in the PR, or the "fails at the pre-change commit" DoD item is unsatisfiable and will be quietly waived. O2's mechanism explains why: the queue never empties and `now` never advances past `maxTime`, so **neither loop-exit condition can fire**.

### 5. Open Question 6 (new, rides along)

**Where does the cone's adjacency come from?** § 7.3 says connectivity is "read at cone-construction time" and § 6 does not list it as something to be built. `WireNet`'s driver/sink arrays are not cached at elaboration on master, and keystone-c calls that caching a prerequisite of levelization. Recommended default: **measure the cone-construction cost on the k2000 fixture first**; if it is material, file the caching as its own task rather than absorbing it here — a closure that pays an uncached adjacency walk per timestamp can be net-negative while every one of P1–P8 passes.

MISSING ORDERING EDGE, NOW OWED HERE (adversarial review, slice ux-docs).

```yaml

```

**Why this lands here rather than upstream.** #441 (TASK-0020) §12 named this issue as a consumer — *"the breadboard canvas needs a gesture machine that is not welded to one `JPanel`; today they would each rebuild it"* — and explicitly declined to write the edge from its own end: *"no ordering edge is written here because this task does not read its output and #401 is not a prerequisite; the dependency runs the other way and **belongs on #401**."* That edge was never written, and #441 has since been closed as a duplicate into **#84**, so the reference it would have pointed at no longer resolves.

**The edge is real, and it is the expensive kind if missed.** This issue's outcome is a second canvas with *"its own geometry, ops, undo and default-hidden palette"*. At master `29afb26` the editor's nine-state interaction machine is an enum on `SimpleEditor` whose live state field and only transition function sit inside `EditWindow`, a `private class ... extends JPanel` — so it cannot be instantiated, driven or asserted without that one panel. A second canvas built before #84 lands has exactly two options: duplicate the nine-state machine for the breadboard, or drive the breadboard through a machine welded to the schematic canvas. The first is the "they would each rebuild it" outcome #441 predicted; the second does not work. #84 produces `InteractionState` and `MouseMachine` as AWT-free types with the ArchUnit rule that keeps them that way, which is precisely what a second canvas needs to exist.

**The full chain, both hops genuine:** **#440** (TASK-0019 — the `jls.edit` coverage floor; `jls.edit` is deliberately unfloored at `pom.xml:408-411`, so a large extraction's "coverage did not fall" is unmeasurable without it) → **#84** (the headless machine) → **#401** (this issue).

**Scope consequence, stated so it is a decision rather than a discovery:** this issue's stated constraint that the second canvas land *"inside the editor's coverage budget"* is only checkable once #440 has set that budget. If this issue is scheduled ahead of #84 anyway, the cost is named in advance — the breadboard's gesture handling lands inside or beside `SimpleEditor` and becomes one more thing #84 has to move, which is the same cost #380 records for running ahead of its own blocker.

The matching record is on #84, which also now carries `part_of_feature: 316` and the inbound consumer set (#804, #593, #521) re-homed off the closed #441.

5181446172.body:
## Boundary with the TASK-C111-* and TASK-C265-* slices (feature/task deduplication pass, cluster C)

**Action required before execution: eight newly-filed tasks own clauses of this task's outcome.** This is the operationally important finding of the pass. No merge is made — every one of the eight is a strict slice of this task, and this task is a strict slice of #317 — but the same `ci.yml` edits are now owned twice and would land twice if both paths are executed.

**The clause-by-clause map.** This task's four `PlatformLaneRatchetTest` assertions, against the slices filed under #111 and #265:

| this task's clause (§8 / O1) | Windows slice | macOS slice |
|---|---|---|
| drop the job-wide `continue-on-error` (`ci.yml:156`, `:263`); accrue the 20-run record; register the byte-stable check name | **#661** | **#667** (also carries #265 Stage 2's taxonomy note, which this task only *consumes*) |
| toolchain fail-closed — remove the `exit 0` / `::notice`-and-continue paths (O6) | **#662** (framed as run-log proof the tools actually ran) | **#668** (same framing, brew side) |
| arm the display suite (`-Djls.test.headless=false`) — macOS-only failure in O1 | **#663** (Windows already armed at `:244`; #663 is about it gating) | **#669** |
| remove `-Djacoco.skip=true`, enforce a calibrated floor (O4, H2) | **#664** | **#670** |

**What this task holds that no slice holds.** `test/jls/PlatformLaneRatchetTest` itself — the standing four-assertion ratchet over `ci.yml` that makes P1–P4 red-then-green and joins the `*RatchetTest` family (O12). Also the cross-platform coverage-spread measurement of §8 step 3 (the package × platform table that is H2's evidence and the basis for any epsilon widening), P7 (the Windows JDK-26 leg stays advisory **matrix-scoped**, `${{ matrix.java != 25 }}`, proven by two deliberate branches), and P8 (`pom.xml` carries the sentence that these lanes **check** floors and never **set** them, per `CONTRIBUTING.md:90-99`). Splitting per-platform would produce two epsilons for one decision — precisely the outcome §8 step 3 and Open Question 2 exist to prevent.

**What the slices hold that this task does not.** #665 (Windows file-handle probes), #666 (`GUI boot (Windows, WindowStation)` promotion), #671 (advisory JDK-26 macOS leg), #672 (`lsof` observation or documented skip for the `/proc`-gated probes), #673 (`GUI boot (macOS, WindowServer)` promotion). §13 of this task lists the GUI rigs as explicitly out of scope, so those five are genuinely outside it.

**#667 already recorded the intended reading from its side:** *"The umbrella outcome 'a macOS- or Windows-only failure blocks the merge' is #406 … this is the macOS slice underneath it, not a second copy."*

**The resolution, stated so a later pass can act on it without re-deriving.** Either (a) this task executes as the umbrella and #661–#664 / #667–#670 close into it as covered, keeping #665, #666, #671, #672, #673 open; or (b) the eight slices execute and this task narrows to `PlatformLaneRatchetTest`, the coverage-spread table, P7 and P8. **(a) is the cheaper reading** — the epsilon, the ratchet test and the 20-run record are one decision each, not two — but it is a maintainer call, not a dedup call, because both tiers are `tier:task` and the lower-number rule does not adjudicate scope. **Whoever starts first must comment on the other set before touching `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.**

**Blocking edge unchanged and still real:** #374 (TASK-0015). O10 shows zero `timeout-minutes` across six workflow files; a required job with no timeout converts a hung macOS or Windows runner — the two platforms with network-dependent toolchain installs — into a six-hour block on every pull request. That must land before any of these checks blocks, on either path.

**Scope ownership at the boundary, unchanged by this pass:** #374 owns timeouts. #378 owns the lane split, the gate budget and the fixture policy. #162 owns the Linux display substrate's fail-closed xvfb. #91 owns retiring `rerunFailingTestsCount` (O8) — this task's Open Question 1 decides only whether the retries stay for one release while the promotion accrues, and must notify #91 either way. #265 Stage 2 owns the cross-platform failure taxonomy this task consumes.

**Disposition: no merge, no closure on this pass. Recorded for the maintainer decision above.**

5227239623.body:
## ABSORBED — create-audit of #600-#868, 2026-08-08

The create stage filed a TASK-C111-\* / TASK-C265-\* decomposition whose per-platform slices reproduce outcomes **this task already owns**. Each of those slices declared its boundary against this issue on the belief that "#406 … was flagged as near-verbatim with #265 by the dedup pass" and would therefore dissolve. It did not: #406 is open, is `tier:task`, is the lower number, and §12 of its body states its ownership explicitly — *"This task owns exactly the two jobs' error policy, their suite arming, and the promotion record."* Six of those slices are therefore second copies of scope that lives here.

Closed as duplicate of this issue: **#661, #663, #664, #667, #669, #670**. Everything below is carried forward from their bodies — after closure this comment is the only record of it, and each item **supersedes nothing in this issue's body; it adds to §5, §8 and §14**.

### Carried forward from #661 (TASK-C111-1 — Windows promotion)
Duplicated: P1/P5/P6/P7 and the §8 promotion steps. New material to honour:

1. **Name the defect classes the promotion is buying against.** The Windows-only regressions this lane exists to catch are concrete, and the promotion PR should say so: a CRLF-sensitive save path, a leaked file handle that locks a circuit file, and a golden rewritten by `autocrlf`. A promotion described only as "the lane blocks now" does not tell a later reader what it protects.
2. **Precedent for the 20-run record format:** #188's `installer-reproducibility-aarch64` promotion, alongside the `ci.yml:328-346` `gui-wayland` block already cited as O5. Two worked examples, not one.
3. **#111 invariant 4 is binding on the burn-in:** any failure encountered is fixed at source or carries a *narrow, documented skip citing the specific test* — never a broad platform mute. This is stricter than "do not pre-mute" in §8 and should replace it.
4. **#111 invariant 2 is binding on the promotion:** the Linux `build` job remains the sole gating authority for SpotBugs. This promotion moves the JaCoCo ratchet (§5 P2) but must not move SpotBugs authority.

### Carried forward from #663 (TASK-C111-3 — Windows display suite)
This issue's O1 already classifies Windows display arming as Background (`ci.yml:244` passes `-Djls.test.headless=false`), so the only work is that the suite must be *green inside the promoted required check*, which is P5/P6. New material:

5. **Anti-vacuity is an assertion, not a PR note.** §9 currently records the executed display-test count as a manual PR observation. Strengthen it: **a run that executed zero display-tagged tests must fail rather than pass**, on both promoted lanes. A green lane that ran nothing is the exact failure this task exists to remove, and it must be machine-detected, not eyeballed. (Note O7's corpus correction: 25 classes, one of them outside `test/jls/ui/`.)
6. Windows-only display failures are fixed **in the test or the product**; residuals carry a per-test documented assumption naming the platform reason (item 3's rule, applied to the display half).

### Carried forward from #667 (TASK-C265-1 — macOS promotion + taxonomy)
Duplicated: P1/P5/P6 for the `macos` job. New material:

7. **The failure taxonomy is a written artifact, and this task should stop treating it as someone else's output it merely consumes.** §12 defers it to "#265 Stage 2"; #265 is a feature and produces no artifact by itself. Land a taxonomy note in `docs/` or as a `ci.yml` job comment classifying the burn-in failures actually observed against these named classes: line-ending, path-separator, file-locking/`@TempDir`, case-sensitivity, `HeadlessException`/AWT, `/proc`-gated, toolchain, TCC-permission. The `VK_DELETE` glyph divergence in `HotkeysHelpAccuracyTest` is the worked model — it was fixed at source.
8. **No failure is silenced with a broad `assumeTrue(!isMac)`** — same rule as item 3, stated for macOS.
9. **Add a post-promotion demonstration:** a PR carrying a deliberate macOS-only divergence of a demonstrated class is shown turning the required check red. This is the macOS analogue of P7's two deliberate branches and is not currently in §5.

### Carried forward from #669 (TASK-C265-3 — macOS display arming)
Duplicated: P3 verbatim. New material: item 5's zero-executed-run assertion applies here too, and the 20-run record (P6) must **cover the armed suite** — a record accrued before the display suite was armed is not evidence about the armed lane. Make that explicit in §8's ordering: arm first, then accrue.

### Carried forward from #664 and #670 (Windows / macOS JaCoCo floors)
Duplicated: P2 verbatim on both jobs, and Open Question 2 already puts "per-package epsilons" and "per-platform floors" on the table. New material:

10. **Calibration has a precondition.** Both slices ordered the floor *after* the HDL goldens execute and the display suite is green, on the ground that the floor must be calibrated from a converged suite. That ordering is correct and is missing from §8, which currently measures the spread in step 3 before arming. **Re-order §8: arm the toolchains and the macOS display suite first, then measure the three-platform spread, then decide the epsilon.** A spread measured against a suite that is still self-skipping is not the spread the floor will face.
11. **Cite the observed numbers in the change**, not just the decision — the package × platform table §9 already requires, pinned beside the value it justifies.
12. **The Windows and macOS floor decisions must be reconciled**: one model, or two with a stated reason. Open Question 2 should be answered once for both lanes, not twice.
13. P8 stands unchanged and is reinforced: Linux floors are never lowered to accommodate a platform lane. A platform-specific gap is named and either closed or floored separately.

### Boundary — what the C-series retains
The remaining slices of that decomposition are **not** duplicates of this task and stay open; they are new substrates or new lanes this issue never claimed:

- **#665** (TASK-C111-5) — the `/proc`-gated file-handle probes observed on Windows, or a written statement of why they cannot be.
- **#672** (TASK-C265-6) — the same probes via `lsof` on macOS, or a documented skip naming both test files.
- **#671** (TASK-C265-5) — a macOS advisory JDK-26 leg. This issue's P7 covers only the *Windows* JDK-26 leg; macOS is single-leg today and gaining a second leg is new work.
- **#666** (TASK-C111-6) — `GUI boot (Windows, WindowStation)` as a required check.
- **#673** (TASK-C265-7) — `GUI boot (macOS, WindowServer)` as a required check, with TCC denial classified as environment and never as a JLS failure.

#666 and #673 are **new rigs**, and are not covered by #411 (TASK-0018) either: #411's "both rigs" are `GUI boot (Linux, Wayland/JBR)` and `GUI boot (Linux, X11/Xvfb)` (its O2/O6), both Linux. Ordering: #666 and #673 depend on this task's promotion of their platform's build lane, not the reverse.

### Ordering restated on both endpoints
This task now precedes #665, #666, #671, #672 and #673 — a platform's GUI-boot rig and probe work is only meaningful once that platform's build lane blocks. Recorded on #111 and #265 as well.

5181631292.body:
**STAGE 3 (CLOSE) — coordination point recorded, not a duplicate.** Cluster A (core model, save format, file identity, importers & logic analysis).

#409 was checked against #404 and against the shared importer report work, and duplicates neither. Recording the boundary and one coordination point that the stage-2 sweep did not surface.

**#409 vs #404 — different defect classes on the same path.** Both produce a named diagnostic where something is silently lost today, and both act at load, which is the surface similarity:

- **#404 (TASK-0003, under FEAT-002 / #314)** — an attribute *name* no element declares. The defect is a gap in the **attribute vocabulary**: the value vanishes at load with nothing said.
- **#409 (TASK-0031, under FEAT-012 / #356)** — a file that parses but is **structurally corrupt**. Per #356 §1 the two classes that fail silently today are net bit-width disagreement and duplicate element names, both enforced only on the editor's connect gesture (`SimpleEditor.canConnect`, four identical copies) and never on the load path.

Distinct outcomes, distinct parents, distinct falsification. Not a merge candidate in either direction.

**Coordination point: three diagnostic vocabularies are being defined concurrently over adjacent surfaces.** None of these is a duplicate of another — they cover different domains — but they will be read together by anyone consuming JLS diagnostics, and nothing currently obliges them to agree on shape:

1. **This issue (#409)** — typed findings from a post-load semantic pass, each carrying a category, the stable ids involved and a one-line remedy. #356 §3 anchors the shape: *"shaped like the existing `src/jls/LoadError.java` taxonomy"*, consumed by the load path, a batch flag with its own exit status, and the merge driver.
2. **#404** — the named load diagnostic for an undeclared attribute, on the same `finishLoad` path.
3. **#608 (TASK-C556-1, under FEAT-C29-1 / #556)** — the one loss-report schema (construct, disposition, location, explanation) that every importer adopts, with #610 asserting dropped-set-equals-reported-set in shared infrastructure.

The recommendation is not to merge or to unify prematurely, but to make the relationship explicit before the second of these lands: **#409's `LoadError`-shaped taxonomy is the load-path dialect and #608's schema is the importer dialect**, and #404's diagnostic should adopt #409's taxonomy rather than mint a third, since it fires on the same path against the same `Circuit`. Whichever of #404 and #409 lands first establishes that taxonomy; the second extends it.

A caution carried over from the #323/#451-vs-#556 finding, which is the same shape of problem one layer out: #323 §3 states its totality as an **equality**, not a containment, and whichever assertion arrives second must inherit the equality. The equivalent trap here is a load-path diagnostic surface that reports a *subset* of what it drops. #356 §4 invariant 1 is the guard — no new invariant is armed until it has run over the entire tracked fixture corpus and the output of every importer and emitter.

Also recorded, from #356's roster: #409's sibling **#436 (TASK-0005)** is shared between FEAT-012 (#356) and FEAT-003 (#334), and #409 sits behind it on a three-link critical path that has no parallelism — TASK-0005 → TASK-0031 → TASK-0032, all three edges necessity rather than convention.

No issue was closed and no body or title was modified by this pass.

## BOUNDARY + ORDERING (mirror): this anchor is what six other issues divide by, and a second issue is now re-homing a fixture out of `riscv/` too

Sim-engine adversarial review, 2026-08-08. Mirror half of a boundary posted on #554/#728; adds the consumer list this task's urgency rests on.

### 1. The boundary with #728

**#728 (TASK-C554-2)** — "the benchmark fixtures are tracked in-tree outside `riscv/`, including at least two circuits below CPU scale" — is a second issue moving a fixture out of `riscv/`. **Not a merge.** The split:

- **This issue owns the CPU-scale calibration anchor** — the artifact the engine programme's measured constants are taken on.
- **#728 owns the sub-CPU-scale fixtures** — a counter and a memory loop, which do not exist anywhere today.

**Edge: #413 → #728.** #728 consumes the re-homed anchor rather than re-homing one itself. Two artifacts each claiming to be *the* tracked CPU-scale fixture is how a published number and a CI band end up measuring different circuits without anyone noticing. #512 (CAP-28) already declares `ordering_after: #413`; the task tier never inherited it.

**One question to answer at execution rather than assume:** do this task's "tracked, censused fixture" and #728's CPU-scale entry name the *same file*? If yes, that overlap is duplication and this issue wins on number. If this task's anchor is a calibration artifact distinct from the suite's flagship workload, both stand and the boundary above is the whole answer. **Resolve it by naming the file each produces, not by merging.**

### 2. What the anchor actually is, on master, today

`docs/capability-roadmap/keystone-c-performance.md` § 2 and § 12 name it precisely, which makes this task's target concrete rather than descriptive:

- **`riscv/build/k2000.jls`** plus `k2000_clk.txt` — 6004 clocked cycles, 120 KB circuit, 193 KB `-t` vector, time limit `12008000`. Siblings `k500`/`k1000` at 1504/3004 cycles.
- **Generated**, not committed, by `riscv/bench_kernel.py 2000` — which § 12 describes as *"a scratch harness, not part of the verification suite, and can be deleted"*.
- **Census**: `elements(all, recursive)=1551 wireNets=297 maxBits=32 subcircuits=0`; 225 logic elements + 297 nets = the 522 nodes every ns/node figure divides by.
- **Oracle intact**: `riscv/verify.py` passes 11/11 on the same jar.

**So the anchor is doubly at risk, not singly.** D5 deletes `riscv/`; but even before that, the anchor is a *build product of a script that describes itself as disposable*. Re-homing the `.jls` alone is not enough — whatever this task tracks must either commit the artifact or commit the generator with a determinism check, because a regenerated k2000 that differs by one element invalidates every constant taken on it.

### 3. The consumers, so the cost of getting this wrong is legible

Everything below divides by a measurement taken on this anchor: **#442** (the ns/event and bytes/event bands, and the events-per-clock-cycle equality asserted against `fired 2,331,793` on 6004 cycles), **#476** (the 47.7%-of-318 ns queue+dedup share), **#393** (the 82.3%-carry-no-time premise and its queue-traffic before/after), **#879** (the k2000 loop-time gate at 0.742 s / 318 ns/event), **#362** (the whole stack factor), **#512** (the first published public number, whose AC-3 is precisely "the published number's fixture is tracked in-tree, not `riscv/`").

**A related gap this task should know about but does not own:** the *instruments* that produced those numbers — `jls.sim.KernelProbe`, `KernelProbe2`, `Census`, `NoDedup` — are also uncommitted (`git grep` finds none at `origin/master`). Re-homing the fixture without them leaves a tracked circuit nobody can take a number on. **#726 owns the instrument**; this issue owns the fixture. Recorded on #554 and #512 so the two land in a usable order.

5227346843.body:
## ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (slice: collab-arch) — O6 is refuted by measurement, two cited issues are closed, and this task has an unnamed real prerequisite

This comment supersedes **O6**, the `related` line, the §13 out-of-scope pointer, and the two Definition-of-Done items that rest on O6. O1–O5 and O7–O9, H1–H4, P1–P9 and §7 are sound and are **not** disturbed — this is a strong issue and the measured O1 failure is exactly the kind of evidence the tracker should carry more of.

### 1. O6 is false. `ElementVocabulary` is not stale, and the file it points at proves the opposite.

O6 claims the allowlist *"has already gone stale"* and warns that *"a merger that reads the stale list will reject `RegisterFile` and `FieldExtend`."* §7.11 and §11 repeat it, and a DoD item is built on it.

Measured on master at `29afb26`:

```
$ python3 - <<'EOF'   # ALLOWED  vs  ElementRegistry.ALL
ALLOWED size: 34
registry rows: 35   distinct tags: 35
in registry not in ALLOWED: ['TestGen']
in ALLOWED not in registry: []
EOF
```

**`RegisterFile` and `FieldExtend` are both present in `ALLOWED`** — they sit on consecutive literal lines in [`ElementVocabulary.java`](https://github.com/anadon/JLS/blob/29afb26/src/jls/collab/op/ElementVocabulary.java) (`"Register", "RegisterFile", "ShiftRegister", …` and `"Extend", "FieldExtend",`). A merger reading this list rejects neither. The prediction in O6 is wrong, and acting on it would produce a change that adds two entries that are already there.

**The single real difference is `TestGen`, and it is a deliberate, test-pinned denial — not staleness.** `TestGen` is a batch-only element that JLS never saves (`ElementRegistry.java:33`: *"`TestGen` is included even though JLS never saves one"*; `Palette.java:25` calls it *"the batch-only `TestGen`"*). Its exclusion from the network vocabulary is asserted on purpose in [`ElementVocabularyTest`](https://github.com/anadon/JLS/blob/29afb26/test/jls/collab/op/ElementVocabularyTest.java):

```java
assertFalse(ElementVocabulary.isAllowed("TestGen"));
assertThrows(..., () -> ElementVocabulary.requireAllowed("TestGen"));
```

So the allowlist is exactly *registry minus deny*, with `deny = {TestGen}` — precisely the invariant `A ⊆ K \ deny` that #212 now carries. **O6′:** *`ElementVocabulary` is consistent with `ElementRegistry` up to one deliberate, test-pinned denial (`TestGen`). The javadoc's "stopgap … until the element registry exists" sentence is stale **prose**, but the list is not stale **data**. A merger may read it as authoritative for network-facing input.* The two DoD items resting on O6 (*"a merger that reads the stale list will reject RegisterFile and FieldExtend — check before shipping"*, and reporting a mismatch to #372) reduce to: confirm `TestGen`'s exclusion is intended for the merge path too, and report nothing else.

That last point is a genuine open question this task should answer rather than inherit: **should a three-way merge of two `.jls` files accept a `TestGen` element?** A merged file is not network input, and `TestGen` is a legal thing to hand-write into a save file per `ElementRegistry.java:35`. If the merger reuses `ElementVocabulary` as its type gate it will refuse a file JLS's own loader accepts — which is P9's failure mode arriving through the front door. Recommended default: the merger gates on `ElementRegistry`, not on `ElementVocabulary`; the two gates have different threat models and conflating them is how the network allowlist quietly becomes a file-format rule.

### 2. Two cited issues were closed in the dedup pass

- **#352 (FEAT-052) is closed** (merged into **#170**). This body leans on it heavily: *"The AUTO column **is** the CRDT's merge policy (FEAT-052, #352)"*, the mermaid node `F352`, `related: [352, …]`, §12's *"Notify #352 on landing"*, and a DoD item *"#352 (FEAT-052) notified as the AUTO column's consumer"*. Corrected: the dedup survivor is **#170**, but the *functional* consumer of the AUTO column is **#171** and specifically its task **#279** (see §3). Notify **#279 and #171** on landing; #170 owns the hostile-input half only.
- **#348 is closed** (merged into **#169**). §13 places *"the online transport and replica loop (TASK-0109 under #348/#352)"* out of scope; corrected to **#169/#170**, with the replica loop itself sitting under **#171**'s roster (#279 merge rules, #280 anti-entropy).

Corrected `related: [356, 334, 319, 171, 279, 170, 169, 167, 163, 166, 165, 78]`.

### 3. The unnamed prerequisite: **#279 must land before P8 can be run at all**

`blocked_by: []` lists two unfiled prerequisites (TASK-0005, TASK-0031) and misses a third that **is** filed. H3/P8 is this task's headline claim:

> `merge3(base, apply(base,A), apply(base,B))` canonical-saves byte-identically to the state two replicas reach after exchanging *A* and *B* through `CausalBuffer`.

There is no "state two replicas reach" to compare against. At `29afb26` the crdt package is four files — `VectorClock`, `OpId`, `OpEnvelope`, `CausalBuffer` — and O7 correctly says it is *a delivery discipline, not merge semantics*. **The replica merge API that P8 compares against is #279's §7.4 deliverable**, and the multi-replica exchange harness is #279's §6. Until #279 lands, P8 cannot be written, let alone run — and P8 is the entire justification given in this issue's Abstract for building offline first (*"what makes it the executable specification and test oracle of the online CRDT"*).

Corrected: `blocked_by` gains **#279**, alongside the two unfiled tasks. This is a measured fact, not a preference — the same standard #399 applied to its own #403 edge. Mirrored on #279 as `blocks: [415]`.

### 4. Boundary with #279 — one rule table, and the direction of derivation is now inverted

This is the cross-generation collision worth naming explicitly, because both issues are open and both author per-kind merge semantics:

| | **#279** (task under #171, collab Stage 2) | **#415** (this issue, under #356) |
|---|---|---|
| Form | op-based, online, in-memory | state-based, offline, three-way over files |
| Rules | add-wins element set keyed by `ElementId`; delete-wins over concurrent attribute edits; per-attribute LWW (Lamport + peer id); OR-set wires | STRICT column per `(record kind, situation)`, AUTO derived by one tiebreak |
| Home | `jls.collab.crdt` | `jls.merge` |
| Consumer | #171, #163's convergence gate | #356, the git merge driver |

They are **not duplicates** — different form, different home, different failure mode, and #415's git-driver and conflict-reporting scope has no counterpart in #279. Do not merge them.

But they are also not independent: **H2 asserts the AUTO column and the CRDT's policy are the same table plus a tiebreak.** If both execute without coordination, JLS ships two per-kind merge tables that must agree by convention — the exact *"second, incompatible answer to the same question"* this issue's own Abstract exists to prevent.

**Boundary, recorded on both endpoints:** the per-kind merge rule table has **exactly one representation**. Given the ordering in §3 (#279 lands first, of necessity), the derivation direction stated in this body is inverted in practice:

- **#279 owns the merge semantics** — the per-kind rules and their confluence proof — because it is unblocked, funded under a capstone-required feature, and is what P8 measures against.
- **This task owns** the STRICT column (the *conflict-reporting* mode, which #279 has no notion of), the situation classifier, `ThreeWayMerge`, the git driver, the `-merge` flag, `docs/merge-rules.md` as the published normative document, and the P8 cross-check itself.
- **H2 is re-read as a claim to be tested, not a construction order:** rather than deriving AUTO from STRICT here, this task derives **STRICT from #279's shipped rules by removing the tiebreak**, and H2 is falsified if any row's shipped online outcome is not "the STRICT outcome, or a tiebreak applied to it". That is a stronger test than the original phrasing, because it is checked against code that exists rather than against a table this task wrote itself.

H4 is unaffected — offline-partial-with-conflicts remains the right offline posture, and it remains this task's distinctive contribution.

### 5. Evidence commit — re-verified on master, and it holds

Pinned at `2d0ca9d`, which #493 records as living only on a branch scheduled for deletion. Re-derived at `29afb26` for this slice: **O4 holds** (`CircuitOp` still `sealed … permits` exactly eleven records, same list, same order); **O8 holds** (`src/jls/merge` does not exist; `docs/merge-rules.md` does not exist); **O5's `String`-switch trap holds** — the reader still dispatches on a `String`, so the §7.11 guard remains necessary. Only O6 failed re-derivation, and it failed at `2d0ca9d` too: the quoted `ALLOWED` literal in #399's own transcript of the same commit already contained `RegisterFile` and `FieldExtend`. This was a reading error, not commit drift. Re-pin to `29afb26` at pickup.

5181394555.body:
## Boundary with #647 (and #645): "a second board" versus "the Basys-3 verdict" — NOT duplicates

Recorded during the feature/task deduplication pass over the HDL-export / external-toolchain / board / PCB / silicon cluster.

This task promises *"a second board exists with both halves, and the first board's bitstream path has actually been walked on hardware and written down."* The newly-filed **#647** (TASK-C599-2) promises *"the Basys-3 verdict lands as code or as a recipe — a `Boards` entry with a byte-pinned golden, or the documented path a Basys-3 owner follows instead, with the open-toolchain goldens proven unmoved."*

If the Basys-3 were chosen as this task's second board, the two would collide. **They are not duplicates, and they should not be allowed to become one by accident.**

**The distinction:**

- **This task's second board is an open-toolchain board.** Its parent #359 (FEAT-023) exists so that the open toolchains become *required behavioural witnesses* — a board whose bitstream path CI can actually exercise. Its other half, the first board's path walked on real hardware with the record filled in, is about ending certification-by-skipping.
- **#647's Basys-3 is explicitly a go/no-go with two admissible outcomes**, one of which is *not* a board. #599 (FEAT-C38-3) frames it as *"supported with its toolchain named, or refused with the cost arithmetic"*, and **#645** requires that verdict to be written and searchable either way. The Basys-3 is the board the ASEE courses actually own, and it is a Xilinx part — so "supported" carries a vendor-toolchain cost that this task's open-toolchain framing does not.

**Both stay open with their scope intact. No issue is closed and no scope moves.**

### The coordination this leaves behind

Two things a scheduler must not get wrong:

1. **Do not let the Basys-3 silently become this task's "second board."** If the #647 verdict comes back *supported*, its `Boards` entry and this task's second board are the same slot and one of the two issues must record a supersession — a decision, not an inference. If the verdict comes back *refused with arithmetic*, this task still needs a second board and must pick a different one.
2. **#647's own guard is the shared one.** Its requirement that *"the open-toolchain goldens are proven unmoved"* is a constraint on whatever this task lands: adding a second board must not perturb the first board's byte-pinned artifacts. Recorded here so the guard is visible from both sides.

Adjacent, also recorded: #632 (TASK-C597-1) reads the board picker from `Boards.all()` specifically so that **adding a board needs no GUI change**. That property is worth honouring when this task adds its second board — if a new `Boards` entry requires a GUI edit, #632's contract is broken from this side.

Body is self-contained; reader does not need the comment to understand the design. No external reference to this comment in body or completion criteria; the ruling is explained inline.
5227652285.body:
## CORRECTION — drop the `WireNet` half; the domain is a port property only

Maintainer ruling 2026-08-08, recorded in full on [#344](https://github.com/anadon/JLS/issues/344#issuecomment-5227650512):

> Simple wires should only be value carriers. The ports/sockets/plugs they connect to carry domain information for either output or input but not both input and output.

This **supersedes** both this issue's original design and my amendment above wherever they put an alphabet on the net.

### What this issue must now build

- **`Put` gains `lo()`/`hi()`** (reserved by #878). ✔ unchanged.
- **`WireNet` gains nothing.** ✘ **Withdrawn** — the §7.4 line adding "the same pair on `WireNet`, beside `WireNet.bits`" is struck. A net carries values and width; it does not carry an alphabet.
- **`makeNet`/`recheck` do not compute, store or fold a net domain.** They validate that the attached ports agree and refuse naming **both ports and both domains**. The rejection is a statement about the ports.
- **The four `SimpleEditor` sites** become a direct port-pair domain check, still unconditional and still immediately above the guarded width check.
- **`initSimulation`** refuses when a net's attached ports disagree — same check, one last time, where reaching it means JLS built an illegal net.
- **`getBits()`'s loud shim is unaffected**: it keys off the *port's* domain (`lo() != 0 || hi() != 1`), which is exactly where it already sat.

### This deletes your own worst hazard

**O3 — the two widening policies (`makeNet` last-wins, `recheck` `Math.max`) — no longer applies to the domain at all.** §7.10's `radix(n)` validation formula, §7.5's single private radix-agreement predicate on `WireNet`, and Open Question 1 ("how do `makeNet` and `recheck` unify?") were all machinery for a net field that will not exist. **If the net holds no domain, there is nothing to widen and no policy to unify.** The never-widen requirement stops being a rule the code must obey and becomes a fact about the data model.

Width keeps its existing behaviour untouched — O3, O4 and H2 still govern *width*, and `bits == 0` remains the unattached sentinel. Only the domain moves.

### Unchanged and still binding

P7 — every existing golden byte-identical, no tolerance clause. P8 — the K9 palette ratchet. O4 — no zero/unknown sentinel for the domain; every port is born `[0,1]`. O9 — no implicit coercion at any boundary; the only sanctioned crossing is an explicit declared mapping (#889) through a bridge element (#453). The element-level binary-only guarantee from my amendment above is unaffected: it was always about which *values* reach a gate, and that is a port-domain question.

5227044532.body:
## WITHDRAWN: this issue is NOT a duplicate of #63 and is not being closed

A dedup pass on 2026-08-08 posted an *"Absorbing #420"* comment on **#63** declaring this task a duplicate of that feature and slating it for closure in the verification stage. **The verification stage has now run and refuted the merge.** This issue stays open, keeps its scope, and keeps its `tier:task` label. The withdrawal is recorded on #63 as well.

This also **reinstates** the earlier 2026-08-04 boundary comment on #63, which had already examined this pair and correctly declined the merge.

### The refutation comes from this issue's own body

The merge rested on the claim that this task *"folds T1 (Yosys `write_json` fallback) in as the routing rule for scanner-rejected file classes rather than leaving it outside,"* and therefore delivers all of #63. Three passages here say otherwise:

- **§13** — *"Out of scope: … growing the scanner (route unhandled file classes to Yosys `write_json` instead, #63 §9)."*
- **§7.11** — the fallback appears as a *failure-mode route*: *"That fallback is an **integration, not a parser**. Do not grow the scanner."*
- **§10** — it is **contingent** scope: *"**H1 refuted** if the scanner fails on a file class the element must support. Then route it to the Yosys `write_json` extraction path … and **record the scope change here**."*

**§8 Method has no step that builds a `write_json` port extractor.** Naming a route to an extractor is not building one. #63's T1 is *production* fallback extraction and its §6 records T1, T2 and T3 as *"mutually independent and safe for concurrent agents"* — an independently schedulable slice this task does not claim.

Additionally, #63 §5 P3 (latency: 3–5 components interactive, reactions well under 10 ms, exchange caching bounding delta-cycle cost) has no counterpart among this issue's P1–P12 — the deadline in P7 is a crash threshold, not a latency measurement — and #63 §5 P2's re-run at close is a feature-tier obligation.

**Your §14 line is consistent with all of this once read in full:** *"#63 closed against **its §7 and its addendum's P4–P6**"* is a scoped claim against two named sections, not against the whole feature. Keep it as written; it is accurate.

### Standing relationship

`#63 = #420 + T1 + (P3 latency) + (P2 re-run)`. This task is a slice of #63 — the intended feature→task hierarchy — covering its planned T2 (element, dialog, persistence, geometry, all five canvas failure states), T3 (harness generator, subprocess transport, lifecycle and reaping, bounded stderr tail) and T4's parity leg.

### Parent re-home, reaffirmed

The machine block reads `part_of_feature: 360`. **#360 (FEAT-024, RESIDUAL) was absorbed into #63 in an earlier dedup pass**, so that field names an issue that is no longer an open owner. **Read this task as a child of #63**, which is the surviving owner of the black-box HDL component capability. The §14 DoD line *"Landing reported on #360 (FEAT-024) with a `STATUS:` comment"* should be discharged **on #63** instead. No body has been edited — this comment is the record.

### Unchanged and still blocking

Both execution-blocking open decisions stand and are unaffected by any of the above:

1. **Confirm the #216 distinction** — that a batch, forward-only conversation is a different thing from the live co-simulation #216 rejected. The maintainer is asked to confirm rather than inherit the claim, and `docs/hdl-cosimulation.md` should not be written before it is settled.
2. **Default palette or progressive disclosure** — Decision D9 (`BRIEF.md` §12) restates K9 as progressive disclosure, while `PaletteContractTest` currently forces exactly one row per registered type outside three tags. This blocks the palette row and may require the view dimension FEAT-050/TASK-0105 introduce.

5181366837.body:
## Cross-cluster note: adjacency with #341 (FEAT-027) — NOT a duplicate

Recorded during the feature/task deduplication pass over the HDL-export / external-toolchain / board / PCB / silicon cluster. This task sits in that cluster as a child of **#365** (FEAT-041), but its outcome brushes **#341** (FEAT-027, the drive-strength / net-kind / multi-driver-resolution feature), which was clustered elsewhere.

**They are not duplicates, and the line between them is sharp:**

- **This task is a static buildability check.** It answers, before anything is simulated, "does this net drive more load than its weakest driver can carry?" — reporting **both numbers** — and "is this input floating?", and it refuses to print `PASS` for a family whose DC check is vacuous. Its inputs are the declared per-family loading figures from the part library (#349).
- **#341 is runtime resolution semantics.** It answers what value a net actually settles to when several drivers of different kinds contend, via #391 (order-independent fold) and #387 (strongest-driver-wins, open-drain floating to Z).

A static fan-out arithmetic check and a simulation-time resolution rule can disagree without either being wrong, and neither can be derived from the other. No merge.

**But the two must be kept in view together**, for one concrete reason: **#349's §4 invariant 3 ships the electrical columns inert** — *"no pass may interpret them until the strength model exists. Transcribed loading figures consumed before the simulator can support them produce confident wrong answers — a fan-out check reporting numbers the simulator contradicts. This is an invariant, not a recommendation."* #349 also pins this with integration criterion IC-7, an architecture test that fails the moment a **non-test** reader of the loading figures appears.

This task is precisely that reader. So the sequencing question a later pass must answer is not "are these duplicates" but **"may #430 land before #341, and if so under what statement of what its numbers mean?"** Options, recorded without deciding: gate this task behind #341; or land it with its verdicts explicitly scoped as a *static datasheet-arithmetic* claim that makes no prediction about simulated values, with IC-7 relaxed by a named, tested exception rather than by deletion. The second is the cheaper path and is consistent with #430's own refusal to print `PASS` where the check is vacuous — but it is a maintainer call, not a dedup finding.

No issue is closed and no scope moves.

5181397912.body:
## Second boundary: two checks under one `jls -check` — adjacency with #607 (#486)

Follow-up to the cross-cluster note above, from the same deduplication pass. Both are recorded on this issue because it is the lower number in each pair.

**#607 (TASK-C486-3)** — *"`jls -check` says whether a net is still a wire — `l_crit = v*t_r/k` per opted-in net, and 'not assessable' everywhere else, including every shipped example"* — under **#486 (FEAT-058)**. It lands a second static electrical verdict in the same command surface as this task's DC check.

**Not duplicates.** Different physics, different inputs, different opt-in models:

- **This task** answers a **DC** question from part-library loading figures: does a net drive more load than its weakest driver can carry (reporting both numbers), and is an input floating. Its data source is #349's per-family loading columns.
- **#607** answers a **transmission-line validity** question from a declared net length (#605) and a declared driver transition time (#603): is the lumped model the design is simulated under still valid for this net. Its data source is authored-per-net, not per-family.

Neither verdict can be derived from the other and neither subsumes the other. **No merge; both stay open with their scope intact.**

### The shared constraint worth writing down

Both are **opt-in-shaped checks that must never report a confident wrong answer on a design that did not opt in**, and they express it the same way:

- This task: *"a family whose DC check is vacuous never reads `PASS`."*
- #607: *"not assessable" everywhere else, **including every shipped example**.*

That is one discipline appearing twice. If `jls -check` grows two different ways of saying "I cannot judge this", students get two vocabularies for the same idea and a green summary line will eventually paper over a vacuous check. Whoever lands the second of these two should reuse the first's not-assessable reporting shape rather than inventing one — and the summary must not collapse *assessed and passed* into the same output as *not assessed*.

Recorded as a coordination note, not a scope change.

5227088748.body:
## Orphaned parent, and a resolved prerequisite (stage 3 CLOSE, cluster E)

**Not a duplicate of anything.** This comment records two facts that changed under this issue during the feature-to-task deduplication pass, plus one boundary that must not be mistaken for a duplicate later. Nothing here is a merge and nothing is closed.

### 1. `part_of_feature: 348` now points at a closed issue — this task has no live parent feature

Both features this issue names are gone:

- **#348 (FEAT-051 RESIDUAL)** — the declared `part_of_feature` — is **closed as a duplicate**. It was a later re-derivation of **#169** (*"Shared session v1: membership lifecycle, snapshot sync, floor control, presence, peer panel"*), and #169 is where its substance now lives.
- **#352 (FEAT-052)**, named in `related` and §12 as the other consumer, is likewise **closed as a duplicate**; its substance is split across **#170** (the element-type allowlist clause) and **#171** (concurrent-edit convergence and per-user undo).

So this task is presently **an orphan**: its owner field resolves to a closed duplicate, and no open feature claims it. That is recorded rather than fixed here, because re-homing is a judgement call about which of two live parents should carry it:

- **#171** — *"Simultaneous editing: op-based CRDT replication, anti-entropy, compaction, collaborative undo"* — is the better fit on substance. §12 of this issue already says every convergence, anti-entropy, compaction and per-user-undo claim in the CRDT work is measured by this harness, and #171 is the issue that makes those claims.
- **#169** is the inheritor of #348 by paperwork, but this task's outcome is not #169's: #169 carries a snapshot, this task applies ops on receipt over a replica loop. Filing it under #169 would put apparatus for Stage 2 convergence under a Stage 1b feature.

**Recommended: re-home to #171.** Flagged for the maintainer rather than done, since a task has one `part_of_feature` field and changing it is a body edit this pass does not make.

### 2. The unfiled prerequisite has a number now — and it is a feature, not a task

The machine block records a second `blocked_by` in prose: *"TASK-0108 (session foundation: identity, transport, membership and sync, owned by FEAT-051) is the second prerequisite and is not yet filed."* It **was** filed, as **#433**, and #433 has since been **closed as a duplicate of #169** — its outcome was the whole of #169's remaining decomposition rather than a slice of it.

**The prerequisite therefore resolves to #169 itself**, and the reason is unchanged and still real: without the session foundation there is no envelope framing, no peer identity to stamp a `VectorClock` with, and nothing to attribute a rejected frame to. 5227266741.body:
## Adversarial review, core-format slice — mirror of the #436 ordering edge, and a scope change on #436 that lands on this task

Posting the far half of an edge that #436 (TASK-0005) declares but could not name, plus one
consequence of a correction made there today. Nothing here changes this task's own outcome.

### 1. The edge, now with both endpoints

#436 was filed before this issue existed and says so in three places — the note under its machine
block, its § Related Work, and its closing mermaid node all read *"TASK-0006 … filed concurrently and
its number does not exist yet"*. The number is **#437**. The declared edge, quoted from #436:

> this task **blocks TASK-0006** (plain text as the default container, the sibling task of FEAT-003 —
> the container flip is only safe after the reference form lands, per FEAT-003's Design notes)

and again in its § Related Work:

> **TASK-0006** … this task must land first: flipping the container before the reference form exposes
> the amplification to git without fixing it.

**This is a real prerequisite, not a preference,** and it survives review: flipping the default
container to plain text is what makes the save text reach `git diff` at all. Doing that while a
single-element insert still produces a Θ(N) diff hands users a worse artifact than the compressed
container did — a 10,744-line fixture (#436 O5, `test/fixtures/riscv-sum1to10.jls`) whose every edit
looks like a rewrite. Recording it here so the edge has two ends:

```yaml
blocked_by: [436]   # TASK-0005 — the stable-id reference form; flipping the container
                    #   before it lands exposes the amplification instead of fixing it
```

If this body already carries that edge, treat this as confirmation and nothing more.

### 2. The consequence of today's scope correction on #436 — read before scheduling

A correctness defect was found and corrected on #436: **its §8 Method, as written, cannot satisfy its
own P1/P2 ratchet.** O4's fixtures are wire-free `AndGate` blocks, so they emit no `ref` items at all;
#436's change (the single reference-emitting site, `src/jls/elem/WireEnd.java:606`/`:611`) would leave
δ(200)=206 and δ(800)=806 exactly as measured. All of that amplification is the ` int id N` base
attribute, which `Circuit.save` reassigns by canonical rank on every write — verified on master
`07a0bea`.

The correction resolves #436's Open Question 2 and brings the dense `id` line into #436's scope: an
`sref`-form block stops emitting the position-dependent `id` line. **Two things follow for this task:**

1. **The precondition this task waits on is now "constant δ, demonstrated on a wired,
   interleaved-replica fixture" — not merely "`sref` has landed".** If #436 lands the reference form
   without the `id` change, its ratchet is either red or measured on the wrong fixture, and the
   premise for flipping the container is not yet true. That is the condition to check at pickup, and
   it is checkable: run #436's `DiffStabilityRatchetTest` and confirm the δ(800)/δ(200) ratio, not the
   magnitude.
2. **The container decision interacts with the `id` change on autosave.** #436 §7.7 notes that
   `.jls~` autosave checkpoints go through the same writer and *"[t]heir container policy is
   TASK-0006's, not this task's"*. With `id` absent from `sref`-form blocks, an autosave written in
   the new form is only readable by a loader carrying the `sref` arm — which is fine within one
   build, and is worth stating explicitly in whatever this task decides about the autosave and undo
   containers, rather than being inherited silently.

### 3. Evidence re-pin

Per #493, `2d0ca9d` citations are unreliable. The facts this task's premise rests on hold on master
`07a0bea`: `Circuit.save` wraps its writer in `canonicalNewlines` so line endings are platform-
independent (#111, #166), writes `FORMAT ` + `formatVersionNeeded()` for top-level saves only, sorts
elements by `Element::getStableId`, and `Circuit.stateHash()` is the SHA-256 of that canonical save
text. **Line numbers have moved; re-derive by content.**

5181467724.body:
## Boundary with #735 (TASK-C557-1) — same bands, different lanes (feature/task deduplication pass, cluster C)

**Not a duplicate.** Recorded because both tasks turn a performance band red and the vocabulary is shared, which reads as duplication at title depth.

**The two tasks.**

- **#442 (this task, TASK-0026, under #335)** — the **required-gate** ratchet, in four assertions of deliberately different kinds: events/cycle as a hard **equality**, ns/event and bytes/event as **ceiling-only bands that ratchet down and never up**, and one **byte-identity** gate over the entire existing golden corpus. It asserts against the **committed calibration fixtures** (#413) and its thresholds are exactly the constants #335 measures — which is why #335 §2 records that filing it under the CI feature was rejected: it would be a gate with no basis.
- **#735 (TASK-C557-1, under #557)** — a **scheduled** lane that re-runs the **published** workloads of the C28 benchmark suite (#726, fixtures #728) under this task's ceiling bands, so a number in `docs/performance.md` cannot silently go stale. Its sibling #738 makes a red lane name *which published number is now a lie*, so the outcome is an engine fix or a reviewed re-publication.

**The relationship is consumption, not duplication.** #557's title and #735's outcome both name *"TASK-0026's ceiling bands"* — this task. #735 does not derive bands; it applies them to a different workload set in a different lane. Distinguishing them precisely:

| | #442 | #735 |
|---|---|---|
| lane | the **required** gate (#335 §4.1: nothing here may lengthen it) | a **scheduled** lane (#317 / #378's long-run lane) |
| inputs | the committed calibration fixtures (#413) | the published benchmark workloads (#726, #728) |
| assertions | equality + two ceiling bands + golden byte-identity | the ceiling bands only |
| what red means | a simulation regression, in a pull request | a **published claim** is now false |
| audience | maintainer, engine funding, capstone budgets | readers of `docs/performance.md` and the README line (#732, #733) |

Absorbing either into the other would put an hours-scale published-workload re-run inside the required gate — violating #335 §4.1 — or drop the event-count equality and the golden byte-identity gate, which #557 never claimed.

**What must stay single, recorded so it does not fork.** The band **definition** and the ratchet-down-never-up rule are this task's, and #735 must consume them rather than restate them. If #735 needs a band this task does not define, extend this task; two band vocabularies over the same metric is how a ceiling quietly becomes a target.

**Open question that governs both, unresolved here.** #335 Open Question 4: what band width is honest for ns/event and bytes/event? Too tight and the lane flakes on a noisy runner; too loose and the gate is decorative. Recommended default: set the band from the observed spread across the three platform legs, and **record the spread beside the band**. That answer blocks this task and should be reused by #735 rather than re-derived. Note the interaction with #406's cross-platform coverage-spread measurement — both are "measure the three-platform spread before setting a threshold" and should share the measurement run if they land together.

**Prerequisite that governs both.** #335's one `blocked_by` is **#353 (FEAT-005)**: a band measured through the quadratic stimulus parse measures the parse, not the engine.

**Evidence of absence at `2d0ca9d`, carried forward:** `git grep -rln "events per cycle\|eventsPerCycle" 2d0ca9d -- test/` returns nothing (exit 1). Neither assertion exists yet, so neither task is superseded.

**Disposition: no merge, no closure. Both tasks stay open with the ownership above.**

5227405971.body:
## LINK PASS (mirror) + EVIDENCE RE-HOMING: this task is a declared prerequisite of three engine changes and none of them said so

Sim-engine adversarial review, 2026-08-08. Mirror half of corrections posted on #476, #393, #879 and #362.

### 1. Ordering edges, written on both endpoints

#362 § 6 states the edge in prose — *"TASK-0026 before the three code changes is **necessity under K3**: the byte-identity gate is what decides whether each change may land. Landing a speedup and then building the gate that would have rejected it inverts the entire safety argument."* — and #362's LINK PASS of 2026-08-02 covered the **feature** tier only. The task tier was never linked, so none of the three consumers carried the edge in a machine block. Corrected:

```yaml
blocked_by:
  - 379   # TASK-0023 — necessity: the bands need measured denominators
blocks:
  - 476   # TASK-0063 — calendar queue / dedup replacement
  - 393   # TASK-0064 — zero-delay closure
  - 879   # TASK-C232-2 — the value-plumbing migration (see §3)
```

Each consumer's own text asks for this gate in the weaker, optional form — "if #442 has landed, extend its gate instead of adding a second one". **That phrasing lets a change land with no gate at all if this task has not.** Under K3 that is exactly backwards, and the edge above is the correction.

### 2. The denominators: the documents this work divides by are not on master, and most of them have a master home

`git ls-tree -r origin/master` returns **zero paths under `docs/plan/`**, `docs/machine-calibration.md` does not exist, and the commits `2d0ca9d` and `3a81a4a` are **not present in the repository at all**. Re-homing map for anything this task's bands cite:

| cited as | on master at |
|---|---|
| `BRIEF.md` § 13 — 318 ns/event | `docs/capability-roadmap/keystone-c-performance.md` § 2 / § 8.1, as **0.742 s `runEventLoop` for 2,331,793 fired events on `riscv/build/k2000.jls` → 318 ns/event, 8,090 cycles/s** |
| `BRIEF.md` § 13 — queue+dedup 47.7%, values 37.6% | keystone-c § 3 / § 11 |
| `BRIEF.md` § 2 — allocation churn | keystone-c § 3, top frames, `SimEvent$PinChanged` 1.92 M/run |
| **events-per-clock-cycle baselines** | keystone-c § 2 event census: `fired 2,331,793 posted 2,596,496 dup-suppressed 264,702 max queue depth 12,093` on 6004 cycles — **this is the equality assertion's baseline integer, measured** |
| `docs/machine-calibration.md:516` — the behavioral ev/instr constant, "MODELED, never measured" | **no master home found.** This is #379's premise and it is now uncited; see § 4 |

**The bands' denominators are therefore recoverable; one of them is not.**

### 3. The value leg's identity changed

#362's `planned_tasks` names the value leg "TASK-0056". **#475 was closed 2026-08-08 as a duplicate of #232**, and #232 had no filed children. It now has two: **#878** (the type, touching only `jls.core`) and **#879** (the plumbing migration, the 61 clone deletions, and the byte-identity claim). #879 is the consumer of this gate, not #475.

### 4. `riscv/` is where the fixture lives and D5 deletes it

Every baseline above is measured on `riscv/build/k2000.jls`, generated by `riscv/bench_kernel.py 2000`. **#413 (TASK-0025) owns re-homing that anchor before `riscv/` is deleted.** A band asserted against a fixture that stops existing turns into an unrunnable lane, not a red one — which is the failure mode that is hardest to notice. If this task's bands are written against the k2000 anchor, **#413 is a real prerequisite of the gate going into CI**, even though it is not a prerequisite of the gate being written. Recorded as an edge to adjudicate rather than asserted, because it depends on whether the committed calibration fixtures this task names are the same artifacts #413 re-homes — if they are, this is a duplicate boundary and not merely an ordering one. #512 (CAP-28) already declares the same `ordering_after: #413` for the same reason.

### 5. A criterion worth sharpening

The event-count **equality** is the strongest assertion in this programme and the one most likely to be quietly relaxed the first time it goes red. Two things make it survivable: (a) the baseline integer is now measured and citable (§ 2), so a moved count is a diff against a number rather than against a memory; and (b) #476's own T3 and #879's H3 each describe a *legitimate* mechanism by which the count could move — width-sensitive equality narrowing dedup, and `PinChanged`-keyed flag design widening it. **When it goes red, the required output is the diagnosis, not a new baseline.** Neither consumer states that; this gate should.

5181362491.body:
## Boundary: #451 vs #608 / #610 — the `.circ` report and the shared loss-report schema

Stage 2 (MIGRATE) of the feature-to-task pass checked this task against the newly filed C29 importer-suite tasks. Two of them touch the same artifact this task produces, and the split is recorded here so neither side re-implements the other.

| Issue | Owns |
|---|---|
| **#451** (this issue) | the `.circ` reader and **the `.circ` migration report as a concrete artifact** — the construct model, the per-attack-vector parse hardening, the written construct map, and the report naming every construct that did not survive with its location and reason |
| **#608** (TASK-C556-1) | **one loss-report schema** — construct, disposition, location, explanation — as a written document any importer can adopt, format-agnostic |
| **#610** (TASK-C556-2) | the dropped-set-equals-reported-set equality **asserted once in shared infrastructure**, and the `.circ` report round-tripping through that shared schema losslessly |

**Not duplicates.** This task owns the first instance; #608/#610 (under **#556**, FEAT-C29-1) generalise it so `.dig` (#558), `.cv` (#559), Falstad (#561) and the Digital test-vector path (#562) tell their losses in the same voice. #633 (TASK-C561-3) states the direction explicitly — *"the report dialect is #556's, unchanged"*.

**Two coordination points an executor of either side needs.**

1. **The totality equality.** This task's parent #323 states it as an equality, not a containment: `C_src(f) \ C_out(f) = R(f)` — a construct dropped but unreported is silent loss, and a construct reported but actually realised trains instructors to ignore the report. #610 moves that assertion into shared infrastructure. Whichever lands second must **inherit the equality**, not weaken it to containment; if the shared assertion arrives as containment, that is a contract deviation on #323 §3 and needs a `REPLAN:` before either closes.
2. **Sequencing is not fixed by an ordering edge.** If #451 lands first, the `.circ` report is the reference dialect #608 transcribes and #610 must prove round-trips losslessly. If #608 lands first, this task emits into the shared schema directly and #610's round-trip is trivial. Either order is sound; what is not sound is two report formats in the tree at once. The `.circ` report is the only one today, so it is the anchor.

Also adjacent and also not a duplicate: **#612** (TASK-C558-1) parses `.dig` as untrusted XML and inherits the same hardening discipline this task establishes (external entities disabled, doctype disallowed, entity resolvers neutralised, one test per vector) — a shared discipline over a different format, not a shared deliverable. **#450** (TASK-0055) is this task's sibling under #323 and its stated prerequisite: the part data must exist before an importer can bind to it.

**Disposition.** #451, #608, #610, #612 and #450 all stay open in their existing tiers. Nothing superseded, nothing closed. A matching boundary note is recorded on #323.
